output:

params:
  # ---- Phase 1 outputs (must already exist on disk) -----------------------
  # The ONLY upstream files this notebook reads are produced by

  #
  # Required artifacts (all under output/ from Phase1BuildMNL + cache/):

  #   output/trips_calibrated.rds   ← per-trip calibrated frame

  #   cache/dodgr_motorcar_<hash>.rds
  #   cache/skim_walk_<hash>.rds, skim_bike_<hash>.rds, skim_transit_<hash>.rds

  mnl_rds:          "outputs/phase1/mnl_fit.rds"
  choice_long_rds:  "outputs/phase1/choice_long.rds"
  trips_cal_rds:    "outputs/phase1/trips_calibrated.rds"
  raw_trips_csv:    "./data/public/psrc_hts/hts_trips.csv"
  cache_dir:        "./cache"
  output_dir:       "./outputs/phase2"

  # ---- Routing & geography ------------------------------------------------
  pbf_path:         "./data/public/osm/washington-260122.osm.pbf"
  base_monday:      "2026-04-13"
  kcm_gtfs_dir:            "./data/gtfs/kcm"             # existing-network feed + its variants (GTFSTriplication.Rmd)
  designed_gtfs_dir:       "./outputs/gtfs"              # Grid, Grid + Local and Node-based feeds
  other_agencies_gtfs_dir: "./data/gtfs/other_agencies"  # added unchanged to every scenario

  # ---- Bus-lane / capacity -------------------------------------------------
  seattle_lanes_geojson:        "outputs/streets/street_grid.geojson"
  # Residual capacity (vph) on bus-lane-affected edges where NEW_lanes <= 0
  # (general-traffic lane fully removed → "local access only" by SDOT
  # convention). Bumped from 50 → 200 because real residential streets
  # carry ~100-200 vph through-traffic from the immediate neighborhood
  # even when no longer signed as through-streets. The 50 vph value
  # produced unrealistic gridlock cascades when combined with inelastic
  # cordon-gateway flow.
  bus_lane_residual_local_vph:  200
  seattle_counts_csv:           "data/public/sdot/traffic_flow_counts.csv"
  gateways_geojson:             "data/own/gateway_points.geojson"

  # ---- Observed-flow seed pipeline ----------------------------------------
  # SND/COMPKEY → OSM way_id directional mapping. Each row gives the OSM
  # way that an SDOT segment (COMPKEY) and SND street segment (SND_ID)
  # corresponds to. Lets us do attribute-join SDOT counts → dodgr edges
  # via way_id rather than a spatial buffer that misclassifies side streets.
  snd_compkey_csv:              "data/own/sdot_snd_osm_crosswalk.csv"
  # Per-corridor manual repair of the SND ↔ OSM way_id mapping, produced by
  # StreetSetup.Rmd. Optional; if missing the raw mapping above is used as-is.
  # One row per (COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR); WAY_IDS is a comma-separated
  # list (the mapping is intentionally many-to-many on each direction).
  way_id_repair_csv:            "outputs/streets/way_id_repair.csv"
  # SDOT 2022 Traffic Flow Counts corridor layer — line features where each
  # corridor is one inter-intersection arterial stretch with its measured
  # AWDT/AMPK/PMPK and the comma-separated list of constituent COMPKEYs.
  # Downloaded from ArcGIS on first use and cached on disk.
  sdot_corridor_url:
    "https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/2022_Arterial_Traffic_Volumes/FeatureServer/3/query?outFields=*&where=1%3D1&f=json"
  sdot_corridor_cache_rds:      "cache/sdot_2022_flow_corridors.rds"
  # WSDOT AADT counts cover state highways (I-5, SR-520, SR-99, I-90 etc.)
  # which SDOT's own data doesn't include. Used to fill freeway segments
  # the SDOT corridor layer doesn't reach.
  wsdot_counts_csv:             "data/public/wsdot/traffic_counts.csv"
  # AADT → peak-hour conversion factor. 0.09 is the standard urban K-factor
  # (Federal Highway Administration / Highway Capacity Manual).
  default_k_factor:             0.09
  # Bbox to clip the count layers to Seattle proper before matching.
  count_bbox_lon: !r c(-122.45, -122.15)
  count_bbox_lat: !r c(47.45, 47.78)
  # Mapping of WSDOT state route number → SND street name list, used to
  # match WSDOT counts to dodgr edges via the SND name (no spatial join).
  wsdot_route_snd_pairs: !r tibble::tribble(
      ~state_route,    ~snd_name,
      "005",           "I5 NB",
      "005",           "I5 SB",
      "005EXP",        "I5 EXPRESS",
      "520",           "SR520 EB",
      "520",           "SR520 WB",
      "099",           "AURORA BR",
      "099",           "AURORA AVE N",
      "099",           "SR99 NB",
      "099",           "SR99 SB",
      "099COTUNNEL",   "SR99 TUNNEL NB",
      "099COTUNNEL",   "SR99 TUNNEL SB",
      "090",           "I90 WB",
      "090",           "I90 EB"
    )

  # ---- Daysim demand (full population OD with cordon gateways) -----------
  # Phase 2 evaluates network alternatives on the Daysim synthetic population
  # rather than the HTS sample. HTS still drives per-trip MNL; Daysim drives
  # OD-level trip volumes for road loading and population mode-share metrics.
  daysim_trips_tsv:    "data/public/soundcast/_trip.tsv"
  daysim_parcel_map:   "data/public/soundcast/parcel_2023_geography.csv"
  daysim_tract_col:    "Census2020Tract"
  daysim_city_col:     "CityName"
  # DEPTM format (used for the per-TOD filters below):
  #   hhmm                   : 700 = 7:00 AM (max <= 2359)
  #   minutes_after_midnight : 420 = 7:00 AM
  #   minutes_after_3am      : 240 = 7:00 AM
  deptm_format:        "minutes_after_midnight"

  # ---- Time-of-day buckets --------------------------------------------
  # Pick which TODs to actually run equilibria for (sub-list of the 5).
  # `AM` only = ~5 hr; `AM, PM` = ~10 hr; all five = ~18 hr sequential.
  # Aggregation in §15 fills in unmodeled TODs using the literature
  # ratios below (tod_share_*, tod_vmt_share, tod_seed_factor).
  #
  # NOTE: rmarkdown's params YAML treats nested maps as parameter sub-
  # fields (value:, label:, etc.), so the named lists below use `!r`
  # expression syntax (same trick `wsdot_route_snd_pairs` uses above).
  # To change values, edit the R expression below in-place.
  tods_to_run: !r c("AM", "Midday", "PM","Evening","Night")
  # TOD bounds in hours-of-day (closed start, open end). Night wraps
  # midnight: [23, 24) ∪ [0, 7). AM peak is [7, 10) so the 09:00 hour
  # (still peak-congested) is represented by AM rather than orphaned;
  # the five bins now tile the full 24 hours with no gap.
  tod_bounds: !r list(
      AM      = c(7,  10),
      Midday  = c(10, 16),
      PM      = c(16, 19),
      Evening = c(19, 23),
      Night   = c(23, 7))
  # Hours of the day in each bin (AM 7-10 = 3 hr; Night 23-24 + 0-7 = 8 hr;
  # sums to 24).
  tod_hours_per_day: !r list(
      AM = 3, Midday = 6, PM = 3, Evening = 4, Night = 8)
  # Per-TOD observed-flow seed multiplier (applied to AMPK from SDOT).
  # PM uses 1.10 (PMPK > AMPK in most arterials); off-peak smaller.
  tod_seed_factor: !r list(
      AM = 1.00, Midday = 0.60, PM = 1.10, Evening = 0.55, Night = 0.15)
  # TOD-share of annual fatalities. Empirical, computed from the SDOT
  # Collisions dataset (all years 2004-2026; n = 427 binned fatal victims,
  # victim-weighted by FATALITIES) bucketed on the tod_bounds above with
  # 09:00 folded into AM. Source/recompute: ThesisTables.Rmd
  # (crash time-of-day shares). Used in Vision Zero
  # to distribute the 29.4 annual baseline across TODs. Fatalities are
  # evening/night-heavy (higher speeds, impairment, low visibility).
  tod_share_fatal: !r list(
      AM = 0.089, Midday = 0.218, PM = 0.187, Evening = 0.220, Night = 0.286)
  # TOD-share of annual serious injuries. Empirical, same SDOT Collisions
  # source (n = 2,507 binned serious-injury victims, weighted by
  # SERIOUSINJURIES). More midday/PM-weighted than fatalities (tracks
  # crash volume / exposure rather than severity).
  tod_share_si: !r list(
      AM = 0.098, Midday = 0.268, PM = 0.223, Evening = 0.198, Night = 0.213)
  # TOD-share of daily VMT (used to fill in unmodeled-TOD VMT in §15
  # daily aggregation). Roughly: AM peak ~13%, midday ~32%, PM ~20%, etc.
  tod_vmt_share: !r list(
      AM = 0.13, Midday = 0.32, PM = 0.20, Evening = 0.21, Night = 0.14)

  # ---- BPR + reliability --------------------------------------------------
  bpr_alpha:                0.15
  bpr_beta:                 4.0
  # bpr_vc_cap = 2.0 caps per-edge BPR factor at 1 + 0.15·2⁴ = 3.4×, which
  # bounds path-aggregate BPR factors in the realistic 1.5-2.5× range
  # typically observed for Seattle AM peak. The previous 3.0
  # produced 13.15× max factors on saturated edges and median path BPR
  # of 4.8×, which over-stated congestion by ~3× vs empirical data.
  bpr_vc_cap:               2.0
  reliability_vc_threshold: 0.85
  # Reliability penalty multiplier on the squared (V/C - threshold)^2 term.
  # Disabled (set to 0) because lambda = 1.0 produces a 5.6x time multiplier
  # at V/C = 3.0 ON TOP of BPR's 13.15x → combined 74x → catastrophic
  # cascade when stacked against inelastic cordon-gateway demand. Pure
  # BPR (lambda = 0) caps at 13.15x and gives results in the realistic
  # 12-18 mph priority-network range. A lambda of 1.0 is
  # "on the high end" of FHWA reliability research.
  reliability_lambda:       0.0

  # ---- Equilibrium loop ---------------------------------------------------
  max_iter:        50   # bumped from 30 — headroom for the now-rerouting (flow-MSA) equilibrium
  rel_tol:         0.01
  msa_start_step:  2
  am_peak_hours:   2
  auto_occupancy:  1.10
  # Residential traffic calming: cap residential/living_street free-flow speed at
  # this many mph (NA = off; current signed limit is 25). Lower = slower network
  # (Vision-Zero lever) + more through-traffic pushed off local streets back to
  # arterials. Enters the cache hash only when set, so uncalmed caches stay valid.
  residential_calm_mph: 15
  # Residential capacity cap (vph): match the 150 living-street floor to push
  # through-traffic off local streets. NA = off; enters the cache hash only when
  # set, so uncapped caches stay valid.
  residential_cap_vph: 150

  # ---- AV-induced demand --------------------------------------------------
  av_drive_tt_shrink: 0.41   # 1 - 0.59 from spec literature review

  # ---- External downloads -------------------------------------------------
  rse_index_url:    "https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/Race_and_Social_Equity_Composite_Index_Current/FeatureServer/0/query?outFields=*&where=1%3D1&outSR=4326&f=geojson"
  lodes_wac_url:    "https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/wa/wac/wa_wac_S000_JT00_2022.csv.gz"

  # ---- Vision Zero --------------------------------------------------------
  vz_baseline_fatalities: 29.4
  vz_baseline_si:         222.8
  vz_hughes_elasticity:   1.0
  vz_nilsson_exp_fatal:   3.0
  vz_nilsson_exp_si:      2.0

  # ---- Walkshed -----------------------------------------------------------
  walkshed_radius_m: 402.336   # ¼ mile

  # ---- Hardware -----------------------------------------------------------
  n_threads:        0          # 0 = all cores - 1
  java_heap_gb:     80

  # ---- Skip / force flags -------------------------------------------------
  force_rebuild:        false
  # Sensitivity-analysis hook (used by run_pipeline.R --quick and SensitivityAnalysis.Rmd). A
  # character vector of config_id values to restrict §14 to, applied ON TOP of
  # the active filter. Empty (default) =
  # run all selected configs, i.e. NO change to normal behaviour. The OFAT
  # sensitivity harness sets this to {baseline__no_pri_no_av, grid_local__pri_av}
  # so each perturbed-constant render only runs those two equilibria. Always
  # keep baseline__no_pri_no_av in the set so the in-notebook Vision Zero
  # denominator and the §13b unseeded-baseline reference still resolve.
  configs_filter: !r character(0)
---

# Overview

Phase 2 evaluates **14 configurations** = 5 transit networks × 4 street networks
(only certain cells filled per the spec). For each configuration we run a
mode-choice ↔ road-equilibrium fixed-point loop until link travel times
converge, then extract a comparable set of metrics for the thesis.

```
                                 STREET NETWORKS
                  Current  | AV-induced | Full-priority | Priority+AV
TRANSIT NETWORK   ----------------------------------------------
Baseline             ✅          ✅              ✅              ✅
3x (Triplicate)      ✅          ✅              ✅              ✅
Grid                 —           —              ✅              ✅
Grid+Local           —           —              ✅              ✅
Node-based           —           —              ✅              ✅   (WIP)
```

**Demand source.** OD-level trip volumes for the equilibrium come from the
**Daysim synthetic population** (full PSRC trip table, AM-peak filtered),
*not* the HTS sample. Trips with one or both ends outside Seattle are
collapsed to one of five cordon **gateway** points where major roads cross
the city boundary. The HTS sample is still used for per-trip MNL
prediction (where we have per-trip variables); HTS-MNL probabilities are
aggregated to per-OD shares and then weighted by Daysim trip totals.

**Per-iteration loop:**

1. Predict per-trip MNL probabilities on the HTS choice frame using the
   current drive-tt skim and pre-baked transit skim.
2. Aggregate HTS probs to per-OD shares.
3. Combine HTS-MNL shares with Daysim OD totals; ODs without HTS
   coverage (cordon-touching and interior-fallback) use **Daysim's own
   per-OD mode shares** (computed from the MODE column of the trip table
   in §6c). Earlier versions used a fixed 0.95 cordon and an HTS-MNL
   global mean for interior fallback — both replaced by direct empirical
   Daysim values once it became clear the data already says what those
   shares are.
4. Aggregate Daysim drive-vehicle volumes to road links via
   `dodgr_flows_aggregate`.
5. Apply BPR + reliability to compute new link times.
6. MSA-blend with previous iteration's times.
7. Recompute drive skims; check convergence.

Transit times are **pre-baked** per configuration (the `_av` GTFS variants
already include AV-induced bus slowdowns, the `_tsp` variants assume
full priority). Dynamic per-iteration transit re-skimming is left as a TODO.

**Mode-share metric** is Daysim-weighted: the average of per-OD mode
shares across the entire Daysim AM-peak universe, weighted by Daysim
trip totals per OD. This is the population-level statistic; the HTS
trip-weighted variant is *not* reported here.

**Outputs** (in `output/phase2/`):

- `config_table.csv` — definition of all 14 configurations
- `mode_share_by_config.csv` — overall mode shares
- `transit_tt_stats_by_config.csv` — mean / median / sd of transit total time
- `vmt_speed_by_config.csv` — VMT, network-average speed, vehicle-hours
- `walkshed_by_config.csv` — % of Seattle area within ¼ mile of any stop
- `employment_accessibility_by_tract.csv` — long: tract × config (jobs reachable in 30 min by transit)
- `vision_zero_by_config.csv` — projected fatalities / serious injuries via Hughes × Nilsson
- `rse_correlation_by_config.csv` — equity correlation (per-config)
- `equilibrium_history_by_config.csv` — iteration-level convergence trace
- `summary_for_thesis.csv` — single tidy table mirroring the Results section
- `arcgis_layers/network_full.gpkg` — single GeoPackage with all
  street metadata + per-TOD baseline values + per-config daily aggregated
  flow/speed + daily deltas vs baseline. Drops into ArcGIS Pro and QGIS
  with proper schema. One layer (`edges`), one row per dodgr edge, all
  scenario columns flat (no joins needed for symbology). See §16 docs
  for the full column list and the thesis-figure → column mapping.

## 1c. Paths and constants

```{r setup-paths}
CACHE_DIR  <- normalizePath(params$cache_dir,  mustWork = FALSE)

  unlink(PBF_PATH)
  if (!isTRUE(file.link(.pbf_src, PBF_PATH))) file.copy(.pbf_src, PBF_PATH)
}
```

## 1d. Helpers

```{r setup-helpers}
# ---- Logging (lifted from Phase1BuildMNL) --------------------------
.log_start_time <- Sys.time()

# Progress is mirrored to `run_progress.log` in the project dir so a HEADLESS
# render can be monitored live (knitr captures cat() into the doc, so plain
# stdout is sparse). Watch it from PowerShell with:
#   Get-Content run_progress.log -Wait -Tail 40
.RUN_LOG <- file.path(getwd(), "logs", paste0("run_progress", Sys.getenv("RUN_LOG_TAG", ""), ".log"))
try(cat("", file = .RUN_LOG), silent = TRUE)   # truncate at the start of each run
.tee <- function(txt) {
  cat(txt)
  try(cat(txt, file = .RUN_LOG, append = TRUE), silent = TRUE)
}
log_stage <- function(stage) {
  sep <- paste(rep("=", 76), collapse = "")
  .tee(sprintf("\n%s\n[%s] %s\n%s\n", sep,
               format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), stage, sep))
}
log_msg <- function(...) {
  .tee(sprintf("[%s] %s\n", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"),
               paste0(..., collapse = "")))
}
log_done <- function(label, t0) {
  dt <- difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")
  .tee(sprintf("[%s] DONE %s (%.1f sec)\n",
               format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), label, as.numeric(dt)))
}
log_sub <- function(...) {
  .tee(sprintf("           %s\n", paste0(..., collapse = "")))
}
fmt_dur <- function(secs) {
  if (!is.finite(secs)) return("?")
  if (secs < 60) return(sprintf("%.0fs", secs))
  if (secs < 3600) return(sprintf("%.1fm", secs / 60))
  sprintf("%.1fh", secs / 3600)
}

# ---- Cache (lifted from Phase1BuildMNL) ----------------------------
with_cache <- function(label, inputs, builder, subdir = "") {
  base_dir <- if (nzchar(subdir)) file.path(CACHE_DIR, subdir) else CACHE_DIR
  dir.create(base_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  hash <- digest::digest(list(label = label, inputs = inputs), algo = "sha1")
  payload  <- file.path(base_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.rds",  label, hash))
  manifest <- file.path(base_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.json", label, hash))
  if (!params$force_rebuild &&
      file.exists(payload) && file.exists(manifest)) {
    log_msg(sprintf("Cache HIT  for %s [%s]", label, substr(hash, 1, 8)))
    return(readRDS(payload))
  }
  log_msg(sprintf("Cache MISS for %s [%s] -- building", label, substr(hash, 1, 8)))
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  obj <- builder()
  saveRDS(obj, payload)
  jsonlite::write_json(
    list(label = label, hash = hash,
         built_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
         seconds  = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))),
    manifest, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
  log_done(sprintf("cached %s", label), t0)
  obj
}

file_signature <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(list(path = path, exists = FALSE))
  fi <- file.info(path)
  list(path = normalizePath(path, winslash = "/"),
       size = fi$size, mtime = format(fi$mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
}

# ---- Cache lookup: latest by mtime --------------------------------------
# Phase1BuildMNL's with_cache writes files named `<label>_<sha1>.rds`.
# The regex below matches *only* that pattern, so it cannot pick up artifacts
# with other names (e.g. a graph cache named
# `dodgr_graph_motorcar_psrc.rds` fails this match).
# Phase 2 reads only Phase 1 outputs.
latest_cache_rds <- function(label, dir = CACHE_DIR) {
  cands <- list.files(dir, pattern = sprintf("^%s_[0-9a-f]+\\.rds$", label),
                      full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(cands) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  cands[order(-as.numeric(file.info(cands)$mtime))][1]
}

# ---- Misc helpers --------------------------------------------------------
clean_geoid11 <- function(x) {
  x <- str_replace_all(as.character(x), "[^0-9]", "")
  substr(str_pad(x, 11, pad = "0"), 1, 11)
}

row_softmax <- function(M) {
  m  <- apply(M, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  m[!is.finite(m)] <- 0
  E  <- exp(sweep(M, 1, m))
  E[!is.finite(E)] <- 0
  rs <- rowSums(E)
  rs[rs == 0] <- 1
  E / rs
}
```


# 2. Load Phase 1 outputs

The Phase 1 pipeline (`Phase1BuildMNL.Rmd`) is the contract: this notebook
reads its outputs and never mutates them. We surface what's loaded here so
stale caches are caught immediately.

```{r load-phase1}
log_stage("Stage 2: Load Phase 1 outputs")

stopifnot(file.exists(params$mnl_rds), file.exists(params$choice_long_rds))

mnl <- readRDS(params$mnl_rds)
choice_long <- readRDS(params$choice_long_rds) |>
  mutate(trip_id = as.numeric(trip_id))

# Per-trip frame with everything Phase 2 needs: origin_id / dest_id / TOD /
# parking_money_usd / estimated_transit_fare / drive_tt_cal / availability.
#
# Two things Phase1BuildMNL does NOT pre-compute on trips_cal:
#   - is_work       built inside choice_wide as
#                     as.integer(str_detect(toupper(dest_purpose_cat), "WORK"))
#                   We re-derive it here from dest_purpose_cat (which IS on
#                   trips_cal).
#   - trip_weight   not used in the MNL fit (no `weights = ...`); we re-pull
#                   it from raw PSRC HTS via TREXPFAC joined on trip_id.
#                   Required for weighted mode-share aggregation downstream.

# Columns required to be physically present on trips_cal:
REQUIRED_TRIPS_COLS_RAW <- c(
  "trip_id", "origin_id", "dest_id", "dow_type", "tod_bin",
  "drive_dist_mi", "travelers_total",
  "parking_money_usd", "estimated_transit_fare",
  "vehicle_count_n", "dest_purpose_cat",
  "walk_avail", "bike_avail", "drive_avail", "transit_avail",
  "walk_tt_raw", "bike_tt_raw",
  "drive_tt_cal", "drive_tt_raw"
)

load_trips_cal <- function() {
  p <- params$trips_cal_rds
  if (!file.exists(p)) {
    stop("trips_cal not found at ", p,
         " — re-knit Phase1BuildMNL.Rmd to produce it.")
  }
  log_msg(sprintf("Loading trips_cal from %s", p))
  tc <- readRDS(p)
  missing <- setdiff(REQUIRED_TRIPS_COLS_RAW, names(tc))
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("\n", paste(rep("!", 76), collapse = ""), "\n",
         sprintf("%s is missing columns: %s\n",
                 p, paste(missing, collapse = ", ")),
         "These should be in the Phase1BuildMNL `trips_cal` object.\n",
         "Run `names(trips_cal)` interactively to confirm what's available.\n",
         paste(rep("!", 76), collapse = ""))
  }
  tc
}

trips_cal_full <- load_trips_cal()

# ---- trip_weight from raw HTS ------------------------------------------
# PSRC HTS uses TREXPFAC as the trip expansion factor. Phase1BuildMNL
# doesn't carry it onto trips_cal because it doesn't enter the MNL likelihood,
# but Phase 2 needs it for weighted mode-share / VMT aggregation.
load_trip_weights <- function(raw_csv, trip_ids) {
  if (!file.exists(raw_csv)) {
    log_msg(sprintf("WARNING: %s not found — falling back to trip_weight = 1",
                    raw_csv))
    return(tibble(trip_id = trip_ids, trip_weight = 1))
  }
  log_msg(sprintf("Reading TREXPFAC from raw HTS: %s", raw_csv))
  weights <- readr::read_csv(raw_csv, show_col_types = FALSE,
                             col_types = readr::cols(
                               trip_id = readr::col_double(),
                               .default = readr::col_guess())) |>
    select(trip_id, any_of(c("trexpfac", "TREXPFAC", "expfac",
                             "trip_weight"))) |>
    setNames(c("trip_id", "trip_weight")) |>
    mutate(trip_id = as.numeric(trip_id),
           trip_weight = coalesce(as.numeric(trip_weight), 1))
  log_msg(sprintf("  TREXPFAC loaded for %d trips (median weight = %.1f)",
                  nrow(weights), median(weights$trip_weight, na.rm = TRUE)))
  weights
}
trip_weights <- load_trip_weights(params$raw_trips_csv,
                                  trip_ids = unique(trips_cal_full$trip_id))

trips_aux <- trips_cal_full |>
  transmute(
    trip_id      = as.numeric(trip_id),
    origin_id    = clean_geoid11(origin_id),
    dest_id      = clean_geoid11(dest_id),
    dow_type     = as.character(dow_type),
    tod_bin      = as.character(tod_bin),
    drive_dist_mi = as.numeric(drive_dist_mi),
    travelers_total = pmax(coalesce(as.integer(travelers_total), 1L), 1L),
    parking_money_usd = coalesce(as.numeric(parking_money_usd), 0),
    estimated_transit_fare = coalesce(as.numeric(estimated_transit_fare),
                                      TRANSIT_FARE_FALLBACK),
    vehicle_count_n = coalesce(as.numeric(vehicle_count_n), 0),
    # is_work re-derived from dest_purpose_cat (matches choice_wide build
    # in Phase1BuildMNL §11).
    is_work = as.integer(stringr::str_detect(
      coalesce(toupper(as.character(dest_purpose_cat)), ""), "WORK")),
    walk_avail     = as.logical(walk_avail),
    bike_avail     = as.logical(bike_avail),
    drive_avail    = as.logical(drive_avail),
    transit_avail  = as.logical(transit_avail),
    walk_tt_raw    = as.numeric(walk_tt_raw),
    bike_tt_raw    = as.numeric(bike_tt_raw),
    # Carry through Phase 1's depart_hour/depart_date so transit_bin_universe
    # can replicate Phase 1's data-driven rep_hour (median observed hour per
    # (dow_type, tod_bin)) rather than the hardcoded AM→8 / Midday→12 etc.
    depart_hour    = as.integer(depart_hour),
    depart_date    = as.Date(depart_date),
    # Phase-1 baseline drive times. The MNL was estimated on drive_tt_cal,
    # so when scenarios change drive_tt_raw via dodgr we apply the same
    # per-trip ratio (cal/raw) to the new raw time. This is a first-order
    # approximation of the GAM calibration that avoids re-running mgcv per
    # iteration. The ratio is exact at baseline; smooth GAM behavior makes
    # it a tight approximation when the route distance is unchanged.
    drive_tt_cal_baseline = as.numeric(drive_tt_cal),
    drive_tt_raw_baseline = as.numeric(drive_tt_raw),
    drive_cal_ratio       = ifelse(
      is.finite(drive_tt_cal) & is.finite(drive_tt_raw) & drive_tt_raw > 0,
      drive_tt_cal / drive_tt_raw, 1)
  ) |>
  left_join(trip_weights, by = "trip_id") |>
  mutate(trip_weight = coalesce(trip_weight, 1)) |>
  semi_join(distinct(choice_long, trip_id), by = "trip_id")
  # NOTE: previously filtered on `is.finite(drive_cal_ratio)` — that was
  # Phase 1's cal_ratio, which is recomputed in §12 from the AM-GAM
  # against Phase 2's skim_drive_full. Filtering happens there now,
  # keying on Phase 2's drive_tt_raw_baseline being finite.

log_msg(sprintf("MNL: %d coefficients, log-likelihood = %.1f",
                length(coef(mnl)), as.numeric(stats::logLik(mnl))))
log_msg(sprintf("choice_long: %d rows, %d trips",
                nrow(choice_long), n_distinct(choice_long$trip_id)))
log_msg(sprintf("trips_aux: %d trips with skim+sociodem", nrow(trips_aux)))

# NOTE: Phase 2 no longer loads Phase 1's `skim_drive` cache. The drive
# skim for every OD (HTS + Daysim) is built fresh in §7 on Phase 2's
# own dodgr graph (which excludes `service` highways and uses the
# (1,n)+(n,1) K-NN snap). For HTS trips, `drive_tt_raw` and
# `drive_dist_mi` from Phase 1's trips_calibrated.rds are NOT used —
# they were routed on a different graph. Phase 2 routes everything
# fresh.

# skim_drive_full (built in §7) is Phase 2's per-OD drive skim covering
# the full HTS ∪ Daysim OD universe. No Phase 1 inheritance.

# ---- Dodgr graph: Phase 2 builds its own (no longer depends on Phase 1)
# Motorcar profile, no turn penalties, largest component, contracted,
# WITH `service` highways excluded (they add noise to routing and are
# rarely useful for through-traffic). Cache version "p2_no_service".
dodgr_graph <- with_cache(
  "dodgr_motorcar_p2",
  list(version = "p2_no_service_v3_oneway_normalize",
       pbf  = file_signature(PBF_PATH),
       # Bbox derived from a generous Seattle envelope plus suffix margin
       # so commuters in/out have at least one reachable PSRC-county
       # county anchor (so dodgr routing succeeds for cordon gateways).
       bbox = c(xmin = -122.55, ymin = 47.20, xmax = -121.95, ymax = 48.05)),
  function() {
    log_msg("Building Phase 2 dodgr graph from OSM PBF...")
    log_msg(sprintf("  PBF: %s", basename(PBF_PATH)))
    bb <- c(xmin = -122.55, ymin = 47.20, xmax = -121.95, ymax = 48.05)
    boundary_poly <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(
      xmin = bb[["xmin"]], ymin = bb[["ymin"]],
      xmax = bb[["xmax"]], ymax = bb[["ymax"]]), crs = CRS_LL))

    log_msg("  Reading driving network via osmextract::oe_read...")
    t1 <- Sys.time()
    drive_tags <- c("highway", "oneway", "maxspeed", "lanes",
                    "access", "motor_vehicle", "name", "ref",
                    "bridge", "tunnel")
    # `service` excluded from the SQL query — saves filter work later.
    streetnet_sf <- osmextract::oe_read(
      PBF_PATH, layer = "lines",
      extra_tags = drive_tags,
      boundary = boundary_poly,
      boundary_type = "spat",
      query = paste(
        "SELECT * FROM lines",
        "WHERE highway IN (",
        "'motorway','trunk','primary','secondary','tertiary',",
        "'unclassified','residential','living_street',",
        "'motorway_link','trunk_link','primary_link',",
        "'secondary_link','tertiary_link')"),
      quiet = TRUE)
    log_msg(sprintf("  oe_read: %d edges (%.0f sec)",
                    nrow(streetnet_sf),
                    as.numeric(Sys.time() - t1, units = "secs")))

    # ---- Inspect and repair the `oneway` column ----
    # dodgr::weight_streetnet only understands TRUE/FALSE or 'yes'/'no'.
    # Raw OSM has several other values:
    #   "-1"           one-way, direction reversed from stored geometry
    #   "reversible"   direction varies by time-of-day (rare)
    #   "alternating"  single-lane bidirectional (rare)
    #   ""             empty string (should be NA, treated as "no")
    #   NA             missing tag (default in OSM is "no")
    # We:
    #   (a) log the value distribution so we know what was found,
    #   (b) reverse geometry for "-1" ways so they can be marked as "yes",
    #   (c) coerce everything else to "yes" or "no" with OSM defaults.
    .ow_raw   <- streetnet_sf$oneway
    .ow_dist  <- table(.ow_raw, useNA = "always")
    .ow_names <- names(.ow_dist)
    .ow_cnts  <- as.numeric(.ow_dist)
    .ow_total <- sum(.ow_cnts)
    log_msg("  `oneway` value distribution (raw OSM):")
    for (i in seq_along(.ow_cnts)) {
      val <- .ow_names[i]
      v_show <- if (is.na(val)) "<NA>" else if (val == "") "<empty>" else val
      log_sub(sprintf("    %-15s : %7d edges (%.2f%%)",
                      v_show, .ow_cnts[i],
                      100 * .ow_cnts[i] / .ow_total))
    }

    .ow_norm <- toupper(trimws(as.character(.ow_raw)))
    .ow_norm[is.na(.ow_raw) | .ow_norm == ""] <- "NO"

    # (b) Coerce to dodgr-acceptable values. `-1` ways are tagged "no"
    # (bidirectional) — this is the conservative choice. The "correct"
    # treatment is to reverse the geometry and tag "yes", but sf::st_reverse
    # on individual LINESTRINGs occasionally produces routing oddities that
    # bloat per-OD travel times (observed on Seattle PBF). Since `-1` ways
    # are a tiny fraction (~0.03%), treating them as bidirectional has
    # negligible network-level impact compared to graph corruption risk.
    # `reversible`/`alternating` are also tagged "no" — direction varies
    # by time-of-day; bidirectional is the average behavior.
    streetnet_sf$oneway <- dplyr::case_when(
      .ow_norm %in% c("YES", "TRUE", "1")                     ~ "yes",
      .ow_norm %in% c("NO",  "FALSE", "0", "-1",
                      "REVERSIBLE", "ALTERNATING")            ~ "no",
      TRUE                                                    ~ "no")
    .ow_clean_dist  <- table(streetnet_sf$oneway, useNA = "always")
    .ow_clean_names <- names(.ow_clean_dist)
    .ow_clean_cnts  <- as.numeric(.ow_clean_dist)
    .ow_clean_total <- sum(.ow_clean_cnts)
    log_msg("  `oneway` after normalization (yes/no):")
    for (i in seq_along(.ow_clean_cnts)) {
      val <- .ow_clean_names[i]
      v_show <- if (is.na(val)) "<NA>" else val
      log_sub(sprintf("    %-5s : %7d edges (%.2f%%)",
                      v_show, .ow_clean_cnts[i],
                      100 * .ow_clean_cnts[i] / .ow_clean_total))
    }

    log_msg("  Weighting (motorcar profile, turn_penalty = FALSE)...")
    t2 <- Sys.time()
    g <- dodgr::weight_streetnet(streetnet_sf, wt_profile = "motorcar",
                                 turn_penalty = FALSE)
    log_msg(sprintf("  Raw graph: %d edges (%.0f sec)",
                    nrow(g),
                    as.numeric(Sys.time() - t2, units = "secs")))

    # Defensive: drop any 'service' that slipped through (shouldn't happen
    # given the SQL filter, but be explicit).
    n_before <- nrow(g)
    g <- g[as.character(g$highway) != "service", , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(g) < n_before)
      log_msg(sprintf("  Dropped %d service edges (post-weight)",
                      n_before - nrow(g)))

    # Largest connected component
    n_before <- nrow(g)
    g <- g[g$component == 1, , drop = FALSE]
    log_msg(sprintf("  Largest component: %d / %d edges retained",
                    nrow(g), n_before))

    log_msg("  Contracting graph (degree-2 chain collapse)...")
    t3 <- Sys.time()
    g_c <- dodgr::dodgr_contract_graph(g)
    log_msg(sprintf("  Contracted: %d edges (%.0f sec)",
                    nrow(g_c),
                    as.numeric(Sys.time() - t3, units = "secs")))
    g_c
  })
log_msg(sprintf("Phase-2 dodgr graph: %d edges, %d vertices",
                nrow(dodgr_graph),
                nrow(dodgr::dodgr_vertices(dodgr_graph))))

# ---- Tract polygons + centroids -----------------------------------------
# Phase 1's `tract_centroids` cache is an sf object with column GEOID +
# geometry (built by compute_pop_weighted_tract_points). Convert to a
# flat (id, lon, lat) tibble to match what r5r / FNN expect downstream.
tracts_path <- latest_cache_rds("tracts_sf")
points_path <- latest_cache_rds("tract_centroids")
stopifnot(!is.na(tracts_path), !is.na(points_path))
tracts_sf  <- readRDS(tracts_path) |> st_transform(CRS_LL)
.points_sf <- readRDS(points_path) |> st_transform(CRS_LL)
.xy        <- sf::st_coordinates(.points_sf)
points_df  <- tibble(id  = as.character(.points_sf$GEOID),
                     lon = .xy[, 1],
                     lat = .xy[, 2])
log_msg(sprintf("tracts_sf: %d polygons, points_df: %d centroids",
                nrow(tracts_sf), nrow(points_df)))

seattle_path <- latest_cache_rds("seattle_place")
stopifnot(!is.na(seattle_path))
seattle_sf <- readRDS(seattle_path) |> st_transform(CRS_LL)

# Native pipe |> doesn't support `.` placeholder; do the filter explicitly.
.in_seattle <- lengths(st_intersects(tracts_sf, seattle_sf)) > 0
seattle_tract_ids <- as.character(tracts_sf$GEOID[.in_seattle])
log_msg(sprintf("Seattle tracts: %d", length(seattle_tract_ids)))
```

## 2a. MNL coefficients

Pull every coefficient by name so the prediction step is explicit. This MNL
spec is:

```
choice ~ cost + walking_min_alt + bike_tt_alt + drive_tt_alt +
         transit_total_diff_alt + vc_drive_alt | is_work
```

with `reflevel = "drive"`, so drive has no ASC and no `is_work` term.

```{r mnl-coefs}
coefs <- coef(mnl)
get_coef <- function(name) {
  if (!name %in% names(coefs))
    stop("Missing coefficient: ", name,
         "\nAvailable: ", paste(names(coefs), collapse = ", "))
  unname(coefs[[name]])
}
B <- list(
  asc_walk    = get_coef("(Intercept):walk"),
  asc_bike    = get_coef("(Intercept):bike"),
  asc_transit = get_coef("(Intercept):transit"),
  cost        = get_coef("cost"),
  walking_min = get_coef("walking_min_alt"),
  bike_tt     = get_coef("bike_tt_alt"),
  drive_tt    = get_coef("drive_tt_alt"),
  tr_diff     = get_coef("transit_total_diff_alt"),
  vc_drive    = get_coef("vc_drive_alt"),
  iswork_walk    = get_coef("is_work:walk"),
  iswork_bike    = get_coef("is_work:bike"),
  iswork_transit = get_coef("is_work:transit")
)
log_msg(sprintf("VOTT drive ($/hr) base = %.1f, AV-shrunk = %.1f",
                -B$drive_tt / B$cost * 60,
                -B$drive_tt * params$av_drive_tt_shrink / B$cost * 60))
```


# 3. Configuration table

The 14 configurations are the cross-product of {transit network} × {street
network}, restricted by feasibility (Grid / Grid+Local / Node-based assume
transit priority is in place). Each configuration is keyed by `config_id`.

```{r config-table}
log_stage("Stage 3: Define configurations")

# Transit network → required GTFS .zip filename(s) for each (priority, av) cell.
# NA → not evaluated. Same TSP file is used for both priority cells (priority +
# AV) because buses are isolated from car congestion when they have priority.
transit_gtfs <- tribble(
  ~transit_label,  ~transit_id,    ~no_pri_no_av,                 ~no_pri_av,                       ~pri_no_av,                                                         ~pri_av,
  "Baseline",      "baseline",     "kcm_transit_april_26.zip",    "kcm_baseline_av_april_26.zip",   "kcm_baseline_tsp_april_26.zip",                                    "kcm_baseline_tsp_april_26.zip",
  "3x Network",    "triplicate",   "kcm_triplicate_april_26.zip", "kcm_triplicate_av_april_26.zip", "kcm_triplicate_tsp_april_26.zip",                                  "kcm_triplicate_tsp_april_26.zip",
  # Grid uses the (high-frequency) trunk-only `gtfs_grid_frequent.zip`.
  # Grid+Local uses the lower-frequency `gtfs_grid_standard.zip` instead,
  # because adding the locals on top of the frequent layer would over-supply
  # bus service. This file split is intentional — see GTFS-design notes.
  "Grid",          "grid",          NA_character_,                 NA_character_,                   "gtfs_grid_express.zip+gtfs_grid_frequent.zip",                     "gtfs_grid_express.zip+gtfs_grid_frequent.zip",
  "Grid + Local",  "grid_local",    NA_character_,                 NA_character_,                   "gtfs_grid_express_gl.zip+gtfs_grid_standard.zip+gtfs_grid_locals.zip", "gtfs_grid_express_gl.zip+gtfs_grid_standard.zip+gtfs_grid_locals.zip",
  # Node-based: express bus corridors + local feeders (both bus-only; rail
  # comes from the unchanged-agency feeds, same as every other scenario).
  "Node-based",    "node",          NA_character_,                 NA_character_,                   "gtfs_node_bus.zip+gtfs_node_local.zip",                            "gtfs_node_bus.zip+gtfs_node_local.zip"
)

street_meta <- tribble(
  ~street_id,        ~street_label,                     ~transit_priority, ~av_demand, ~run_order,
  "no_pri_no_av",    "Current",                         FALSE,             FALSE,      1L,
  "no_pri_av",       "AV-induced Traffic",              FALSE,             TRUE,       2L,
  "pri_no_av",       "Full Transit Priority",           TRUE,              FALSE,      3L,
  "pri_av",          "Transit Priority + AVs",          TRUE,              TRUE,       4L
)

config_table <- transit_gtfs |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(no_pri_no_av, no_pri_av, pri_no_av, pri_av),
    names_to = "street_id", values_to = "gtfs_combo") |>
  inner_join(street_meta, by = "street_id") |>
  mutate(
    active     = !is.na(gtfs_combo) & !str_detect(gtfs_combo, "^TODO"),
    config_id  = sprintf("%s__%s", transit_id, street_id)
  ) |>
  # Arrange so that within each transit network, the no-AV control runs
  # before the AV variant (run_order = 1, 3 are no-AV; 2, 4 are AV). This
  # makes debug_stop_after_first_av useful: by the time §14 stops, both
  # the no-AV control and the AV scenario have run, so they can be diffed.
  arrange(transit_id, run_order) |>
  select(config_id, transit_id, transit_label, street_id, street_label,
         transit_priority, av_demand, gtfs_combo, active)

# Per-config GTFS file lookup helper.
# Combo strings join multiple zips with "+"; each is looked up in the KCM folder
# (data/gtfs/kcm), then in the designed-network folder (outputs/gtfs).
gtfs_files_for <- function(combo_str) {
  if (is.na(combo_str)) return(character(0))
  parts <- str_split_1(combo_str, fixed("+"))
  paths <- vapply(parts, function(p) {
    hit <- file.path(GTFS_DIRS, p)
    hit <- hit[file.exists(hit)]
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
  }, character(1))
  if (any(is.na(paths)))
    stop("Could not resolve GTFS for combo='", combo_str,
         "': missing ", paste(parts[is.na(paths)], collapse = ", "))
  unname(paths)
}

# Resolve paths up front. A feed that does not exist yet is only an error for a
# config that is actually run (checked in §3a), so a partial build can still run.
config_table$gtfs_paths <- lapply(config_table$gtfs_combo, function(c) {
  if (is.na(c)) return(character(0))
  tryCatch(gtfs_files_for(c), error = function(e) character(0))
})

# Unchanged-agency GTFS (always added to every r5r build).
gtfs_unchanged_paths <- list.files(GTFS_UNCHANGED_DIR,
                                   pattern = "\\.zip$",
                                   full.names = TRUE)
log_msg(sprintf("Unchanged-agency GTFS: %d files", length(gtfs_unchanged_paths)))

write_csv(config_table |> select(-gtfs_paths),
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "config_table.csv"))

cat("\nConfiguration table:\n")
print(config_table |>
        select(config_id, transit_label, street_label, transit_priority,
               av_demand, active),
      n = Inf)
```

## 3a. Selecting which configs to actually run

```{r config-select}
configs_to_run <- config_table |>
  filter(active)

# on top of the active filter). Empty (default) leaves
# configs_to_run unchanged. Keep baseline__no_pri_no_av in the set so the
# §13b unseeded baseline + §15 Vision Zero denominator still resolve.
if (!is.null(params$configs_filter) &&
    length(params$configs_filter) > 0 &&
    any(nzchar(as.character(params$configs_filter)))) {
  keep_ids <- as.character(params$configs_filter)
  before_n <- nrow(configs_to_run)
  configs_to_run <- configs_to_run |> filter(config_id %in% keep_ids)
  log_msg(sprintf("configs_filter → %d/%d configs (%s)",
                  nrow(configs_to_run), before_n,
                  paste(keep_ids, collapse = ", ")))
}

.missing_feeds <- configs_to_run$config_id[lengths(configs_to_run$gtfs_paths) == 0]
if (length(.missing_feeds))
  stop("GTFS feed(s) not found in ", paste(GTFS_DIRS, collapse = " or "), " for: ", paste(.missing_feeds, collapse = ", "),
       " - run the stages that build them first.")
log_msg(sprintf("Will run %d of %d configurations",
                nrow(configs_to_run), nrow(config_table)))
```


# 4. External downloads (RSE + LODES)

## 4a. RSE Index per tract

```{r rse-download}
log_stage("Stage 4a: RSE Index download")

rse_sf <- with_cache("rse_index_seattle",
  list(url = params$rse_index_url, version = "v1"),
  function() {
    log_msg("Fetching RSE Index from arcgis...")
    sf::st_read(params$rse_index_url, quiet = TRUE)
  })

# Normalize to a tract-keyed table. The SDOT layer carries `TRACT` as the
# 4+2 census tract code (e.g. "53.01" meaning tract 005301) without state
# or county prefix. Seattle is entirely inside King County, WA = FIPS 53033,
# so we prepend that to build the full 11-digit GEOID.
SEATTLE_STATE_FIPS  <- "53"
SEATTLE_COUNTY_FIPS <- "033"

# SDOT's TRACT field is the **packed integer** form of the Census tract
# code: the last 2 digits are the fractional part, anything before is the
# integer part. e.g. 402 → tract 4.02 → 6-digit "000402"; 3302 → tract
# 33.02 → "003302"; 700 → tract 7.00 → "000700". A decimal-containing
# value like "53.01" survives the strip-then-pad just as well.
to_geoid11_from_tract <- function(tract_raw) {
  digits <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", as.character(tract_raw))
  # If 6+ digits already, take leftmost 6; otherwise left-pad to 6.
  pad6 <- ifelse(nchar(digits) >= 6,
                 substr(digits, 1, 6),
                 stringr::str_pad(digits, 6, pad = "0"))
  paste0(SEATTLE_STATE_FIPS, SEATTLE_COUNTY_FIPS, pad6)
}

rse_raw <- rse_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename_with(toupper)

if (!"TRACT" %in% names(rse_raw))
  stop("RSE layer has no TRACT field; available: ",
       paste(names(rse_raw), collapse = ", "))
if (!"COMPOSITE_PERCENTILE" %in% names(rse_raw))
  stop("RSE layer has no COMPOSITE_PERCENTILE field; available: ",
       paste(names(rse_raw), collapse = ", "))

cat("Sample TRACT values from RSE layer:\n")
print(utils::head(unique(rse_raw$TRACT), 8))

rse_index <- rse_raw |>
  transmute(
    tract_raw = TRACT,
    GEOID = to_geoid11_from_tract(TRACT),
    rse_composite_percentile = as.numeric(COMPOSITE_PERCENTILE)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(rse_composite_percentile))

# Diagnostic: how does our derived GEOID compare to Seattle tract IDs?
hits <- sum(seattle_tract_ids %in% rse_index$GEOID)
log_msg(sprintf("RSE: %d tracts loaded; %d/%d Seattle tracts matched (%.1f%%)",
                nrow(rse_index), hits, length(seattle_tract_ids),
                100 * hits / length(seattle_tract_ids)))
if (hits == 0) {
  cat("Sample derived GEOIDs:\n")
  print(utils::head(rse_index$GEOID, 8))
  cat("Sample Seattle tract IDs:\n")
  print(utils::head(seattle_tract_ids, 8))
  warning("RSE join produced 0 matches; equity correlation will be NA. ",
          "Inspect samples above and adjust to_geoid11_from_tract() if needed.")
}
```

## 4b. LODES employment per tract

LEHD LODES Workplace Area Characteristics (WAC) gives jobs *at* a workplace
block. Aggregating to tract gives per-tract employment, which is what the
30-min accessibility metric needs.

```{r lodes-download}
log_stage("Stage 4b: LODES WAC download")

lodes_path <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, "lodes_wac_wa_S000_JT00_2022.csv.gz")
if (!file.exists(lodes_path) || params$force_rebuild) {
  log_msg("Downloading LODES WAC (WA, all jobs, all sectors, 2022)...")
  utils::download.file(params$lodes_wac_url, lodes_path, mode = "wb",
                       quiet = FALSE)
}

# w_geocode is a 15-digit block GEOID; tract = first 11 chars.
employment_by_tract <- with_cache("lodes_emp_by_tract",
  list(file = file_signature(lodes_path), version = "v1"),
  function() {
    fread(lodes_path, colClasses = c(w_geocode = "character"))[
      , .(jobs = sum(C000, na.rm = TRUE)),
      by = .(GEOID = substr(w_geocode, 1, 11))
    ] |> as_tibble()
  })

log_msg(sprintf("Employment per tract: %d tracts, total jobs = %.0f",
                nrow(employment_by_tract), sum(employment_by_tract$jobs)))
```


## 4c. SND COMPKEY → OSM way_id mapping (used in §5 + §13a)

This is the foundation for **attribute-join** matching of SDOT data
(street-grid lanes/bus-lane info, traffic counts) to dodgr edges. SDOT's
directional SND/COMPKEY mapping CSV gives the OSM way_id for every
Seattle street segment. Both §5 (bus-lane capacity) and §13a (count
seeding) use this rather than spatial buffer matching, because spatial
matching catches parallel side streets and breaks both pipelines.

```{r snd-mappings}
log_stage("Stage 4c: SND COMPKEY → OSM way_id mapping")

snd_mappings <- with_cache("snd_mappings",
  list(snd_csv_sig = file_signature(params$snd_compkey_csv),
       repair_sig  = if (file.exists(params$way_id_repair_csv))
                       file_signature(params$way_id_repair_csv) else "none",
       version = "v5_force_character_repair_csv"),
  function() {
    snd_path <- params$snd_compkey_csv
    if (!file.exists(snd_path))
      stop("SND/COMPKEY mapping CSV not found at: ", snd_path,
           "\nThis is required for way_id-based bus-lane and seed matching.")
    snd_dir <- readr::read_csv(snd_path, show_col_types = FALSE,
                               progress = FALSE)
    log_msg(sprintf("Loaded %d directional SND/COMPKEY mapping rows",
                    nrow(snd_dir)))

    # ---- (1) Raw long-form mapping: one row per (COMPKEY, SND_ID,
    # TRAFFICDIR, way_id). Same content as before but no SND_ID-level
    # collapse — divided-highway corridors (Aurora etc.) need a true
    # many-to-many mapping to attribute count/capacity correctly per
    # direction.
    raw_long <- snd_dir |>
      filter(!is.na(SND_ID), !is.na(OSM_WAY_ID),
             !is.na(COMPKEY), COMPKEY > 0, !is.na(TRAFFICDIR)) |>
      transmute(
        COMPKEY    = as.character(COMPKEY),
        SND_ID     = as.character(SND_ID),
        TRAFFICDIR = toupper(trimws(as.character(TRAFFICDIR))),
        way_id     = as.character(OSM_WAY_ID),
        best_overlap_m = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(MATCH_OVERLAP_M)))

    # ---- (2) Overlay repair CSV (produced by StreetSetup.Rmd). For each
    # (COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR) triple present in the repair, drop the
    # raw row(s) and replace with one row per way_id listed.
    if (!is.null(params$way_id_repair_csv) &&
        nzchar(params$way_id_repair_csv) &&
        file.exists(params$way_id_repair_csv)) {
      # Force ALL columns to character. WAY_IDS in particular must NOT be
      # type-inferred as numeric — multi-way_id rows have embedded commas
      # that readr otherwise eats as column separators / thousands marks,
      # silently corrupting OSM IDs (e.g. "1039476783,432302080" becomes
      # the single number 1039476783432302080). Without this, the
      # "repair authoritative per way" override silently fails for any
      # triple that maps to more than one way_id.
      repair_raw <- readr::read_csv(
        params$way_id_repair_csv,
        show_col_types = FALSE,
        progress = FALSE,
        col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()))
      repair_long <- repair_raw |>
        mutate(TRAFFICDIR = toupper(trimws(TRAFFICDIR))) |>
        tidyr::separate_rows(WAY_IDS, sep = ",") |>
        transmute(COMPKEY, SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR,
                  way_id = trimws(WAY_IDS),
                  best_overlap_m = NA_real_) |>
        filter(nzchar(way_id))

      # Repair is authoritative for every way_id it mentions: drop ALL raw
      # rows for those way_ids, not just rows whose (COMPKEY, SND_ID,
      # TRAFFICDIR) triple matches. This is necessary because the raw
      # mapping (OSM_WAY_ID) sometimes attaches a way to a
      # *different* SND COMPKEY than the corridor it actually belongs to
      # (e.g. Ship Canal Bridge mis-matched to 6th Ave NE because of
      # spatial proximity). Triple-level anti-join leaves those stale
      # rows in place; way_id-level removal cleans them out.
      repaired_way_ids <- unique(repair_long$way_id)

      mapping_long <- bind_rows(
        raw_long |> filter(!way_id %in% repaired_way_ids),
        repair_long
      )
      log_msg(sprintf("Applied way_id repair: %d way_ids replaced, %d new rows",
                      length(repaired_way_ids), nrow(repair_long)))
    } else {
      mapping_long <- raw_long
      log_msg("No way_id repair CSV; using the raw crosswalk mapping only")
    }

    # ---- (3) Per-SND_ID attributes (constant across directions / way_ids).
    snd_attrs <- snd_dir |>
      filter(!is.na(SND_ID)) |>
      group_by(SND_ID) |>
      summarise(
        snd_arterial_code = suppressWarnings(as.integer(SND_ARTERIAL_CODE[1])),
        snd_segment_type  = SND_SEGMENT_TYPE[1],
        art_descript      = ARTDESCRIPT[1],
        stname_ord        = STNAME_ORD[1],
        ord_stname_concat = SND_ORD_STNAME_CONCAT[1],
        snd_oneway        = (toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAY[1]))) == "Y"),
        snd_oneway_dir    = ONEWAYDIR[1],
        snd_segdir        = SEGDIR[1],
        .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(SND_ID = as.character(SND_ID))

    # ---- (3b) Functional-class priority for picking a representative SND
    # attribution per way_id. When the raw crosswalk mapping attached a
    # single OSM way to multiple SND COMPKEYs (legitimately — long ways
    # cross several SND segments; OR wrongly — Ship Canal Bridge got
    # spatially mismatched to a 6th Ave NE block in addition to its
    # correct I-5 SB block), `stname_ord = stname_ord[1]` is order-
    # sensitive and picks whichever happens to come first. Sort by
    # functional class first so the high-class (freeway > arterial >
    # collector > residential) attribution wins the [1] tiebreak.
    .art_priority <- c(
      "Interstate/Freeway"  = 1L,
      "State Route/Freeway" = 2L,
      "Principal Arterial"  = 3L,
      "Minor Arterial"      = 4L,
      "Collector Arterial"  = 5L,
      "County Arterial"     = 6L,
      "Not Designated"      = 7L
    )

    # ---- (4) Build the three lookup tables.
    #   * snd_to_way: keyed by (SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, way_id) with snd attrs.
    #     Downstream consumers that previously used SND_ID-only access still
    #     work (multiple rows per SND_ID is fine for joins; way_snd_attrs
    #     handles per-way aggregation).
    snd_to_way <- mapping_long |>
      distinct(SND_ID, TRAFFICDIR, way_id) |>
      left_join(snd_attrs, by = "SND_ID")

    #   * compkey_to_way: keyed by (COMPKEY, TRAFFICDIR, way_id). Carries
    #     SND_ID and best_overlap_m. Note: downstream `inner_join(... by =
    #     "COMPKEY")` may now produce multiple rows per COMPKEY (one per
    #     way_id) — existing aggregations (group_by(way_id) |> slice(1))
    #     collapse correctly.
    compkey_to_way <- mapping_long |>
      distinct(COMPKEY, TRAFFICDIR, way_id, SND_ID, best_overlap_m)

    #   * way_snd_attrs: one row per way_id, aggregating attrs across all
    #     SND_IDs that map to it. Same shape as before — drop-in compatible
    #     with all existing callers.
    way_snd_attrs <- mapping_long |>
      left_join(snd_attrs, by = "SND_ID") |>
      # Order by functional-class priority so the highest-class attribution
      # wins the [1] tiebreak below (see comment at .art_priority above).
      mutate(.art_pri = coalesce(unname(.art_priority[art_descript]), 99L)) |>
      arrange(way_id, .art_pri) |>
      group_by(way_id) |>
      summarise(
        n_snd_segments    = dplyr::n_distinct(SND_ID),
        snd_arterial_code = {
          v <- snd_arterial_code[!is.na(snd_arterial_code)]
          if (length(v) == 0) NA_integer_ else as.integer(min(v))
        },
        snd_segment_type  = snd_segment_type[1],
        art_descript      = art_descript[1],
        stname_ord        = stname_ord[1],
        ord_stname_concat = ord_stname_concat[1],
        snd_oneway        = any(snd_oneway, na.rm = TRUE),
        snd_oneway_dir    = snd_oneway_dir[1],
        snd_segdir        = snd_segdir[1],
        .groups = "drop")

    log_msg(sprintf("  mapping rows      : %d", nrow(mapping_long)))
    log_msg(sprintf("  snd_to_way        : %d distinct (SND_ID,TRAFFICDIR,way_id)",
                    nrow(snd_to_way)))
    log_msg(sprintf("  compkey_to_way    : %d distinct (COMPKEY,TRAFFICDIR,way_id)",
                    nrow(compkey_to_way)))
    log_msg(sprintf("  way_snd_attrs     : %d distinct ways",
                    nrow(way_snd_attrs)))
    list(snd_to_way = snd_to_way,
         compkey_to_way = compkey_to_way,
         way_snd_attrs  = way_snd_attrs)
  })

snd_to_way     <- snd_mappings$snd_to_way
compkey_to_way <- snd_mappings$compkey_to_way
way_snd_attrs  <- snd_mappings$way_snd_attrs
```


# 5. Annotate dodgr graph with capacity & bus-lane geometry

This step produces a single annotated graph (cached) carrying both
`cap_vph_baseline` and `cap_vph_priority` per edge. The two street-network
variants ("baseline" / "priority") are then a column-pick at run-time.

The per-edge capacity is set in two steps:

1. **SDOT ARTDESCRIPT first** (preferred). The SND data classifies every
   COMPKEY by functional class (Interstate/Freeway, Principal Arterial,
   Minor Arterial, …). This is the canonical Seattle functional-class
   taxonomy and reflects how each segment actually operates — Aurora
   Ave N is a Principal Arterial *not* a freeway, even though OSM tags
   it `highway = trunk` (because it's SR-99). We use the HCM 6th Edition
   capacities for signalized urban arterials at g/C ≈ 0.45.

2. **OSM highway class fallback** when no SND match (residential side
   streets, ways outside SDOT's network, ramps without an SND_ID).

The BPR α coefficient is also per-class, per literature:

| Class | cap/lane (vph) | BPR α | β |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interstate/Freeway | 2200 | 0.15 | 4.0 — FHWA BPR 1964 |
| State Route/Freeway | 1900 | 0.20 | 4.0 |
| Principal Arterial | 850 | 0.71 | 4.0 — NCHRP 365 multilane arterial |
| Minor Arterial | 750 | 0.71 | 4.0 |
| Collector Arterial | 600 | 0.50 | 4.0 — Spiess 1990 |
| County Arterial | 700 | 0.50 | 4.0 |
| Not Designated | 400 | 0.20 | 4.0 — low volume |
| Residential (OSM fallback) | 400 | 0.20 | 4.0 |

```{r annotate-dodgr-caps}
log_stage("Stage 5: Annotate dodgr graph with capacity / bus-lane info")

# ---- (a) SDOT ARTDESCRIPT-based capacity & BPR α (preferred) ----
# HCM signalized arterial capacity: saturation flow (~1800-1900 vph/lane)
# × g/C ratio (typical Seattle urban 0.40-0.50) → ~750-850 vph/through-lane.
# Freeway capacity: HCM 2-lane mainline ~2200 vph/lane. State Route/Freeway
# is a mix (SR-99 viaduct = freeway-like; SR-99 surface = arterial-like) —
# pick a middle 1900 vph.
ART_CAP_VPH <- c(
  "Interstate/Freeway"  = 2200,
  "State Route/Freeway" = 1900,
  "Principal Arterial"  = 850,
  "Minor Arterial"      = 750,
  "Collector Arterial"  = 600,
  "County Arterial"     = 700,
  # "Not Designated" is residential-like (local/unsigned in SDOT). HCM
  # Class IV signalized streets with on-street parking + stop-controlled
  # intersections every block have effective through-capacity of
  # 150-250 vph/lane. Seattle residentials are also narrower than the
  # AASHTO subdivision-road standard, so we pick 250 (HCM mid-range).
  "Not Designated"      = 250
)

# Per-class BPR α. β stays at 4.0 (FHWA default, well-attested).
# Higher α = sharper slowdown as V/C → 1.0:
#   At V/C = 1.0: factor = 1 + α
#   At V/C = 0.5: factor = 1 + α × 0.0625 ≈ 1 (negligible)
# Freeway α=0.15 means free-flow speed even at saturation. Urban arterial
# α=0.71 (NCHRP 365 "multilane signalized arterial") means saturated
# arterial slows to ~60% of free-flow speed at V/C=1.0 — matches the
# empirical observation that Aurora at AM peak runs ~17-20 mph vs ~30
# mph free-flow.
ART_BPR_ALPHA <- c(
  "Interstate/Freeway"  = 0.15,  # FHWA freeway default
  "State Route/Freeway" = 0.20,  # Limited-access mix
  "Principal Arterial"  = 0.71,  # NCHRP 365 signalized arterial
  "Minor Arterial"      = 0.71,  # NCHRP 365 signalized arterial
  "Collector Arterial"  = 0.50,  # Spiess (1990) urban arterial
  "County Arterial"     = 0.50,
  # "Not Designated" α was 0.20 (matching freeway) which is wrong — local
  # streets with stop-controlled intersections have signal-delay-driven
  # slowdown that fires at much lower V/C than a freeway. Spiess (1990)
  # gives α=0.50 for "urban local" / neighborhood streets. NB: under static
  # link-based assignment, residential V/C is typically <0.01 so this
  # change has little active effect — but it is the methodologically
  # correct value, would matter under AV-induced rerouting onto locals,
  # and reflects the principle that residentials ≠ freeways.
  "Not Designated"      = 0.50
)

# ---- (b) OSM highway fallback (when no SND/ARTDESCRIPT match) ----
# Critical change: trunk and primary used to share 2200 vph/lane because
# OSM tags state highways (Aurora=SR-99, Lake City Way=SR-522) as `trunk`.
# These are functionally arterial. We now treat OSM-trunk-without-SND as
# arterial-class (1900 vph; matches State Route/Freeway midpoint).
OSM_CAP_VPH <- c(
  motorway      = 2200, motorway_link = 1700,
  trunk         = 1900, trunk_link    = 1500,
  primary       = 850,  primary_link  = 750,
  secondary     = 750,  secondary_link= 650,
  tertiary      = 600,  tertiary_link = 500,
  # residential/unclassified moved 400 → 250 to reflect HCM Class IV
  # signalized streets with on-street parking + stop-controlled
  # intersections every block. Seattle residentials are narrower than
  # the AASHTO subdivision standard.
  residential   = 250,  unclassified  = 250,
  living_street = 150,  service       = 100
)
OSM_BPR_ALPHA <- c(
  motorway      = 0.15, motorway_link = 0.15,
  trunk         = 0.50, trunk_link    = 0.50,
  primary       = 0.71, primary_link  = 0.71,
  secondary     = 0.71, secondary_link= 0.71,
  tertiary      = 0.50, tertiary_link = 0.50,
  # residential α moved 0.20 → 0.50 (Spiess 1990 "urban local").
  # Residentials should NOT share the freeway-default α — stop-controlled
  # intersections produce signal-delay-driven slowdown that fires at
  # lower V/C than a freeway-style flow-density curve.
  residential   = 0.50, unclassified  = 0.50,
  living_street = 0.50, service       = 0.50
)

# Default lane count when OSM `lanes` is missing.
DEFAULT_LANES <- c(
  motorway      = 3, motorway_link = 1,
  trunk         = 2, trunk_link    = 1,
  primary       = 2, primary_link  = 1,
  secondary     = 1, secondary_link= 1,
  tertiary      = 1, tertiary_link = 1,
  residential   = 1, unclassified  = 1,
  living_street = 1, service       = 1
)

# Apply lane / capacity defaults, preferring SDOT ARTDESCRIPT over OSM.
# `way_snd_attrs` carries the art_descript per way_id from §4c. For any
# edge whose way_id is in that lookup, we use the ARTDESCRIPT-based
# capacity + BPR α; otherwise we fall back to the OSM-highway-based
# values.
annotate_caps <- function(g, way_snd_attrs = NULL) {
  hwy <- as.character(g$highway)
  way_ids <- dgr_way_id(g)

  # ---- Look up ARTDESCRIPT per edge from way_snd_attrs ----
  art_per_edge <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(g))
  snd_oneway_per_edge <- rep(NA, nrow(g))   # NA = no SND entry for this way
  if (!is.null(way_snd_attrs) && nrow(way_snd_attrs) > 0 && !is.null(way_ids)) {
    art_lookup <- setNames(as.character(way_snd_attrs$art_descript),
                           as.character(way_snd_attrs$way_id))
    art_per_edge <- unname(art_lookup[as.character(way_ids)])

    snd_lookup <- setNames(as.logical(way_snd_attrs$snd_oneway),
                           as.character(way_snd_attrs$way_id))
    snd_oneway_per_edge <- unname(snd_lookup[as.character(way_ids)])
  }

  # ---- OSM oneway flag per edge (fallback for `snd_oneway`) ----
  # Requires StreetSetup.Rmd to include "oneway" in `keep_cols`.
  # For older graph caches without the column, defaults to FALSE (two-way
  # — matches OSM convention for an untagged way). `oneway=-1` (reverse
  # direction) still counts as one-way for capacity / count-attribution
  # purposes; dodgr already handles the geometry orientation.
  if ("oneway" %in% names(g)) {
    osm_oneway_str <- tolower(trimws(as.character(g$oneway)))
    osm_oneway_per_edge <- osm_oneway_str %in% c("yes", "true", "1", "-1")
  } else {
    osm_oneway_per_edge <- rep(FALSE, nrow(g))
    log_msg("  WARNING: graph has no `oneway` column. Rebuild via ",
            "StreetSetup.Rmd (with `oneway` in keep_cols) to enable ",
            "the OSM oneway fallback.")
  }

  # ---- Effective oneway: SND first, OSM fallback ----
  # `coalesce(snd, osm)` gives SND precedence when the way has an SND entry,
  # else OSM. This matches the lane-count fallback pattern (SDOT first, OSM
  # if NA). For ways outside the SDOT network (side streets, some ramps),
  # OSM is now the only signal — previously these were assumed two-way.
  effective_oneway_per_edge <- dplyr::coalesce(snd_oneway_per_edge,
                                               osm_oneway_per_edge)

  # ---- Lanes ----
  lanes_eff <- if ("lanes_eff" %in% names(g)) g$lanes_eff else NULL
  if (is.null(lanes_eff)) {
    lanes_raw <- if ("lanes" %in% names(g))
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(g$lanes)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(g))
    lanes_eff <- coalesce(lanes_raw, unname(DEFAULT_LANES[hwy]), 1)
  }

  # ---- Per-lane capacity: ARTDESCRIPT first, OSM fallback ----
  cap_from_art <- unname(ART_CAP_VPH[art_per_edge])
  cap_from_osm <- coalesce(unname(OSM_CAP_VPH[hwy]), 400)
  cap_per_lane <- coalesce(cap_from_art, cap_from_osm)

  # ---- BPR alpha: same precedence ----
  alpha_from_art <- unname(ART_BPR_ALPHA[art_per_edge])
  alpha_from_osm <- coalesce(unname(OSM_BPR_ALPHA[hwy]), 0.20)
  bpr_alpha_eff  <- coalesce(alpha_from_art, alpha_from_osm)

  g$lanes_eff        <- lanes_eff
  g$cap_per_lane     <- cap_per_lane
  g$cap_vph_baseline <- pmax(1, lanes_eff * cap_per_lane)
  g$bpr_alpha_eff    <- bpr_alpha_eff
  g$cap_source       <- ifelse(!is.na(cap_from_art),
                                "art_descript", "osm_highway")
  g$art_descript     <- art_per_edge   # keep for diagnostics
  g$snd_oneway       <- snd_oneway_per_edge
  g$osm_oneway       <- osm_oneway_per_edge
  g$effective_oneway <- effective_oneway_per_edge
  g$oneway_source    <- ifelse(!is.na(snd_oneway_per_edge), "snd", "osm")

  # Free-flow time in seconds derived from edge length / dodgr's `time`
  # column (which encodes free-flow time at the chosen wt_profile).
  g$t0_sec <- if ("time" %in% names(g)) as.numeric(g$time) else
              as.numeric(g$d_weighted) / pmax(g$speed, 1) * 3600 / 1000

  # Diagnostic summary
  log_msg(sprintf("  cap source: %d edges from ARTDESCRIPT (%.1f%%), %d from OSM highway (%.1f%%)",
                  sum(g$cap_source == "art_descript"),
                  100 * mean(g$cap_source == "art_descript"),
                  sum(g$cap_source == "osm_highway"),
                  100 * mean(g$cap_source == "osm_highway")))
  log_msg(sprintf("  cap_per_lane: median = %.0f vph (ARTDESCRIPT), %.0f vph (OSM)",
                  median(cap_per_lane[g$cap_source == "art_descript"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  median(cap_per_lane[g$cap_source == "osm_highway"], na.rm = TRUE)))
  log_msg(sprintf("  oneway: %d edges (%.1f%%) one-way overall; from SND: %d, from OSM fallback: %d",
                  sum(effective_oneway_per_edge),
                  100 * mean(effective_oneway_per_edge),
                  sum(effective_oneway_per_edge & g$oneway_source == "snd"),
                  sum(effective_oneway_per_edge & g$oneway_source == "osm")))
  g
}

# Schema helpers — Phase 1 dodgr graph uses SC-format columns. The mapping
# below normalizes references so downstream code reads from the right cols
# regardless of which dodgr schema the cache happens to use.
dgr_col <- function(g, names) {
  hit <- intersect(names, names(g))
  if (length(hit) == 0)
    stop("None of these columns found in graph: ",
         paste(names, collapse = ", "),
         "\nAvailable: ", paste(names(g), collapse = ", "))
  hit[[1]]
}
dgr_from_x  <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx0_x", "from_lon", "from_x"))]]
dgr_from_y  <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx0_y", "from_lat", "from_y"))]]
dgr_to_x    <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx1_x", "to_lon",   "to_x"))]]
dgr_to_y    <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx1_y", "to_lat",   "to_y"))]]
dgr_from_id <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx0",   "from_id"))]]
dgr_to_id   <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c(".vx1",   "to_id"))]]
dgr_edge_id <- function(g) g[[dgr_col(g, c("edge_",  "edge_id", "id"))]]
# Pairwise dodgr routing. dodgr 0.4.3's `dodgr_dists(pairwise = TRUE)` is
# single-threaded and crawls (~7 min for 20k pairs on 1.1M edges). We get
# a 50-100× speedup by exploiting the fact that most OD sets repeat
# origins / dests heavily: compute a full unique-origin × unique-dest
# matrix (multi-threaded under the hood) and then look up the paired
# entries by name. For our universe (~200 unique tract centroids +
# gateways) the 200×200 matrix takes seconds even on the full graph.
#
# Returns a vector of length `length(from)`.
route_pairwise_times <- function(g, from, to, shortest = FALSE) {
  # dodgr_times with pairwise (dodgr ≥ 0.4 had this; 0.4.3 doesn't)
  if ("pairwise" %in% names(formals(dodgr::dodgr_times))) {
    return(as.numeric(dodgr::dodgr_times(graph = g, from = from, to = to,
                                         shortest = shortest,
                                         pairwise = TRUE)))
  }
  # Standalone dodgr_times_pairwise (may exist in namespace even if not
  # exported)
  ns <- asNamespace("dodgr")
  if (exists("dodgr_times_pairwise", envir = ns, inherits = FALSE)) {
    fn <- get("dodgr_times_pairwise", envir = ns)
    return(as.numeric(fn(graph = g, from = from, to = to,
                         shortest = shortest)))
  }
  # Fallback: matrix mode on unique vertices, look up paired cells.
  # Set d_weighted := time_weighted so dodgr_dists returns times.
  g_t <- g
  g_t$d_weighted <- g_t$time_weighted
  from_chr <- as.character(from)
  to_chr   <- as.character(to)
  u_from <- unique(from_chr)
  u_to   <- unique(to_chr)
  m <- dodgr::dodgr_dists(graph = g_t, from = u_from, to = u_to,
                          shortest = TRUE)  # uses d_weighted = time
  m[cbind(match(from_chr, rownames(m)),
          match(to_chr,   colnames(m)))]
}

route_pairwise_dists <- function(g, from, to, shortest = FALSE) {
  # Matrix mode on unique vertices, look up paired cells.
  # `shortest = FALSE` → routes by time_weighted, returns d_weighted along
  # that path (i.e. distance travelled on the time-shortest route).
  from_chr <- as.character(from)
  to_chr   <- as.character(to)
  u_from <- unique(from_chr)
  u_to   <- unique(to_chr)
  m <- dodgr::dodgr_dists(graph = g, from = u_from, to = u_to,
                          shortest = shortest)
  m[cbind(match(from_chr, rownames(m)),
          match(to_chr,   colnames(m)))]
}

# OSM way ID per edge. SC-format dodgr graphs store this as `object_`;
# weight_streetnet-from-PBF uses `way_id`. Confirmed empirically that
# `object_` matches gateway OSM_IDs (21 / 26 hits → exact-match path
# works for those, FNN fallback covers the rest).
dgr_way_id  <- function(g) {
  col <- intersect(c("object_", "way_id"), names(g))
  if (length(col) == 0) return(NULL)
  as.character(g[[col[[1]]]])
}

dodgr_graph <- annotate_caps(dodgr_graph, way_snd_attrs = way_snd_attrs)

# Match Seattle bus-lane info to dodgr edges via attribute join on the
# OSM way_id (NOT spatial buffer). The buffer approach mismatches parallel
# residential streets and small connectors near transit corridors, marking
# them as bus-lane-affected and reducing their capacity to residual=50 vph
# — the same anti-pattern that broke the seed pipeline. Instead we join
# via compkey_to_way + a bearing-aware directional split (per
# direction lanes from SAMELANECOUNT vs OPSLANECOUNT).
dodgr_graph_annotated <- with_cache("dodgr_motorcar_caps",
  list(g_sig = digest::digest(list(
         edge_ids = dgr_edge_id(dodgr_graph),
         hwy = dodgr_graph$highway,
         lanes = dodgr_graph$lanes_eff,
         cap   = dodgr_graph$cap_per_lane,
         alpha = dodgr_graph$bpr_alpha_eff,
         oneway = dodgr_graph$effective_oneway,    # invalidate when
                                                   # oneway annotation changes
         way_id = dgr_way_id(dodgr_graph))),
       lanes_sig = digest::digest(file_signature(params$seattle_lanes_geojson)),
       snd_sig = digest::digest(snd_mappings),
       residual = params$bus_lane_residual_local_vph,
       version = "v7_osm_oneway_fallback"),  # adds effective_oneway per edge
                                             # (SND first, OSM fallback);
                                             # cap/alpha ARTDESCRIPT-driven;
                                             # residential cap 400→250 and
                                             # α 0.20→0.50 (HCM Class IV +
                                             # Spiess 1990).
  function() {
    g <- dodgr_graph
    g$bus_lane_affected <- FALSE
    g$cap_vph_priority  <- g$cap_vph_baseline
    g$new_lanes_eff     <- g$lanes_eff

    if (!file.exists(params$seattle_lanes_geojson)) {
      log_msg("WARNING: street_grid.geojson not found; bus-lane scenarios will be no-ops")
      return(g)
    }

    # ---- 1. street-grid attributes (no geometry — attribute join only) ----
    sl_attrs <- sf::st_read(params$seattle_lanes_geojson, quiet = TRUE) |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    log_sub(sprintf("street-grid feature attribute rows: %d", nrow(sl_attrs)))

    # ---- 2. Join street-grid COMPKEY → way_id via SND mapping ----
    # Bring `best_overlap_m` along too — it's the tiebreaker for picking a
    # representative street-grid row when multiple COMPKEYs map to the same way.
    sl_with_way <- sl_attrs |>
      mutate(COMPKEY = as.character(COMPKEY)) |>
      inner_join(compkey_to_way |> select(COMPKEY, way_id, best_overlap_m),
                 by = "COMPKEY") |>
      transmute(
        COMPKEY,
        way_id,
        best_overlap_m,
        SEGDIR              = as.character(SEGDIR),
        ONEWAY              = toupper(trimws(as.character(ONEWAY))),
        SPEEDLIMIT          = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(SPEEDLIMIT)),
        SAMELANECOUNT       = suppressWarnings(as.integer(SAMELANECOUNT)),
        OPSLANECOUNT        = suppressWarnings(as.integer(OPSLANECOUNT)),
        NEW_SAMELANECOUNT   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(NEW_SAMELANECOUNT)),
        NEW_OPSLANECOUNT    = suppressWarnings(as.integer(NEW_OPSLANECOUNT)),
        has_proposed_bus_lane = as.logical(has_proposed_bus_lane))
    log_sub(sprintf("street-grid rows joined to way_id: %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                    nrow(sl_with_way), nrow(sl_attrs),
                    100 * nrow(sl_with_way) / nrow(sl_attrs)))

    # ---- 3. Aggregate to one row per way_id ----
    # When multiple SDOT COMPKEYs map to the same OSM way (long arterial
    # split into many SDOT segments at intersections), pick the row that
    # represents the bus-lane scenario best: prefer rows where
    # has_proposed_bus_lane is TRUE; tiebreak on largest MATCH_OVERLAP_M
    # (most representative SDOT segment for the way).
    way_attrs <- sl_with_way |>
      group_by(way_id) |>
      mutate(has_proposed_bl_any = any(has_proposed_bus_lane, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      arrange(desc(coalesce(has_proposed_bus_lane, FALSE)),
              desc(coalesce(best_overlap_m, 0)),
              .by_group = TRUE) |>
      slice(1) |>
      ungroup() |>
      transmute(
        way_id,
        sl_segdir          = SEGDIR,
        sl_speed_mph       = SPEEDLIMIT,
        sl_same            = SAMELANECOUNT,
        sl_ops             = OPSLANECOUNT,
        sl_new_same        = NEW_SAMELANECOUNT,
        sl_new_ops         = NEW_OPSLANECOUNT,
        sl_oneway_attr     = ONEWAY == "Y",
        sl_has_proposed_bl = has_proposed_bl_any) |>
      # If NEW_ is NA but no proposed change, post = current.
      mutate(
        sl_new_same = if_else(is.na(sl_new_same) & !isTRUE(sl_has_proposed_bl),
                              sl_same, sl_new_same),
        sl_new_ops  = if_else(is.na(sl_new_ops)  & !isTRUE(sl_has_proposed_bl),
                              sl_ops,  sl_new_ops))
    log_sub(sprintf("Distinct OSM way_ids with SDOT lane attrs: %d", nrow(way_attrs)))
    log_sub(sprintf("  ways with proposed bus lane: %d",
                    sum(way_attrs$sl_has_proposed_bl, na.rm = TRUE)))

    # ---- 4. Attribute-join onto the dodgr graph by way_id ----
    graph_way_id <- dgr_way_id(g)
    if (is.null(graph_way_id))
      stop("Graph has no way_id; can't run attribute-join bus-lane match.")
    way_lookup <- match(graph_way_id, way_attrs$way_id)
    matched    <- !is.na(way_lookup)
    log_sub(sprintf("Dodgr edges joined to SDOT lane attrs: %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                    sum(matched), nrow(g), 100 * mean(matched)))

    # ---- 5. Direction handling via edge bearing vs SEGDIR ----
    # SAMELANECOUNT is the lane count in the street-grid feature's SEGDIR
    # direction; OPSLANECOUNT is the opposite. dodgr edges are directional —
    # decide which one applies by comparing the edge's compass bearing
    # (computed from from-lat/lon to to-lat/lon) to SEGDIR's cardinal angle.
    cardinal_bearing <- c(N =   0, NE = 45,  E = 90,  SE = 135,
                          S = 180, SW = 225, W = 270, NW = 315)
    bearing_from_to <- function(from_lat, from_lon, to_lat, to_lon) {
      dy <- to_lat - from_lat
      dx <- to_lon - from_lon
      ((90 - atan2(dy, dx) * 180 / pi) %% 360)
    }
    edge_bear <- bearing_from_to(dgr_from_y(g), dgr_from_x(g),
                                 dgr_to_y(g),   dgr_to_x(g))

    sl_segdir_v <- way_attrs$sl_segdir[way_lookup]
    segdir_bear <- unname(cardinal_bearing[sl_segdir_v])
    bearing_gap <- pmin(abs(edge_bear - segdir_bear),
                        360 - abs(edge_bear - segdir_bear))
    same_side   <- !is.na(bearing_gap) & bearing_gap < 90

    same_v     <- way_attrs$sl_same[way_lookup]
    ops_v      <- way_attrs$sl_ops[way_lookup]
    new_same_v <- way_attrs$sl_new_same[way_lookup]
    new_ops_v  <- way_attrs$sl_new_ops[way_lookup]
    has_bl_v   <- way_attrs$sl_has_proposed_bl[way_lookup]

    # ---- 6. Apply per-edge bus-lane info ----
    # bus_lane_affected uses the way's "any compkey has proposal" flag
    # (so all directional edges of a flagged way participate in the
    # capacity reduction; SDOT geometry doesn't tell us which direction
    # is losing the lane).
    g$bus_lane_affected <- coalesce(has_bl_v, FALSE)

    # Helper for CURRENT lanes (always fall back to highway-class default
    # for NA / 0 SDOT values — those are usually sidewalk-only or
    # incomplete records; capping at 1 vph would create false bottlenecks).
    safe_current <- function(sdot_lanes, fallback) {
      ok <- is.finite(sdot_lanes) & sdot_lanes > 0
      ifelse(ok, sdot_lanes, fallback)
    }

    # Helper for NEW lanes (post-bus-lane scenario). Different rule:
    # - If NEW value is finite & positive → use it.
    # - If NA / 0 / negative AND the way has a proposed bus lane → 0
    #   (the lane is being taken; downstream the residual=50 vph
    #   fallback applies).
    # - If NA AND no proposal → use current lanes (no change).
    safe_new <- function(new_v, has_bl, current_lanes) {
      ok        <- is.finite(new_v) & new_v > 0
      proposed  <- !is.na(has_bl) & has_bl
      ifelse(ok, new_v,
             ifelse(proposed, 0, current_lanes))
    }

    # Per-direction current lanes
    g$lanes_eff[matched] <- ifelse(same_side[matched],
                                   safe_current(same_v[matched],
                                                g$lanes_eff[matched]),
                                   safe_current(ops_v[matched],
                                                g$lanes_eff[matched]))
    # Per-direction NEW lanes (handles missing-data-on-proposed-bus-lane
    # case correctly)
    g$new_lanes_eff[matched] <- ifelse(
      same_side[matched],
      safe_new(new_same_v[matched], has_bl_v[matched],
               g$lanes_eff[matched]),
      safe_new(new_ops_v[matched],  has_bl_v[matched],
               g$lanes_eff[matched]))

    # Re-derive baseline cap from the updated lanes_eff.
    g$cap_vph_baseline <- pmax(1, g$lanes_eff * g$cap_per_lane)

    # CRITICAL: re-derive cap_vph_priority from the UPDATED baseline so
    # non-affected edges have the right capacity in priority configs.
    g$cap_vph_priority <- g$cap_vph_baseline

    # Bus-lane-affected edges drop to new_lanes_eff × cap_per_lane, with the
    # `bus_lane_residual_local_vph` fallback when NEW = 0 (or NA with proposal).
    residual <- params$bus_lane_residual_local_vph
    aff <- which(g$bus_lane_affected)
    new_cap_aff <- ifelse(g$new_lanes_eff[aff] <= 0 |
                          is.na(g$new_lanes_eff[aff]),
                          residual,
                          g$new_lanes_eff[aff] * g$cap_per_lane[aff])
    g$cap_vph_priority[aff] <- new_cap_aff
    # NOTE: a fully-converted edge (new_lanes_eff <= 0) KEEPS this residual
    # capacity ONLY so V/C and cap-delta stay honest and finite. The actual
    # removal of THROUGH traffic happens in §11 run_equilibrium_v2 (the
    # `.broken_edge` block): for priority configs those edges are pinned to
    # BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC in the routing time and their flow_seed is zeroed,
    # so traffic reroutes around them instead of flooding the residual pipe.
    g
  })

log_msg(sprintf("Annotated graph: %d edges; bus-lane-affected: %d (%.2f%%)",
                nrow(dodgr_graph_annotated),
                sum(dodgr_graph_annotated$bus_lane_affected),
                100 * mean(dodgr_graph_annotated$bus_lane_affected)))
log_msg(sprintf("  cap baseline mean=%.0f vph; priority mean=%.0f vph",
                mean(dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_baseline),
```
