```{r annotate-dodgr-caps}
                mean(dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_priority)))
log_msg(sprintf("  edges where priority < baseline cap: %d (%.2f%%)",
                sum(dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_priority <
                      dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_baseline),
                100 * mean(dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_priority <
                             dodgr_graph_annotated$cap_vph_baseline)))
```

## 5a. Observed-flow seed (runs in §13)

Observed-flow seeding is a 1-time cost that requires a baseline equilibrium
run, so the actual pipeline runs in **§13 — Build observed-flow seed**,
after the Daysim demand frame, equilibrium helper, and per-trip frame are
defined. We just declare a placeholder column here so the BPR step can
look it up safely on first iteration.

```{r seed-placeholder}
dodgr_graph_annotated$flow_seed <- 0
```


# 6. Build Daysim demand with cordon gateways

Phase 2 evaluates network alternatives over the **Daysim synthetic
population**, not the HTS sample. HTS still drives per-trip MNL prediction
(it's the only data with the per-trip variables that enter the choice
model), but OD-level trip totals come from Daysim's full trip table.

Trips that begin or end outside Seattle are collapsed to one of five
cordon **gateway** points placed where major freeways and arterials cross
the city boundary. Each external tract is matched to its nearest gateway
by free-flow road-network travel time on the contracted dodgr graph.

This section caches a single OD frame keyed by `(origin_id, dest_id)` with
columns `(trips, involves_gateway, od_kind)`. AM-peak only (per the user
decision; per-TOD evaluation is a TODO).

## 6a. Load gateways and identify Seattle tracts

```{r daysim-gateways}
log_stage("Stage 6a: Gateways + Seattle tract membership")

stopifnot(file.exists(params$gateways_geojson))
gateways_sf <- sf::st_read(params$gateways_geojson, quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_transform(CRS_LL)

gateways <- tibble::tibble(
  id          = sprintf("GW_%04d", as.integer(gateways_sf$OBJECTID)),
  lon         = sf::st_coordinates(gateways_sf)[, 1],
  lat         = sf::st_coordinates(gateways_sf)[, 2],
  direction   = as.character(gateways_sf$Direction),
  label       = as.character(gateways_sf$Label),
  osm_id      = as.character(gateways_sf$OSM_ID)
)

inbound_gws  <- gateways |>
  filter(direction %in% c("Inbound", "Bidirectional"))
outbound_gws <- gateways |>
  filter(direction %in% c("Outbound", "Bidirectional"))

log_msg(sprintf("Gateways: %d total (%d inbound, %d outbound, %d bidir)",
                nrow(gateways),
                sum(gateways$direction == "Inbound"),
                sum(gateways$direction == "Outbound"),
                sum(gateways$direction == "Bidirectional")))

# All PSRC tract centroids needed for gateway assignment to non-Seattle
# tracts. Phase 1's tract_centroids cache covers HTS-touched tracts only;
# Daysim has many more, so we re-pull the full PSRC universe via tigris
# (this hits the tigris cache → fast on second run).
all_tracts_sf <- with_cache("tracts_psrc_all",
  list(state = "WA",
       counties = c("King", "Pierce", "Snohomish", "Kitsap"),
       year = 2020),
  function() {
    psrc_counties <- c("King", "Pierce", "Snohomish", "Kitsap")
    do.call(rbind, lapply(psrc_counties, function(cty)
      tigris::tracts(state = "WA", county = cty, year = 2020,
                     class = "sf"))) |>
      sf::st_make_valid() |>
      mutate(id = clean_geoid11(GEOID))
  })
log_msg(sprintf("Loaded %d PSRC tract polygons", nrow(all_tracts_sf)))

all_tract_centroids <- with_cache("tract_centroids_psrc",
  list(tracts_digest = digest::digest(all_tracts_sf$id),
       counties = c("King", "Pierce", "Snohomish", "Kitsap"), year = 2020,
       # v2: pop-weighted centroids across the full PSRC tract universe,
       # matching Phase1BuildMNL §3 (which used pop-weighted for the
       # HTS-touched Seattle subset). Phase 2 previously used plain
       # st_point_on_surface for Daysim-only tracts, creating a centroid
       # mismatch within the same pipeline (off by hundreds of meters in
       # dense tracts with water/parks pulling point-on-surface away).
       version = "v2"),
  function() {
    log_msg("Computing pop-weighted centroids for PSRC tracts (one-time)...")
    psrc_counties <- c("King", "Pierce", "Snohomish", "Kitsap")
    blocks_list <- lapply(psrc_counties, function(cty) {
      log_msg(sprintf("  loading blocks: %s", cty))
      b <- tigris::blocks(state = "WA", county = cty, year = 2020,
                          class = "sf") |>
        sf::st_make_valid()
      # tigris 2020 returns population in POP20; older versions may use
      # P0010001 or POP10. Pick whichever is present.
      pop_col <- intersect(c("POP20", "P0010001", "POP10"), names(b))[1]
      b$pop <- if (!is.na(pop_col)) as.numeric(b[[pop_col]]) else 0
      b$tract_geoid <- substr(b$GEOID20, 1, 11)
      b |> select(tract_geoid, pop)
    })
    blocks_sf <- do.call(rbind, blocks_list)
    log_msg(sprintf("  %d blocks total, %.0f population summed",
                    nrow(blocks_sf), sum(blocks_sf$pop, na.rm = TRUE)))

    # Pop-weighted average of block point-on-surface coordinates per tract
    # (matches Phase1BuildMNL §3 compute_pop_weighted_tract_points).
    blocks_planar <- sf::st_transform(blocks_sf, CRS_PLANAR)
    block_pts <- sf::st_point_on_surface(blocks_planar)
    xy <- sf::st_coordinates(block_pts)
    pop_weighted_pts <- blocks_planar |>
      mutate(X = xy[, 1], Y = xy[, 2],
             pop = coalesce(as.numeric(pop), 0)) |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
      group_by(tract_geoid) |>
      summarise(
        pop_sum = sum(pop, na.rm = TRUE),
        Xw = if_else(pop_sum > 0, sum(X * pop, na.rm = TRUE) / pop_sum,
                     mean(X, na.rm = TRUE)),
        Yw = if_else(pop_sum > 0, sum(Y * pop, na.rm = TRUE) / pop_sum,
                     mean(Y, na.rm = TRUE)),
        .groups = "drop")
    pts_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(pop_weighted_pts,
                           coords = c("Xw", "Yw"), crs = CRS_PLANAR) |>
      sf::st_transform(CRS_LL)
    out <- tibble(
      id  = pop_weighted_pts$tract_geoid,
      lon = sf::st_coordinates(pts_sf)[, 1],
      lat = sf::st_coordinates(pts_sf)[, 2])

    # Fallback to point-on-surface for tracts not covered by blocks
    # (rare — usually tracts with zero block population).
    missing <- setdiff(all_tracts_sf$id, out$id)
    if (length(missing) > 0) {
      log_msg(sprintf("  %d tracts have no blocks; using point-on-surface fallback",
                      length(missing)))
      fb <- all_tracts_sf |>
        filter(id %in% missing) |>
        sf::st_transform(CRS_PLANAR) |>
        sf::st_point_on_surface() |>
        sf::st_transform(CRS_LL) |>
        mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
               lat = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
        sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
        select(id, lat, lon)
      out <- bind_rows(out, fb)
    }
    log_msg(sprintf("  produced %d pop-weighted centroids", nrow(out)))
    out
  })

# Recompute Seattle membership across the full PSRC tract set (Phase 1 only
# stored the Seattle-only subset). Native pipe |> doesn't accept the `.`
# placeholder, so we keep the spatial test out of the pipe.
.all_tracts_ll <- st_transform(all_tracts_sf, CRS_LL)
.in_seattle_full <- lengths(st_intersects(.all_tracts_ll, seattle_sf)) > 0
seattle_tract_ids_full <- as.character(.all_tracts_ll$id[.in_seattle_full])
log_msg(sprintf("Seattle tracts: %d (subset of %d PSRC tracts)",
                length(seattle_tract_ids_full), nrow(all_tracts_sf)))
```

## 6b. Match external tracts to nearest gateway by free-flow network time

```{r daysim-gateway-match}
log_stage("Stage 6b: Network-time gateway assignment for external tracts")

ext_centroids <- all_tract_centroids |>
  filter(!(id %in% seattle_tract_ids_full))

verts <- dodgr::dodgr_vertices(dodgr_graph_annotated)

snap_to_vertex <- function(lon, lat) {
  ix <- dodgr::match_pts_to_verts(verts, data.frame(x = lon, y = lat))
  verts$id[ix]
}

gateway_match <- with_cache("gateway_match_v3",
  list(verts_sig = digest::digest(verts$id),
       gw_sig = digest::digest(gateways), version = "v3"),
  function() {
    ext_centroids$vertex <- snap_to_vertex(ext_centroids$lon,
                                           ext_centroids$lat)
    inbound_gws$vertex   <- snap_to_vertex(inbound_gws$lon,  inbound_gws$lat)
    outbound_gws$vertex  <- snap_to_vertex(outbound_gws$lon, outbound_gws$lat)

    log_msg("Computing free-flow times: external tracts → inbound gateways...")
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    t_in <- dodgr::dodgr_times(graph = dodgr_graph_annotated,
                               from = unique(ext_centroids$vertex),
                               to   = unique(inbound_gws$vertex))
    log_done("dodgr_times (inbound)", t0)

    log_msg("Computing free-flow times: outbound gateways → external tracts...")
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    t_out <- dodgr::dodgr_times(graph = dodgr_graph_annotated,
                                from = unique(outbound_gws$vertex),
                                to   = unique(ext_centroids$vertex))
    log_done("dodgr_times (outbound)", t0)

    inbound_by_vert  <- split(inbound_gws$id,  inbound_gws$vertex)
    outbound_by_vert <- split(outbound_gws$id, outbound_gws$vertex)

    pick_inbound <- function(v) {
      row_t <- t_in[v, ]
      if (all(!is.finite(row_t))) return(NA_character_)
      inbound_by_vert[[ names(row_t)[which.min(row_t)] ]][1]
    }
    pick_outbound <- function(v) {
      col_t <- t_out[, v]
      if (all(!is.finite(col_t))) return(NA_character_)
      outbound_by_vert[[ names(col_t)[which.min(col_t)] ]][1]
    }

    ext_centroids$gateway_inbound  <-
      vapply(ext_centroids$vertex, pick_inbound,  character(1))
    ext_centroids$gateway_outbound <-
      vapply(ext_centroids$vertex, pick_outbound, character(1))

    # Fallback: any tract whose snapped vertex couldn't network-reach a
    # gateway falls through to Euclidean nearest in lon/lat space. This
    # handles tracts in disconnected pockets of the motorcar graph (small
    # islands, remote dead-ends, ferry-only access). Without the fallback
    # we silently drop their Daysim trips → underloaded gateways.
    if (!requireNamespace("FNN", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("FNN")
    fallback_match <- function(unreached_idx, gw_table, label) {
      if (length(unreached_idx) == 0) return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(ext_centroids)))
      out <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(ext_centroids))
      nn <- FNN::get.knnx(
        data  = as.matrix(gw_table[, c("lon", "lat")]),
        query = as.matrix(ext_centroids[unreached_idx, c("lon", "lat")]),
        k = 1)
      out[unreached_idx] <- gw_table$id[nn$nn.index[, 1]]
      log_msg(sprintf("  %s fallback: %d tracts assigned by Euclidean nearest",
                      label, length(unreached_idx)))
      out
    }
    .miss_in  <- which(is.na(ext_centroids$gateway_inbound))
    .miss_out <- which(is.na(ext_centroids$gateway_outbound))
    fb_in  <- fallback_match(.miss_in,  inbound_gws,  "inbound")
    fb_out <- fallback_match(.miss_out, outbound_gws, "outbound")
    ext_centroids$gateway_inbound[.miss_in]   <- fb_in[.miss_in]
    ext_centroids$gateway_outbound[.miss_out] <- fb_out[.miss_out]

    list(
      ext_centroids = ext_centroids,
      gateways_v    = list(
        inbound  = inbound_gws  |> mutate(vertex = vertex),
        outbound = outbound_gws |> mutate(vertex = vertex)),
      n_network_in  = nrow(ext_centroids) - length(.miss_in),
      n_fallback_in = length(.miss_in),
      n_network_out = nrow(ext_centroids) - length(.miss_out),
      n_fallback_out = length(.miss_out)
    )
  })

ext_centroids <- gateway_match$ext_centroids
inbound_gws   <- gateway_match$gateways_v$inbound
outbound_gws  <- gateway_match$gateways_v$outbound

log_msg(sprintf("External tracts: %d total", nrow(ext_centroids)))
log_msg(sprintf("  inbound:  %d via network time, %d via Euclidean fallback (%.1f%%)",
                gateway_match$n_network_in, gateway_match$n_fallback_in,
                100 * gateway_match$n_fallback_in / nrow(ext_centroids)))
log_msg(sprintf("  outbound: %d via network time, %d via Euclidean fallback (%.1f%%)",
                gateway_match$n_network_out, gateway_match$n_fallback_out,
                100 * gateway_match$n_fallback_out / nrow(ext_centroids)))
.still_na_in  <- sum(is.na(ext_centroids$gateway_inbound))
.still_na_out <- sum(is.na(ext_centroids$gateway_outbound))
if (.still_na_in + .still_na_out > 0)
  log_msg(sprintf("  WARNING: still NA after fallback — in=%d, out=%d",
                  .still_na_in, .still_na_out))

tract_gateway <- ext_centroids |>
  select(id, gateway_inbound, gateway_outbound)
```

## 6c. Pull Daysim trips per TOD and aggregate to OD

```{r daysim-trips-load}
log_stage(sprintf("Stage 6c: Daysim trip table → cordon-snapped OD (TODs: %s)",
                  paste(params$tods_to_run, collapse = ", ")))

stopifnot(file.exists(params$daysim_trips_tsv))
stopifnot(file.exists(params$daysim_parcel_map))

# Convert a TOD bin (hours-of-day pair) into the DEPTM filter range
# expected by the Daysim trip table. `bounds` is a length-2 numeric;
# bounds[1] is the start hour (inclusive), bounds[2] is the end hour
# (exclusive). Night wraps midnight when bounds[2] <= bounds[1].
tod_deptm_range <- function(bounds, fmt = params$deptm_format) {
  hr_start <- as.numeric(bounds[1])
  hr_end   <- as.numeric(bounds[2])
  to_dep <- function(h) {
    if (fmt == "hhmm")                       h * 100
    else if (fmt == "minutes_after_midnight") h * 60
    else if (fmt == "minutes_after_3am")      (h - 3) * 60
    else stop("Unknown deptm_format: ", fmt)
  }
  list(dep_lo = to_dep(hr_start), dep_hi = to_dep(hr_end),
       wraps  = hr_end <= hr_start)
}

build_od_full <- function(tod_name = "AM",
                           tod_bounds = params$tod_bounds[[tod_name]]) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(DBI); library(duckdb)
  })
  con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")
  on.exit(dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA threads=4;")

  # ---- Parcel map ----
  parcel_map <- fread(params$daysim_parcel_map) |>
    mutate(
      ParcelID = as.character(ParcelID),
      !!params$daysim_tract_col := as.character(.data[[params$daysim_tract_col]]),
      !!params$daysim_city_col  := as.character(.data[[params$daysim_city_col]])
    )
  dbWriteTable(con, "parcel_map", parcel_map, overwrite = TRUE)
  dbExecute(con, "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pm_parcel ON parcel_map(ParcelID);")

  trips_rel <- sprintf(
    "read_csv_auto('%s', delim='\\t', header=true, quote='\"', escape='\"')",
    normalizePath(params$daysim_trips_tsv, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  )

  # ---- TOD filter on DEPTM ----
  r <- tod_deptm_range(tod_bounds)
  dep_lo <- r$dep_lo; dep_hi <- r$dep_hi
  fmt    <- params$deptm_format
  if (r$wraps) {
    # Night wraps midnight: pull trips with deptm >= bounds[1] OR < bounds[2]
    deptm_clause <- sprintf(
      "(t.deptm >= %f OR t.deptm < %f)", dep_lo, dep_hi)
    log_msg(sprintf("%s DEPTM filter: deptm >= %g OR deptm < %g (wraps midnight)",
                    tod_name, dep_lo, dep_hi))
  } else {
    deptm_clause <- sprintf(
      "(t.deptm >= %f AND t.deptm < %f)", dep_lo, dep_hi)
    log_msg(sprintf("%s DEPTM filter: [%g, %g) under '%s'",
                    tod_name, dep_lo, dep_hi, fmt))
  }

  # ---- Pull trips ----
  # MODE 8 = school bus, excluded. Other diagnostics (TRAVTIME, MODE) kept
  # for sanity-checking the OD table downstream.
  # `deptm_clause` (built above) handles Night-wraps-midnight TODs: it's
  # `deptm >= lo OR deptm < hi` for wrapping bins and `deptm >= lo AND
  # deptm < hi` for non-wrapping bins.
  sql <- sprintf("
    WITH t AS (
      SELECT
        CAST(TRY_CAST(OPCL AS HUGEINT) AS VARCHAR) AS opcl_v,
        CAST(TRY_CAST(DPCL AS HUGEINT) AS VARCHAR) AS dpcl_v,
        TRY_CAST(TREXPFAC AS DOUBLE)               AS w,
        TRY_CAST(DEPTM    AS DOUBLE)               AS deptm,
        TRY_CAST(MODE     AS INTEGER)              AS mode_code
      FROM %s
    )
    SELECT
      LPAD(o.%s, 11, '0') AS origin_tract,
      LPAD(d.%s, 11, '0') AS dest_tract,
      lower(trim(o.%s))   AS o_city,
      lower(trim(d.%s))   AS d_city,
      COALESCE(t.w, 0.0)  AS w,
      t.mode_code
    FROM t
    JOIN parcel_map o ON t.opcl_v = o.ParcelID
    JOIN parcel_map d ON t.dpcl_v = d.ParcelID
    WHERE t.deptm IS NOT NULL
      AND %s
      AND COALESCE(t.mode_code, 0) <> 8
    ", trips_rel,
       params$daysim_tract_col, params$daysim_tract_col,
       params$daysim_city_col,  params$daysim_city_col,
       deptm_clause)
  raw <- dbGetQuery(con, sql)
  log_msg(sprintf("%s Daysim records: %d (weighted person-trips: %.0f)",
                  tod_name, nrow(raw), sum(raw$w, na.rm = TRUE)))

  # ---- Cordon snap: non-Seattle ends → assigned gateway ----
  gw_in_lookup  <- setNames(tract_gateway$gateway_inbound,  tract_gateway$id)
  gw_out_lookup <- setNames(tract_gateway$gateway_outbound, tract_gateway$id)

  # PSRC Daysim MODE codes:
  #   1 walk; 2 bike; 3 SOV; 4 HOV2; 5 HOV3+; 6 transit (walk access);
  #   7 transit (drive access); 8 school bus (already filtered out).
  # Drive = {3,4,5}; transit = {6,7}; walk = 1; bike = 2.
  od <- raw |>
    mutate(
      o_in_seattle = origin_tract %in% seattle_tract_ids_full,
      d_in_seattle = dest_tract   %in% seattle_tract_ids_full,
      origin_id_remap = ifelse(o_in_seattle, origin_tract,
                               unname(gw_in_lookup[origin_tract])),
      dest_id_remap   = ifelse(d_in_seattle, dest_tract,
                               unname(gw_out_lookup[dest_tract]))
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(origin_id_remap), !is.na(dest_id_remap)) |>
    filter(origin_id_remap != dest_id_remap) |>
    # Drop pure GW→GW pass-through (mostly I-405 etc., not Seattle traffic;
    # any real freeway pass-through volume is captured by SDOT seeding).
    filter(!(startsWith(origin_id_remap, "GW_") &
             startsWith(dest_id_remap,   "GW_"))) |>
    group_by(origin_id_remap, dest_id_remap) |>
    summarise(
      trips      = sum(w, na.rm = TRUE),
      w_drive    = sum(w * (mode_code %in% c(3L, 4L, 5L)), na.rm = TRUE),
      w_transit  = sum(w * (mode_code %in% c(6L, 7L)),     na.rm = TRUE),
      w_walk     = sum(w * (mode_code == 1L),              na.rm = TRUE),
      w_bike     = sum(w * (mode_code == 2L),              na.rm = TRUE),
      n_records  = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      origin_id = origin_id_remap,
      dest_id   = dest_id_remap,
      trips     = as.numeric(trips),
      o_is_gw   = startsWith(origin_id, "GW_"),
      d_is_gw   = startsWith(dest_id,   "GW_"),
      involves_gateway = o_is_gw | d_is_gw,
      od_kind = case_when(
        !o_is_gw & !d_is_gw ~ "internal_internal",
        TRUE                ~ "cordon"),
      # Per-OD Daysim mode shares (used as the empirical fallback for
      # ODs that aren't covered by the HTS-MNL prediction). For ODs with
      # zero trips after filtering, denominator is clamped at 1e-9 — but
      # this can't actually fire because we're inside summarise() of trips.
      p_drive_dsm   = w_drive   / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
      p_transit_dsm = w_transit / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
      p_walk_dsm    = w_walk    / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
      p_bike_dsm    = w_bike    / pmax(trips, 1e-9)
    ) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, trips, n_records,
           w_drive, w_transit, w_walk, w_bike,
           p_drive_dsm, p_transit_dsm, p_walk_dsm, p_bike_dsm,
           involves_gateway, od_kind)

  total <- sum(od$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
  log_msg(sprintf("Aggregated %s OD: %d pairs, %.0f weighted person-trips",
                  tod_name, nrow(od), total))

  # Trip-weighted aggregate Daysim mode shares per OD-kind. These should
  # replace the previous fixed-0.95 cordon assumption and HTS-MNL global
  # interior fallback — both were guesses at what the data already says.
  agg <- od |>
    group_by(od_kind) |>
    summarise(
      trips_w   = sum(trips),
      p_drive   = sum(w_drive)   / sum(trips),
      p_transit = sum(w_transit) / sum(trips),
      p_walk    = sum(w_walk)    / sum(trips),
      p_bike    = sum(w_bike)    / sum(trips),
      .groups = "drop")
  log_msg(sprintf("[%s] Daysim aggregate mode share by OD-kind (trip-weighted):",
                  tod_name))
  print(agg)

  for (k in c("internal_internal", "cordon")) {
    sel <- od$od_kind == k
    log_sub(sprintf("%-18s pairs: %6d  (%.1f%% of weighted trips)",
                    k, sum(sel), 100 * sum(od$trips[sel]) / total))
  }
  od
}

# ---- Build per-TOD od_daysim list -------------------------------------
# One entry per TOD selected in `params$tods_to_run`. Cache key includes
# the TOD name and its bounds so changing `tods_to_run` doesn't invalidate
# caches for already-built TODs.
log_msg(sprintf("Building Daysim OD tables for %d TOD(s): %s",
                length(params$tods_to_run),
                paste(params$tods_to_run, collapse = ", ")))

od_daysim_per_tod <- lapply(params$tods_to_run, function(tod_name) {
  bounds <- params$tod_bounds[[tod_name]]
  if (is.null(bounds)) stop("No tod_bounds defined for TOD '", tod_name, "'")
  with_cache(sprintf("od_daysim_%s", tolower(tod_name)),
    list(tsv     = file_signature(params$daysim_trips_tsv),
         parcels = file_signature(params$daysim_parcel_map),
         gws     = digest::digest(tract_gateway),
         fmt     = params$deptm_format,
         tod     = tod_name,
         bounds  = as.numeric(bounds),
         # v3: per-TOD build (was v2 AM-only).
         version = "v3"),
    function() build_od_full(tod_name = tod_name, tod_bounds = bounds))
})
names(od_daysim_per_tod) <- params$tods_to_run

# Back-compat alias. `od_daysim` (singular) is still used by §7 to define
# the routing universe and by some §15 weights — it should be the *union*
# across all modeled TODs (unique OD pairs, but per-TOD trip counts merged
# additively for any callers that consume trip totals). Callers that need
# TOD-specific trips should index into `od_daysim_per_tod[[tod]]`.
od_daysim <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(od_daysim_per_tod), function(tn)
    od_daysim_per_tod[[tn]] |> mutate(tod = tn))) |>
  group_by(origin_id, dest_id) |>
  summarise(
    # Trip totals — sum across modeled TODs (so accessibility/weight uses
    # all modeled trips). The p_*_dsm fields are trip-weighted means.
    trips         = sum(trips, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_records     = sum(n_records, na.rm = TRUE),
    w_drive       = sum(w_drive, na.rm = TRUE),
    w_transit     = sum(w_transit, na.rm = TRUE),
    w_walk        = sum(w_walk, na.rm = TRUE),
    w_bike        = sum(w_bike, na.rm = TRUE),
    involves_gateway = any(involves_gateway),
    od_kind       = od_kind[1],
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    p_drive_dsm   = w_drive   / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
    p_transit_dsm = w_transit / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
    p_walk_dsm    = w_walk    / pmax(trips, 1e-9),
    p_bike_dsm    = w_bike    / pmax(trips, 1e-9))
log_msg(sprintf("od_daysim (union across %d TOD): %d unique OD pairs",
                length(od_daysim_per_tod), nrow(od_daysim)))
```


# 7. Build the drive skim (Phase 2 routing — no Phase 1 dependency)

Phase 2 routes the full OD universe — both HTS Seattle-internal pairs
*and* Daysim AM-peak pairs — on its own dodgr graph (the one built
in §2 above, which excludes `service` highways). This replaces what
used to be a "expand Phase 1's skim_drive" step; Phase 1's drive skim
is no longer consulted.

Steps:
1. Build a points table that unions every tract/gateway needed by HTS
   trips and Daysim OD volume.
2. FNN K-NN snap each tract centroid to dodgr vertices (K=10 stored);
   gateways snap via their exact OSM_ID match.
3. Route every (origin, dest) pair in the union universe with (1,1)
   one-shot, then retry the (1,n) and (n,1) K-NN tiers for any pair
   that came back NA. No radial fallback (intentional restriction).

Output `skim_drive_full` has one row per OD with: `origin_id`,
`dest_id`, `drive_tt_raw` (minutes), `drive_dist_mi`, `o_vertex`,
`d_vertex`, `snap_k`, `drive_source = "dodgr"` (every OD is dodgr-
routed; no r5r fallback). Pairs that fail all K-NN tiers have NA
times and are dropped from flow loading.

```{r expand-drive-skim}
log_stage("Stage 7: Build drive skim (HTS + Daysim universe)")

build_expanded_skim_drive <- function() {
  # ---- Points table: union of every tract/gateway HTS + Daysim need ----
  hts_ods <- trips_aux |>
    filter(origin_id %in% seattle_tract_ids,
           dest_id   %in% seattle_tract_ids) |>
    semi_join(distinct(choice_long, trip_id), by = "trip_id") |>
    distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
  daysim_ods <- od_daysim |> distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
  all_ods <- bind_rows(hts_ods, daysim_ods) |>
    distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
  log_msg(sprintf("OD routing universe: %d unique pairs (HTS: %d, Daysim: %d, union: %d)",
                  nrow(all_ods), nrow(hts_ods), nrow(daysim_ods), nrow(all_ods)))

  all_ids <- unique(c(all_ods$origin_id, all_ods$dest_id))
  all_tract_only <- all_ids[!startsWith(all_ids, "GW_")]
  all_gw_only    <- all_ids[ startsWith(all_ids, "GW_")]

  pts_tract <- all_tract_centroids |>
    filter(id %in% all_tract_only)
  pts_gw <- gateways |>
    filter(id %in% all_gw_only) |>
    select(id, lat, lon, osm_id)
  pts_xy <- bind_rows(
    pts_tract |> mutate(osm_id = NA_character_),
    pts_gw)
  log_msg(sprintf("Points to snap: %d (tract: %d, gateway: %d)",
                  nrow(pts_xy), nrow(pts_tract), nrow(pts_gw)))

  # ---- K-NN k=10 for tracts (matches Phase 1 §6 line 1304). The k=1
  # vertex is kept for the fast one-shot routing pass; k=2..10 are
  # held in `knn_vert_id_all` for the retry loop below to recover
  # ODs that fail with the k=1 pair.
  is_gw <- startsWith(pts_xy$id, "GW_")
  pts_xy$vertex     <- NA_character_
  pts_xy$match_dist <- NA_real_
  K_MAX <- 10L
  knn_vert_id_all <- NULL  # populated below for non-gateway tracts

  if (any(!is_gw)) {
    nn_t <- FNN::get.knnx(
      data  = as.matrix(verts[, c("x", "y")]),
      query = as.matrix(pts_xy[!is_gw, c("lon", "lat")]),
      k = K_MAX)
    pts_xy$vertex[!is_gw]     <- verts$id[nn_t$nn.index[, 1]]
    pts_xy$match_dist[!is_gw] <- nn_t$nn.dist[, 1]
    # Build full K-NN vertex matrix indexed by tract id
    knn_vert_id_all <- matrix(verts$id[as.vector(nn_t$nn.index)],
                              nrow = nrow(nn_t$nn.index))
    rownames(knn_vert_id_all) <- pts_xy$id[!is_gw]
  }

  if (any(is_gw)) {
    graph_way_ids <- dgr_way_id(dodgr_graph_annotated)
    if (is.null(graph_way_ids)) {
      log_msg("WARNING: graph carries no way_id column; all gateways will use FNN fallback.")
    }
    for (i in which(is_gw)) {
      gw_osm <- pts_xy$osm_id[i]
      if (is.na(gw_osm) || gw_osm == "" || is.null(graph_way_ids)) next
      on_way <- which(graph_way_ids == as.character(gw_osm))
      if (length(on_way) == 0) next
      way_vert_ids <- unique(c(dgr_from_id(dodgr_graph_annotated)[on_way],
                               dgr_to_id(dodgr_graph_annotated)[on_way]))
      way_v <- verts[verts$id %in% way_vert_ids, , drop = FALSE]
      d2 <- (way_v$x - pts_xy$lon[i])^2 + (way_v$y - pts_xy$lat[i])^2
      best <- which.min(d2)
      pts_xy$vertex[i]     <- way_v$id[best]
      pts_xy$match_dist[i] <- sqrt(d2[best])
    }
    # FNN fallback for gateways without OSM_ID match
    unset <- is_gw & is.na(pts_xy$vertex)
    if (any(unset)) {
      nn_g <- FNN::get.knnx(
        data  = as.matrix(verts[, c("x", "y")]),
        query = as.matrix(pts_xy[unset, c("lon", "lat")]),
        k = 1)
      pts_xy$vertex[unset]     <- verts$id[nn_g$nn.index[, 1]]
      pts_xy$match_dist[unset] <- nn_g$nn.dist[, 1]
    }
  }
  log_msg(sprintf("Snapped: %d points; median match_dist = %.4f deg (~%.0f m)",
                  sum(!is.na(pts_xy$vertex)),
                  median(pts_xy$match_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
                  median(pts_xy$match_dist, na.rm = TRUE) * 111000))

  # ---- Snap every OD in the routing universe ----
  od_new <- all_ods |>
    inner_join(pts_xy |> select(id, o_vertex = vertex),
               by = c("origin_id" = "id")) |>
    inner_join(pts_xy |> select(id, d_vertex = vertex),
               by = c("dest_id" = "id")) |>
    filter(!is.na(o_vertex), !is.na(d_vertex), o_vertex != d_vertex) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, o_vertex, d_vertex)
  log_msg(sprintf("ODs to route: %d (after vertex snap)", nrow(od_new)))

  # ---- Route new ODs in one pass ----
  if (nrow(od_new) > 0) {
    log_msg("Routing dodgr_pairwise on new ODs (one-shot)...")
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    tt_sec <- route_pairwise_times(dodgr_graph_annotated,
                                   from = od_new$o_vertex,
                                   to   = od_new$d_vertex,
                                   shortest = FALSE)
    dist_m <- route_pairwise_dists(dodgr_graph_annotated,
                                   from = od_new$o_vertex,
                                   to   = od_new$d_vertex,
                                   shortest = FALSE)
    log_done("dodgr_times + dists (pairwise)", t0)

    od_new <- od_new |>
      mutate(
        drive_tt_raw  = as.numeric(tt_sec) / 60,
        drive_dist_mi = as.numeric(dist_m) / 1609.344,
        drive_source  = "dodgr",
        snap_k        = 11L)   # k1=1, k2=1
    n1 <- sum(is.finite(od_new$drive_tt_raw))
    log_msg(sprintf("  k=(1,1) routed: %d/%d (%.1f%%); median tt = %.1f min",
                    n1, nrow(od_new), 100 * n1 / nrow(od_new),
                    median(od_new$drive_tt_raw, na.rm = TRUE)))

    # ---- K-NN retry loop for unrouted pairs (matches Phase 1 §6 lines
    # 1338-1390). For each (k1, k2) tier ordered by k1+k2, route the
    # still-unrouted pairs with their k1-th nearest origin vertex and
    # k2-th nearest dest vertex. Only tract-tract or tract-gw routes
    # retry — pure GW endpoints don't have alternative k vertices.
    knn_vertex <- function(tract_ids, k) {
      if (is.null(knn_vert_id_all)) return(rep(NA_character_, length(tract_ids)))
      idx <- match(tract_ids, rownames(knn_vert_id_all))
      out <- rep(NA_character_, length(tract_ids))
      ok <- !is.na(idx)
      if (any(ok)) out[ok] <- knn_vert_id_all[cbind(idx[ok], k)]
      out
    }
    # Snapshot the OSM_ID-snapped gateway vertices (don't retry these).
    pts_xy_gw_lookup <- setNames(pts_xy$vertex[is_gw], pts_xy$id[is_gw])
    get_vert_at_k <- function(ids, k) {
      out <- knn_vertex(ids, k)
      gw_match <- match(ids, names(pts_xy_gw_lookup))
      ok_gw <- !is.na(gw_match)
      if (any(ok_gw)) out[ok_gw] <- pts_xy_gw_lookup[gw_match[ok_gw]]
      out
    }
    # Intentional restriction: only (k1=1, k2=2..10) and (k2=1, k1=2..10).
    # The Phase 1 audit showed essentially all snap recoveries land on
    # (1,n) or (n,1) tiers; (n,n) for both n>1 adds combinatorial work for
    # marginal recovery. No radial fallback either — same reason.
    rounds <- tibble(
      k1 = c(rep(1L, K_MAX - 1), 2:K_MAX),
      k2 = c(2:K_MAX,            rep(1L, K_MAX - 1))
    ) |>
      arrange(k1 + k2, k1, k2)
    log_msg(sprintf("  K-NN retry: %d (k1,k2) tiers for unrouted pairs",
                    nrow(rounds)))
    n_recovered_knn <- 0L
    for (r in seq_len(nrow(rounds))) {
      still_na <- !is.finite(od_new$drive_tt_raw) | od_new$drive_tt_raw <= 0
      if (!any(still_na)) break
      k1 <- rounds$k1[r]; k2 <- rounds$k2[r]
      sub_idx <- which(still_na)
      o_v <- get_vert_at_k(od_new$origin_id[sub_idx], k1)
      d_v <- get_vert_at_k(od_new$dest_id[sub_idx],   k2)
      ok_input <- !is.na(o_v) & !is.na(d_v) & o_v != d_v
      if (!any(ok_input)) next
      sub_idx <- sub_idx[ok_input]
      o_v <- o_v[ok_input]; d_v <- d_v[ok_input]
      tt_sec2 <- tryCatch(
        route_pairwise_times(dodgr_graph_annotated, from = o_v, to = d_v,
                             shortest = FALSE),
        error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, length(o_v)))
      dd_m2 <- tryCatch(
        route_pairwise_dists(dodgr_graph_annotated, from = o_v, to = d_v,
                             shortest = FALSE),
        error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, length(o_v)))
      ok_r <- is.finite(tt_sec2) & tt_sec2 > 0 &
              is.finite(dd_m2)   & dd_m2 > 0
      if (any(ok_r)) {
        recovered_idx <- sub_idx[ok_r]
        od_new$drive_tt_raw[recovered_idx]  <- as.numeric(tt_sec2[ok_r]) / 60
        od_new$drive_dist_mi[recovered_idx] <- as.numeric(dd_m2[ok_r]) / 1609.344
        od_new$o_vertex[recovered_idx]      <- o_v[ok_r]
        od_new$d_vertex[recovered_idx]      <- d_v[ok_r]
        od_new$snap_k[recovered_idx]        <- k1 * 10L + k2
        n_recovered_knn <- n_recovered_knn + sum(ok_r)
      }
    }
    log_msg(sprintf("  K-NN retry recovered: %d ODs (snap_k distribution: %s)",
                    n_recovered_knn,
                    paste(sort(unique(od_new$snap_k[od_new$snap_k > 11])),
                          collapse = ", ")))

    # NOTE: Phase 1's radial fallback (1.5 km / 25-vertex matrix search)
    # is intentionally OMITTED here. The (1,n) and (n,1) K-NN tiers
    # already recover the vast majority of would-be radial recoveries
    # in Phase 1's data; the marginal recoveries from radial don't
    # justify the per-OD matrix-routing cost. ODs still unrouted after
    # K-NN remain NA and are dropped from flow loading.

    n_final <- sum(is.finite(od_new$drive_tt_raw))
    log_msg(sprintf("  FINAL routed (Daysim-new): %d/%d (%.1f%%)",
                    n_final, nrow(od_new),
                    100 * n_final / pmax(nrow(od_new), 1)))
  } else {
    od_new <- od_new |>
      mutate(drive_tt_raw = numeric(0),
             drive_dist_mi = numeric(0),
             drive_source = character(0),
             snap_k = integer(0))
  }

  # No Phase 1 stitch — Phase 2 routes everything fresh.
  list(skim = od_new, pts_xy = pts_xy)
}

skim_drive_expanded <- with_cache("skim_drive_p2",
  list(od_sig   = digest::digest(od_daysim),
       hts_sig  = digest::digest(distinct(
                   trips_aux |> filter(origin_id %in% seattle_tract_ids,
                                       dest_id   %in% seattle_tract_ids),
                   origin_id, dest_id)),
       graph_sig = digest::digest(dgr_edge_id(dodgr_graph_annotated)),
       # p2_v1: Phase 2 routes the full HTS ∪ Daysim OD universe on its
       # own dodgr graph (no Phase 1 dependency). (1,n) and (n,1) K-NN
       # snap, no radial fallback. `service` highways excluded from the
       # graph upstream.
       version = "p2_v1"),
  build_expanded_skim_drive)

skim_drive_full <- skim_drive_expanded$skim
pts_xy <- skim_drive_expanded$pts_xy

log_msg(sprintf("skim_drive_full: %d ODs routed on Phase 2's graph",
                nrow(skim_drive_full)))

# Phase 2 only manipulates dodgr-routed pairs. Everything else (r5r-fallback
# legacy HTS ODs, plus any unroutable Daysim ODs) keeps its baseline drive_tt.
skim_drive_dodgr <- skim_drive_full |>
  filter(drive_source == "dodgr",
         !is.na(o_vertex), !is.na(d_vertex), o_vertex != d_vertex,
         is.finite(drive_tt_raw))
log_msg(sprintf("Dodgr-routable ODs (will iterate per scenario): %d",
                nrow(skim_drive_dodgr)))
```


# 8. Per-config R5R networks (cached)

For each unique GTFS combo, we set up a routing dir containing the OSM PBF
and the right scenario zips plus all unchanged-agency zips, then call
`r5r::build_network`. The directory itself is the cache: r5r writes
`network.dat` next to the inputs, and we hash the input set.

```{r build-r5r-fn}
# Cached r5r builder. Returns the r5r_network handle.
build_r5r_for_config <- function(gtfs_paths, label,
                                 unchanged_paths = gtfs_unchanged_paths) {
  combo_sig <- digest::digest(list(
    gtfs_scen = lapply(sort(gtfs_paths), file_signature),
    gtfs_unc  = lapply(sort(unchanged_paths), file_signature),
    pbf       = file_signature(PBF_PATH),
    version   = "v1"
  ), algo = "sha1")
  r5r_dir <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, "r5r", paste0(label, "_", substr(combo_sig, 1, 12)))
  network_dat <- file.path(r5r_dir, "network.dat")

  if (file.exists(network_dat) && !params$force_rebuild) {
    log_msg(sprintf("R5R cache HIT  for %s [%s] → %s", label,
                    substr(combo_sig, 1, 8), basename(r5r_dir)))
  } else {
    if (file.exists(r5r_dir)) unlink(r5r_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    dir.create(r5r_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    # Hardlink (fast) where possible; fall back to copy.
    file_link <- function(from, to) {
      ok <- tryCatch(file.link(from, to), error = function(e) FALSE,
                     warning = function(w) FALSE)
      if (isTRUE(ok)) return(invisible(TRUE))
      file.copy(from, to, overwrite = TRUE)
    }
    file_link(PBF_PATH, file.path(r5r_dir, basename(PBF_PATH)))
    for (p in c(gtfs_paths, unchanged_paths)) {
      file_link(p, file.path(r5r_dir, basename(p)))
    }
    log_msg(sprintf("R5R cache MISS for %s [%s] -- building (%d GTFS files)",
                    label, substr(combo_sig, 1, 8),
                    length(gtfs_paths) + length(unchanged_paths)))
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    r5r::build_network(data_path = r5r_dir,
                       verbose = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
    log_done(sprintf("built r5r network for %s", label), t0)
  }
  list(dir = r5r_dir, sig = combo_sig)
}
```

```{r build-all-r5r}
log_stage("Stage 8: Build R5R networks for all unique GTFS combos")

# Unique GTFS combos across all active configs, ALWAYS including the baseline
# no_pri_no_av reference combo. Two shared steps depend on it even when
# `configs_filter` narrows the scenario set:
#   • §9b walk/bike skims reuse the baseline combo's r5r network;
#   • §13b's unseeded-baseline equilibrium (which produces the flow-seed
#     calibration applied to EVERY scenario) needs the baseline transit skim,
#     and its cache key hashes that skim object — so if it's absent the key
#     hashes digest(NULL), forcing a rebuild that then fails.
# The baseline r5r network + skim are disk-cache HITs from prior full runs
# (their cache keys don't depend on which configs are selected), so this adds
# no compute — it just repopulates the in-memory r5r_index / transit_skims.
base_ref_combo <- config_table |>
  filter(transit_id == "baseline", street_id == "no_pri_no_av")
unique_combos <- bind_rows(configs_to_run, base_ref_combo) |>
  distinct(gtfs_combo, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(combo_label = transit_id) |>
  select(combo_label, gtfs_combo, gtfs_paths)

log_msg(sprintf("%d unique transit-network builds needed", nrow(unique_combos)))

r5r_index <- setNames(vector("list", nrow(unique_combos)),
                      vapply(seq_len(nrow(unique_combos)),
                             function(i) digest::digest(
                               unique_combos$gtfs_combo[i]),
                             character(1)))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(unique_combos))) {
  row <- unique_combos[i, ]
  paths <- row$gtfs_paths[[1]]
  if (length(paths) == 0) next
  res <- build_r5r_for_config(paths, label = row$combo_label)
  r5r_index[[digest::digest(row$gtfs_combo)]] <- res
}

# We do NOT keep multiple r5r networks alive simultaneously — Java heap
# would explode. Each scenario opens its own and stops it.
r5r_dir_for_combo <- function(combo_str) {
  r5r_index[[digest::digest(combo_str)]]$dir
}
```


# 9. Per-config transit skims (cached)

For each unique GTFS combo, compute transit travel-time skims for every
intra-Seattle OD pair and every TOD bin. The skim is the same shape as
Phase 1's `skim_transit` — `transit_walk_raw / transit_wait_raw /
transit_ivtt_raw / transit_total_raw` per OD per (dow_type, tod_bin).

```{r transit-skim-fn}
# Constants ALIGNED with Phase1BuildMNL.Rmd (Phase 1) so per-config
# transit skims produce the same transit_total/walk/wait/ivtt values the
# MNL was estimated on. Prior values (5/30/3/60) drifted from Phase 1 and
# created systematic differences in transit utility that the MNL couldn't
# anticipate. See audit-Phase1-vs-Phase2 section 5 for the chase.
TRANSIT_TIME_WINDOW       <- 20L     # routing time window in minutes
TRANSIT_WINDOW_PRE        <- 10L     # depart this many min before rep_hour
TRANSIT_ROUTING_WALK_MIN  <- 45L
TRANSIT_ROUTING_TOTAL_MIN <- 180L
MAX_TRANSIT_RIDES         <- 4L
TRANSIT_ORIGIN_CHUNK      <- 200L

ettm_safe <- function(...) {
  args <- list(...)
  fmls <- names(formals(r5r::expanded_travel_time_matrix))
  args <- args[names(args) %in% fmls]
  do.call(r5r::expanded_travel_time_matrix, args)
}
# r5r column names changed between major versions:
#   r5r <= 1.x: total_time, access_time, wait_time, ride_time, ...
#   r5r >= 2.x: same names but optionally `_p50` suffix when percentiles
#               are tracked. Normalize back to the unsuffixed names so
#               the downstream data.table aggregation can stay the same.
.r5r_norm_cols <- function(dt) {
  if (!data.table::is.data.table(dt)) dt <- data.table::as.data.table(dt)
  cols <- names(dt)
  rename_if_present <- function(old_name, new_name) {
    if (new_name %in% names(dt) && !(old_name %in% names(dt)))
      data.table::setnames(dt, new_name, old_name)
  }
  rename_if_present("total_time",    "total_time_p50")
  rename_if_present("access_time",   "access_time_p50")
  rename_if_present("wait_time",     "wait_time_p50")
  rename_if_present("ride_time",     "ride_time_p50")
  rename_if_present("transfer_time", "transfer_time_p50")
  rename_if_present("egress_time",   "egress_time_p50")
  dt
}
safe_median <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE))
}

# OD universe = (origin, dest, dow_type, tod_bin) bins from trips_aux,
# restricted to Seattle.
trips_seattle <- trips_aux |>
  filter(origin_id %in% seattle_tract_ids,
         dest_id   %in% seattle_tract_ids)

# Data-driven rep_hour, matching Phase1BuildMNL §10. Phase 1 took
# the median of observed depart_hour per (dow_type, tod_bin); we do the
# same here so the per-config transit skim Phase 2 builds produces the
# same time-of-day samples the MNL was estimated on. Departure date is
# the first observed date in the bin (also matching Phase 1).
transit_bin_universe <- trips_seattle |>
  filter(is.finite(depart_hour)) |>
  group_by(dow_type, tod_bin) |>
  summarise(
    rep_hour    = as.integer(round(median(depart_hour, na.rm = TRUE))),
    depart_date = suppressWarnings(min(depart_date, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_trips     = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    # Fallback to a sensible date if min returned Inf (no valid dates)
    depart_date = if_else(is.finite(depart_date),
                          depart_date,
                          BASE_MONDAY +
                            ifelse(dow_type == "Weekend", 5L, 0L)),
    rep_datetime = as.POSIXct(
      paste0(depart_date, " ", sprintf("%02d:00:00", rep_hour)),
      tz = "America/Los_Angeles"))
log_msg("Transit-skim rep hours by bin (data-driven median, Phase-1-matched):")
print(transit_bin_universe |>
        select(dow_type, tod_bin, rep_hour, depart_date, n_trips))

build_transit_skim <- function(r5r_network, label, od_pairs,
                               points_use, bins) {
  log_msg(sprintf("[%s] building transit skim (%d OD pairs × %d bins)",
                  label, nrow(od_pairs), nrow(bins)))
  # Outer progress: per-bin × chunk
  total_chunks <- sum(pmax(1L, ceiling(
    sapply(seq_len(nrow(bins)), function(i) {
      n_o <- od_pairs |>
        semi_join(bins[i, ], by = c("dow_type", "tod_bin")) |>
        distinct(origin_id) |> nrow()
      n_o
    }) / TRANSIT_ORIGIN_CHUNK)))
  pb <- progress::progress_bar$new(
    format = "  [:bar] :percent | :elapsed elapsed | eta :eta | :msg",
    total = pmax(1L, total_chunks), clear = FALSE, width = 90)

  out_list <- vector("list", nrow(bins))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(bins))) {
    b <- bins[i, ]
    od_bin <- od_pairs |>
      semi_join(b, by = c("dow_type", "tod_bin")) |>
      distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
    if (nrow(od_bin) == 0) next
    o_ids <- sort(unique(od_bin$origin_id))
    chunks <- split(o_ids, ceiling(seq_along(o_ids) / TRANSIT_ORIGIN_CHUNK))
    dep_dt <- b$rep_datetime - TRANSIT_WINDOW_PRE * 60

    bin_out <- vector("list", length(chunks))
    for (k in seq_along(chunks)) {
      oc <- chunks[[k]]
      od_sub <- od_bin |> filter(origin_id %in% oc)
      o_pts  <- points_use |> filter(id %in% unique(od_sub$origin_id))
      d_pts  <- points_use |> filter(id %in% unique(od_sub$dest_id))
      if (nrow(o_pts) == 0 || nrow(d_pts) == 0) {
        pb$tick(tokens = list(msg = sprintf("%s %s %d/%d (skip)",
                                            b$dow_type, b$tod_bin, k, length(chunks))))
        next
      }
      m <- ettm_safe(
        r5r_network = r5r_network,
        origins = o_pts, destinations = d_pts,
        mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), mode_egress = "WALK",
        departure_datetime = dep_dt,
        time_window = TRANSIT_TIME_WINDOW,
        breakdown = TRUE,
        max_walk_time = TRANSIT_ROUTING_WALK_MIN,
        max_trip_duration = TRANSIT_ROUTING_TOTAL_MIN,
        max_rides = MAX_TRANSIT_RIDES,
        n_threads = N_VCPU, progress = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
      # Normalize column names across r5r versions before aggregation.
      dt_m <- .r5r_norm_cols(as.data.table(m))
      if (nrow(dt_m) > 0) {
        bin_out[[k]] <- dt_m[, .(
          transit_total_raw    = safe_median(total_time),
          transit_access_raw   = safe_median(access_time),
          transit_wait_raw     = safe_median(wait_time),
          transit_ivtt_raw     = safe_median(ride_time),
          transit_transfer_raw = safe_median(transfer_time),
          transit_egress_raw   = safe_median(egress_time)
        ), by = .(from_id, to_id)] |>
          as_tibble() |>
          transmute(
            origin_id = as.character(from_id), dest_id = as.character(to_id),
            transit_total_raw,
            transit_walk_raw = transit_access_raw + transit_transfer_raw +
                               transit_egress_raw,
            transit_wait_raw, transit_ivtt_raw)
      }
      pb$tick(tokens = list(msg = sprintf("%s %s %d/%d",
                                          b$dow_type, b$tod_bin, k, length(chunks))))
    }
    bin_df <- bind_rows(bin_out)
    if (nrow(bin_df) > 0) {
      out_list[[i]] <- bin_df |>
        mutate(dow_type = b$dow_type, tod_bin = b$tod_bin)
    }
  }
  bind_rows(out_list)
}
```

```{r build-all-transit-skims}
log_stage("Stage 9: Build transit skims for each unique GTFS combo")

od_pairs_all <- trips_seattle |>
  distinct(origin_id, dest_id, dow_type, tod_bin)

points_use <- points_df |> filter(id %in% seattle_tract_ids)
log_msg(sprintf("OD universe: %d (origin × dest × bin) entries; %d Seattle centroids",
                nrow(od_pairs_all), nrow(points_use)))

# Build & cache one transit skim per unique GTFS combo.
transit_skims <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(unique_combos))) {
  row <- unique_combos[i, ]
  combo_str <- row$gtfs_combo
  if (is.na(combo_str)) next

  combo_short <- substr(digest::digest(combo_str), 1, 8)
  cache_label <- sprintf("transit_skim_%s_%s", row$combo_label, combo_short)
  # Include file signatures of every GTFS .zip that feeds into r5r so that
  # editing/replacing a GTFS file invalidates the cached skim automatically.
  combo_paths <- gtfs_files_for(combo_str)
  all_gtfs_for_skim <- c(combo_paths, gtfs_unchanged_paths)
  gtfs_files_sig <- digest::digest(lapply(all_gtfs_for_skim, file_signature))
  inputs <- list(
    combo = combo_str,
    od_sig = digest::digest(od_pairs_all),
    pts_sig = digest::digest(points_use),
    win = TRANSIT_TIME_WINDOW,
    gtfs_files_sig = gtfs_files_sig,
    # v3: aligned transit routing constants with Phase 1 (TRANSIT_WINDOW_PRE
    # 5→10, TRANSIT_ROUTING_WALK_MIN 30→45, MAX_TRANSIT_RIDES 3→4, chunk
    # 60→200, plus data-driven rep_hour per (dow_type, tod_bin) replacing
    # the hardcoded AM→8 mapping). All 8 transit skims rebuild.
    version = "v3"
  )

  transit_skims[[combo_str]] <- with_cache(
    cache_label, inputs,
    function() {
      r5r_dir <- r5r_dir_for_combo(combo_str)
      log_msg(sprintf("Starting r5r at %s", basename(r5r_dir)))
      net <- r5r::build_network(data_path = r5r_dir, verbose = FALSE,
                                overwrite = FALSE)
      on.exit(try(r5r::stop_r5(net), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
      build_transit_skim(net, label = row$combo_label,
                         od_pairs = od_pairs_all,
                         points_use = points_use,
                         bins = transit_bin_universe)
    },
    subdir = "skim_t2")
}

log_msg(sprintf("Built %d transit skims", length(transit_skims)))
```


# 9b. Walk and bike skims (r5r-routed, full Seattle universe)

Phase 1 routed walk and bike per HTS-trip via r5r WALK / BICYCLE modes
(Phase1BuildMNL §5a-b). For Phase 2 we extend this to **every
Seattle-internal OD pair** so `predict_interior_mnl_shares` can feed
the MNL real network-routed walk/bike times for any Daysim OD — not
the haversine-×-1.4 / fixed-speed surrogate that previously stood in.

Walk/bike are GTFS-schedule-independent, so we build once using the
baseline r5r network and reuse across all 12 scenario configs.

```{r build-walk-bike-skims}
log_stage("Stage 9b: Build walk + bike skims (full Seattle internal OD universe)")

# Same departure datetime as the AM-Weekday transit skim — needed for
# r5r's API but doesn't affect walk/bike routing (no schedules).
am_wday_row <- transit_bin_universe |>
  filter(dow_type == "Weekday", tod_bin == "AM") |> head(1)
walk_bike_dep_dt <- if (nrow(am_wday_row) > 0)
  am_wday_row$rep_datetime[1] else
  as.POSIXct(paste0(BASE_MONDAY, " 08:00:00"),
             tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
log_msg(sprintf("Departure datetime for walk/bike: %s",
                format(walk_bike_dep_dt)))

# OD universe = all Seattle internal pairs (matches the transit skim's
# universe so MNL inputs are consistent across modes).
od_pairs_internal_seattle <- trips_seattle |>
  distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
log_msg(sprintf("Walk/bike OD universe: %d Seattle-internal pairs",
                nrow(od_pairs_internal_seattle)))

points_use_seattle <- points_df |> filter(id %in% seattle_tract_ids)

build_walk_or_bike_skim <- function(mode_name, max_trip_min, label) {
  # Reuse any pre-built r5r network — walk/bike doesn't depend on GTFS.
  # Pick the baseline combo's network (will already be loaded if §9 ran).
  baseline_combo <- config_table |>
    filter(transit_id == "baseline", street_id == "no_pri_no_av") |>
    pull(gtfs_combo) |> head(1)
  r5r_dir <- r5r_dir_for_combo(baseline_combo)
  log_msg(sprintf("Routing %s skim via r5r (n=%d ODs)...",
                  label, nrow(od_pairs_internal_seattle)))
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  net <- r5r::build_network(data_path = r5r_dir, verbose = FALSE,
                            overwrite = FALSE)
  on.exit(try(r5r::stop_r5(net), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  origin_ids <- sort(unique(c(od_pairs_internal_seattle$origin_id,
                              od_pairs_internal_seattle$dest_id)))
  pts <- points_use_seattle |> filter(id %in% origin_ids)
  m <- r5r::travel_time_matrix(
    r5r_network = net,
    origins = pts, destinations = pts,
    mode = mode_name,
    departure_datetime = walk_bike_dep_dt,
    max_trip_duration = max_trip_min,
    n_threads = N_VCPU,
    progress = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  log_msg(sprintf("  %s skim done (%.0f sec; %d finite OD pairs)",
                  label,
                  as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"),
                  nrow(m)))
  # r5r column name varies across versions:
  #   r5r <= 1.x: `travel_time`
  #   r5r >= 2.x: `travel_time_p50` (median percentile)
  # Pick whichever is present; fall back to any column starting with
  # "travel_time" if neither standard name is found.
  m_df <- as_tibble(m)
  tt_col <- if      ("travel_time"     %in% names(m_df)) "travel_time"
            else if ("travel_time_p50" %in% names(m_df)) "travel_time_p50"
            else {
              cand <- grep("^travel_time", names(m_df), value = TRUE)
              if (length(cand) == 0)
                stop(sprintf("No travel_time column in r5r output (got: %s)",
                             paste(names(m_df), collapse = ", ")))
              cand[1]
            }
  log_sub(sprintf("    r5r travel-time column: %s", tt_col))
  tibble(
    origin_id = as.character(m_df$from_id),
    dest_id   = as.character(m_df$to_id),
    tt_min    = as.numeric(m_df[[tt_col]]))
}

# r5r WALK default speed ≈ 3.6 km/h = 2.24 mph (matches Phase 1).
# r5r BICYCLE default speed ≈ 12 km/h = 7.45 mph (matches Phase 1).
skim_walk_p2 <- with_cache("skim_walk_p2",
  list(od_sig = digest::digest(od_pairs_internal_seattle),
       pts_sig = digest::digest(points_use_seattle),
       version = "p2_v1"),
  function() build_walk_or_bike_skim("WALK",    60L, "walk"),
  subdir = "skim_t2")
skim_bike_p2 <- with_cache("skim_bike_p2",
  list(od_sig = digest::digest(od_pairs_internal_seattle),
       pts_sig = digest::digest(points_use_seattle),
       version = "p2_v1"),
  function() build_walk_or_bike_skim("BICYCLE", 60L, "bike"),
  subdir = "skim_t2")

log_msg(sprintf("Walk skim: %d ODs, median walk_tt = %.1f min",
                nrow(skim_walk_p2),
                median(skim_walk_p2$tt_min, na.rm = TRUE)))
log_msg(sprintf("Bike skim: %d ODs, median bike_tt = %.1f min",
                nrow(skim_bike_p2),
                median(skim_bike_p2$tt_min, na.rm = TRUE)))
```


# 10. Equilibrium loop helper

`run_equilibrium_v2()` runs the BPR + MSA loop with mode-choice feedback,
using the new MNL spec and the pre-baked transit skim for the configuration.

```{r equilibrium-helper}
# Predict MNL mode share for ALL Seattle-internal Daysim ODs (both ODs
# with HTS samples and ODs without) using a UNIFIED method:
#
#   For each Daysim OD (A → B):
#   1. Take all HTS trips with origin tract = A (a "kernel" of trips
#      that share the origin context — household characteristics,
#      vehicle ownership, traveler counts at A).
#   2. Override each kernel trip's travel times with THIS OD's times:
#         drive_tt = drive_tt_lookup(A,B) at current iter (congested+GAM)
#         transit_*  = AM-Weekday transit skim for (A,B)
#         walk_tt    = haversine(A,B) × 1.4 / 3 mph
#         bike_tt    = haversine(A,B) × 1.4 / 10 mph
#   3. Override each kernel trip's parking_money_usd with the destination
#      tract's average parking (parking is destination-specific — downtown
#      is $$, suburbs are free — so the kernel trip's parking, which was
#      for ITS destination, would be wrong for B). All other per-trip
#      features (travelers_total, vehicle_count_n, is_work,
#      estimated_transit_fare) are kept from the kernel trip.
#   4. Compute MNL utility per (Daysim OD × kernel trip) pair → softmax.
#   5. Average per OD weighted by trip_weight to get per-OD mode share.
#
# This eliminates the prior split between "HTS-covered" and "interior-
# fallback" prediction paths — all interior ODs go through the same MNL
# pipeline. Cordon ODs (involves_gateway = TRUE) still use Daysim's
# empirical mode shares because we have no HTS sample of external-
# commuter trip features to apply MNL with.
predict_interior_mnl_shares <- function(od_interior, trips_in,
                                         transit_skim_long,
                                         drive_tt_lookup,
                                         av_demand,
                                         tod_bin  = "AM",
                                         dow_type = "Weekday") {
  # od_interior: (origin_id, dest_id, ...) for non-cordon Daysim ODs not in HTS
  # trips_in:    full HTS sample with per-trip features and trip_weight
  # transit_skim_long: full transit skim
  # drive_tt_lookup:   (origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt) — current iter's
  #                    congested+calibrated drive_tt per OD
  # av_demand:   apply av_drive_tt_shrink to drive_tt coefficient
  # tod_bin, dow_type: filter the transit skim to this slice. The mode-
  #                    choice kernel sees the right transit travel times
  #                    for the TOD being modeled, not always AM-peak.
  if (nrow(od_interior) == 0) {
    return(tibble(origin_id = character(0), dest_id = character(0),
                  p_drive = numeric(0), p_walk = numeric(0),
                  p_bike = numeric(0), p_transit = numeric(0),
                  n_hts_kernel = integer(0)))
  }
  ts_tod <- transit_skim_long |>
    filter(dow_type == !!dow_type, tod_bin == !!tod_bin) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, transit_walk_raw, transit_wait_raw,
           transit_ivtt_raw, transit_total_raw)
  pts <- all_tract_centroids

  # Destination-tract parking-cost lookup (HTS-trip-weighted mean of
  # parking_money_usd at each destination). Used to override the kernel
  # trip's own parking cost with the Daysim OD's destination's typical
  # parking cost. Without this we'd apply, e.g., $0 parking (because the
  # kernel trip went somewhere with free parking) to a Daysim OD that
  # actually goes downtown.
  parking_by_dest <- trips_in |>
    group_by(dest_id) |>
    summarise(
      parking_dest = stats::weighted.mean(parking_money_usd, trip_weight,
                                          na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop")

  trips_feat <- trips_in |>
    select(origin_id, trip_id, trip_weight,
           travelers_total, parking_money_usd, vehicle_count_n,
           is_work, estimated_transit_fare)

  expanded <- od_interior |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id) |>
    inner_join(trips_feat, by = "origin_id",
               relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    # Override parking with dest-tract average (per (3) above).
    left_join(parking_by_dest, by = "dest_id") |>
    mutate(parking_money_usd = coalesce(parking_dest, parking_money_usd)) |>
    select(-parking_dest) |>
    inner_join(skim_drive_full |>
                 select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_dist_mi),
               by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    left_join(drive_tt_lookup, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    left_join(ts_tod, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    # Walk and bike from r5r per-OD skims (matches Phase 1's MNL training).
    # Falls back to haversine only if an OD pair isn't covered by the
    # walk/bike skim — should be rare since the skims cover all Seattle
    # internal pairs.
    left_join(skim_walk_p2 |>
                transmute(origin_id, dest_id, walk_tt_raw_od = tt_min),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    left_join(skim_bike_p2 |>
                transmute(origin_id, dest_id, bike_tt_raw_od = tt_min),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    inner_join(pts |> transmute(origin_id = id, lon_o = lon, lat_o = lat),
               by = "origin_id") |>
    inner_join(pts |> transmute(dest_id = id, lon_d = lon, lat_d = lat),
               by = "dest_id") |>
    mutate(
      # Haversine fallback for ODs not in the walk/bike skims (rare).
      hav_m = .haversine_m(lon_o, lat_o, lon_d, lat_d),
      walk_tt_raw_od = coalesce(walk_tt_raw_od,
                                hav_m * 1.4 / 1609.344 / 3.0 * 60),
      bike_tt_raw_od = coalesce(bike_tt_raw_od,
                                hav_m * 1.4 / 1609.344 / 10.0 * 60),
      transit_walk = coalesce(transit_walk_raw, 0),
      transit_wait = coalesce(transit_wait_raw, 0),
      transit_ivtt = coalesce(transit_ivtt_raw, NA_real_))

  bd <- if (av_demand) B$drive_tt * params$av_drive_tt_shrink else B$drive_tt
  cost_drive <- (DRIVE_COST_PER_MILE * expanded$drive_dist_mi +
                 expanded$parking_money_usd) /
                pmax(expanded$travelers_total, 1)
  U_drive <- B$cost     * cost_drive +
             bd         * expanded$drive_tt +
             B$vc_drive * expanded$vehicle_count_n
  U_walk  <- B$asc_walk +
             B$iswork_walk * expanded$is_work +
             B$walking_min * expanded$walk_tt_raw_od
  U_bike  <- B$asc_bike +
             B$iswork_bike * expanded$is_work +
             B$bike_tt     * expanded$bike_tt_raw_od
  U_transit <- B$asc_transit +
               B$iswork_transit * expanded$is_work +
               B$cost           * expanded$estimated_transit_fare +
               B$walking_min    * expanded$transit_walk +
               B$tr_diff        * (expanded$transit_ivtt +
                                   expanded$transit_wait -
                                   expanded$drive_tt)

  # Availability filters — match Phase 1's HTS-trip availability rules
  # (Phase1BuildMNL P1:1562–1569). For AM-peak conditions:
  #
  #   drive_avail   : drive_tt finite & positive
  #   walk_avail    : walk_tt finite & positive
  #   bike_avail    : bike_tt finite & positive
  #   transit_avail : transit_ivtt finite & positive, AND
  #                   transit_walk <= 45 min  (P1 MAX_TRANSIT_WALK_MIN)
  #                   transit_wait <= 60 min  (P1 MAX_TRANSIT_WAIT_MIN)
  #                   transit_total <= 180 min (P1 MAX_TRANSIT_TOTAL_MIN)
  # (P1 also caps `n_rides <= 4`, but Phase 2 doesn't aggregate that
  # column from r5r — the `max_rides = 4` setting on the routing call
  # itself already prevents the >4-ride itineraries from being returned.)
  MAX_TRANSIT_WALK_MIN  <- 45
  MAX_TRANSIT_WAIT_MIN  <- 60
  MAX_TRANSIT_TOTAL_MIN <- 180
  transit_total <- coalesce(expanded$transit_total_raw, NA_real_)
  U_drive[!is.finite(expanded$drive_tt)        | expanded$drive_tt <= 0]        <- -Inf
  U_walk [!is.finite(expanded$walk_tt_raw_od) | expanded$walk_tt_raw_od <= 0] <- -Inf
  U_bike [!is.finite(expanded$bike_tt_raw_od) | expanded$bike_tt_raw_od <= 0] <- -Inf
  U_transit[!is.finite(expanded$transit_ivtt) | expanded$transit_ivtt <= 0 |
            !is.finite(expanded$transit_walk) | expanded$transit_walk > MAX_TRANSIT_WALK_MIN |
            !is.finite(expanded$transit_wait) | expanded$transit_wait > MAX_TRANSIT_WAIT_MIN |
            !is.finite(transit_total)         | transit_total > MAX_TRANSIT_TOTAL_MIN]   <- -Inf

  Umat <- cbind(drive = U_drive, walk = U_walk,
                bike  = U_bike,  transit = U_transit)
  P <- row_softmax(Umat)

  expanded |>
    mutate(p_drive = P[, "drive"], p_walk = P[, "walk"],
           p_bike  = P[, "bike"],  p_transit = P[, "transit"]) |>
    group_by(origin_id, dest_id) |>
    summarise(
      p_drive       = weighted.mean(p_drive,   trip_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      p_transit     = weighted.mean(p_transit, trip_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      p_walk        = weighted.mean(p_walk,    trip_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      p_bike        = weighted.mean(p_bike,    trip_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_hts_kernel  = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop")
}

# Daysim-loaded OD volumes. Per-OD mode shares come from TWO sources:
#   1. interior_mnl (Seattle-internal Daysim ODs): per-OD MNL prediction
#      using HTS trips at the origin tract as a per-trip-feature kernel,
#      with the Daysim OD's actual travel times overriding the kernel
#      trip's times. Built by predict_interior_mnl_shares per iteration.
#      Same logic applied to every interior OD — no special handling for
#      ODs that happen to have HTS samples vs not.
#   2. cordon (one endpoint is a gateway): Daysim's empirical mode shares
#      from the trip table's MODE codes. We have no HTS sample of
#      external-commuter trip features, so MNL with internal-Seattle
#      features would be extrapolation. Daysim's own observed shares are
#      the best signal for cordon trips.
#
# Returns one row per Daysim OD with assigned shares + drive_vehicles_peakhr.
#
# `am_peak_hours` is a legacy parameter name; it actually accepts the
# hours-per-day for the *current* TOD (e.g. 2 for AM, 6 for Midday, 8
# for Night). Callers should pass `params$tod_hours_per_day[[tod_bin]]`.
od_drive_volumes <- function(interior_mnl, od_demand,
                             am_peak_hours, auto_occupancy) {
  od_out <- od_demand |>
    left_join(interior_mnl |>
                rename(p_drive_int   = p_drive,
                       p_transit_int = p_transit,
                       p_walk_int    = p_walk,
                       p_bike_int    = p_bike),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    mutate(
      coverage = case_when(
        !is.na(p_drive_int) ~ "interior_mnl",
        involves_gateway    ~ "cordon",
        TRUE                ~ "uncovered"),  # shouldn't fire for valid data
      p_drive = case_when(
        coverage == "interior_mnl" ~ p_drive_int,
        coverage == "cordon"       ~ p_drive_dsm,
        TRUE                       ~ p_drive_dsm),
      p_transit = case_when(
        coverage == "interior_mnl" ~ p_transit_int,
        coverage == "cordon"       ~ p_transit_dsm,
        TRUE                       ~ p_transit_dsm),
      p_walk = case_when(
        coverage == "interior_mnl" ~ p_walk_int,
        coverage == "cordon"       ~ p_walk_dsm,
        TRUE                       ~ p_walk_dsm),
      p_bike = case_when(
        coverage == "interior_mnl" ~ p_bike_int,
        coverage == "cordon"       ~ p_bike_dsm,
        TRUE                       ~ p_bike_dsm),
      drive_person_trips_window = trips * p_drive,
      drive_vehicles_peakhr =
        drive_person_trips_window / am_peak_hours / auto_occupancy
    )
  od_out
}

set_edge_times <- function(g, new_t) {
  g$time          <- new_t
  g$time_weighted <- new_t
  g
}

run_equilibrium_v2 <- function(config_row, trips_in, transit_skim_long,
                               graph_in, skim_drive_dodgr_in,
                               od_demand_in,
                               tod_bin   = params$tods_to_run[[1]],
                               dow_type  = "Weekday",
                               flow_seed_vec_in = NULL,
                               od_cal_lookup_in = NULL,
                               global_cal_ratio_in = NULL,
                               hours_in = NULL,
                               residential_calm_mph = NA,
                               residential_cap_vph = NA) {
  scenario <- config_row$config_id
  use_priority <- isTRUE(config_row$transit_priority)
  av_demand    <- isTRUE(config_row$av_demand)

  # TOD-specific lookups (default to the back-compat singletons set up in
  # §12 if the caller didn't pass any). `hours_in` lets §14 plug in this
  # TOD's hours-per-day for the vehicles/hour denominator; default uses
  # tod_hours_per_day[[tod_bin]] when available, else legacy am_peak_hours.
  if (is.null(od_cal_lookup_in))    od_cal_lookup_in    <- od_drive_cal_lookup
  if (is.null(global_cal_ratio_in)) global_cal_ratio_in <- global_drive_cal_ratio
  if (is.null(hours_in)) {
    hr <- params$tod_hours_per_day[[tod_bin]]
    hours_in <- if (!is.null(hr) && is.finite(as.numeric(hr)) && hr > 0)
      as.numeric(hr) else params$am_peak_hours
  }

  log_sub(sprintf("[%s][%s] equilibrium starting (priority=%s, av=%s, %d Daysim ODs)",
                  scenario, tod_bin, use_priority, av_demand, nrow(od_demand_in)))

  g <- graph_in
  # Pick capacity column based on transit priority flag.
  g$cap_vph_eff <- if (use_priority) g$cap_vph_priority else g$cap_vph_baseline

  # --- Bus-lane "break" (priority configs only) -----------------------------
  # A directional edge that loses ALL general lanes (bus_lane_affected &
  # new_lanes_eff <= 0) is removed from THROUGH routing: its congested routing
  # time is pinned to a prohibitive value each MSA iter so no shortest path
  # uses it, and its fixed background seed is zeroed so it can't flood. Capacity
  # and t0_sec are left untouched, so V/C, cap-delta and free-flow speed stay
  # honest and finite (no divide-by-zero). The mask is per directional edge, so
  # one-way / two-way / asymmetric conversions are all handled automatically.
  BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC <- 1e7
  .broken_edge <- if (use_priority)
    (g$bus_lane_affected & (is.na(g$new_lanes_eff) | g$new_lanes_eff <= 0))
    else rep(FALSE, nrow(g))
  .broken_edge[is.na(.broken_edge)] <- FALSE

  # --- Residential traffic calming (optional) -------------------------------
  # Cap residential / living_street free-flow speed at `residential_calm_mph`
  # by raising t0_sec where it currently implies a faster speed. This slows the
  # network (the Vision-Zero lever — lower network speed → fewer fatalities) AND
  # makes local streets less attractive for through-routing (some diverted flow
  # returns to arterials), WITHOUT removing any edge — local access stays open,
  # so no choking and no divide-by-zero. Mask is per directional edge.
  if (length(residential_calm_mph) == 1 && is.finite(residential_calm_mph)) {
    .resi <- g$highway %in% c("residential", "living_street")
    .resi[is.na(.resi)] <- FALSE
    .dist <- if ("d_m" %in% names(g)) g$d_m else g$d
    .calm_t0 <- .dist / (residential_calm_mph * 0.44704)   # mph -> m/s
    g$t0_sec[.resi] <- pmax(g$t0_sec[.resi], .calm_t0[.resi])
    log_sub(sprintf("[%s] residential calming: %d edges capped at %g mph",
                    scenario, sum(.resi), residential_calm_mph))
  }

  # --- Residential capacity restriction (optional) --------------------------
  # Cap residential / living_street capacity at `residential_cap_vph` (e.g. the
  # 150 vph living-street floor). Together with the speed calming above this
  # pushes through-traffic off local streets (lower cap -> higher V/C -> steeper
  # BPR penalty -> routing prefers arterials) WITHOUT removing the edge, so
  # local access stays open and V/C stays finite (cap floored at >0).
  if (length(residential_cap_vph) == 1 && is.finite(residential_cap_vph)) {
    .resc <- g$highway %in% c("residential", "living_street")
    .resc[is.na(.resc)] <- FALSE
    g$cap_vph_eff[.resc] <- pmin(g$cap_vph_eff[.resc], residential_cap_vph)
    log_sub(sprintf("[%s] residential cap: %d edges capped at %g vph",
                    scenario, sum(.resc), residential_cap_vph))
  }

  # Per-TOD flow_seed: caller's vector overrides whatever is currently on
  # the graph. Caller should pass the TOD-scaled SDOT/WSDOT observed flows
  # (§13a) minus the unseeded-baseline model flows (§13b) for this TOD.
  if (!is.null(flow_seed_vec_in)) {
    if (length(flow_seed_vec_in) != nrow(g))
      stop(sprintf("flow_seed_vec_in length mismatch: %d vs %d edges",
                   length(flow_seed_vec_in), nrow(g)))
    g$flow_seed <- as.numeric(flow_seed_vec_in)
  }
  # Zero the fixed background seed on fully-converted bus-lane edges so it
  # can't flood streets that are no longer general-traffic through routes.
  if (any(.broken_edge)) g$flow_seed[.broken_edge] <- 0
  # Reset to free-flow times (broken edges pinned high so routing avoids them).
  g <- set_edge_times(g, g$t0_sec)
  if (any(.broken_edge)) {
    g$time_weighted[.broken_edge] <- BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC
    g$time[.broken_edge]          <- BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC
  }

  # Per-OD drive_tt lookup for the interior-MNL prediction. Initialized
  # from free-flow dodgr × TOD-GAM cal_ratio; the equilibrium loop updates
  # this from the converged od_skim_min each iteration so interior-MNL
  # sees congested TOD times. (Per-trip drive_tt is no longer needed since
  # we replaced per-trip MNL prediction with per-OD kernel MNL.)
  drive_tt_lookup_interior <- skim_drive_full |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt_raw) |>
    left_join(od_cal_lookup_in |>
                select(origin_id, dest_id, cal_ratio),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    mutate(cal_ratio = coalesce(cal_ratio, global_cal_ratio_in),
           drive_tt  = as.numeric(drive_tt_raw) * cal_ratio) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt)

  # ODs needing interior-MNL prediction = ALL Seattle-internal Daysim
  # ODs (non-cordon). No HTS-covered/interior_fallback distinction —
  # both go through the same MNL kernel approach. Cordon ODs (gateway-
  # touching) still use Daysim's empirical mode shares in od_drive_volumes.
  od_interior_all <- od_demand_in |>
    filter(!involves_gateway)
  log_sub(sprintf("[%s] interior-MNL universe: %d Seattle-internal ODs",
                  scenario, nrow(od_interior_all)))

  history <- vector("list", params$max_iter)
  prev_time <- g$time_weighted

  pb_iter <- progress::progress_bar$new(
    format = paste0("    iter [:bar] :percent | :elapsed | ",
                    "max_rel_change=:msg"),
    total = params$max_iter, clear = FALSE, width = 80)

  for (k in seq_len(params$max_iter)) {
    iter_t0 <- Sys.time()

    # 1. Predict per-OD MNL shares for ALL Seattle-internal Daysim ODs.
    #    For each OD (A→B), uses HTS trips at origin A as a per-trip-
    #    feature kernel; overrides each kernel trip's travel times with
    #    THIS OD's times and parking with B-tract's avg. Uniform treatment
    #    of HTS-covered and not-HTS-covered interior ODs.
    interior_mnl <- predict_interior_mnl_shares(
      od_interior_all, trips_in, transit_skim_long,
      drive_tt_lookup_interior, av_demand,
      tod_bin = tod_bin, dow_type = dow_type)

    # 2. Combine interior-MNL + Daysim-empirical (cordon) into per-OD
    #    drive vehicle volumes. `hours_in` is the hours-per-day in this
    #    TOD (passes through to vehicles/hour denominator).
    od_vol <- od_drive_volumes(interior_mnl, od_demand_in,
                               am_peak_hours  = hours_in,
                               auto_occupancy = params$auto_occupancy)

    # 4. Map OD volumes to graph vertices via the expanded drive skim
    od_v <- skim_drive_dodgr_in |>
      distinct(origin_id, dest_id, o_vertex, d_vertex) |>
      inner_join(od_vol, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id"))

    # Pre-aggregate by vertex pair to avoid duplicate-key bugs.
    od_va <- od_v |>
      group_by(o_vertex, d_vertex) |>
      summarise(flow = sum(coalesce(drive_vehicles_peakhr, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop")
    o_unique <- unique(od_va$o_vertex)
    d_unique <- unique(od_va$d_vertex)
    flow_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = length(o_unique), ncol = length(d_unique),
                       dimnames = list(o_unique, d_unique))
    flow_mat[cbind(match(od_va$o_vertex, o_unique),
                   match(od_va$d_vertex, d_unique))] <- od_va$flow

    # 5. Assign flows. The static columns are stripped as a
    # workaround: dodgr's flow-aggregate is finicky about NA-containing extra
    # columns. We keep the SC-format columns the routing core needs.
    static_cols <- c(
      ".vx0", ".vx1", ".vx0_x", ".vx0_y", ".vx1_x", ".vx1_y",
      "edge_", "d", "d_weighted", "time", "time_weighted",
      "highway", "component",
      # weight_streetnet schema fallbacks (no-op if SC-format)
      "edge_id", "from_id", "to_id",
      "from_lon", "from_lat", "to_lon", "to_lat",
      "geom_num", "way_id"
    )
    g_clean <- g[, intersect(static_cols, names(g))]
    class(g_clean) <- class(g)
    # ROUTE BY CONGESTED TIME: dodgr_flows_aggregate has no `shortest` arg and
    # minimises `d_weighted`, which set_edge_times never updates (so it stays
    # free-flow distance). Without this line flows never reroute as links
    # congest, while the skim (route_pairwise_times) does — they diverge. Copy
    # the congested time into d_weighted so the assignment is a proper
    # time-based equilibrium that load-balances (and avoids broken bus edges,
    # which carry BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC).
    g_clean$d_weighted <- g_clean$time_weighted
    # CRITICAL: norm_sums = FALSE.
    # dodgr's default norm_sums = TRUE normalises so the per-origin row-sum
    # of edge-flows equals the row-sum of `flows` — i.e., it treats `flows`
    # as a probability distribution. We want the literal interpretation:
    #   flow_on_edge_e = sum_{(i,j) : e in path(i,j)} flows[i,j]
    # Without this, ~95% of expected edge-flow is silently lost (dodgr
    # 0.4.3 with motorcar paths: ~3 edges/vehicle instead of 30+), making
    # flow_seed dominate the equilibrium and AV-induced demand invisible
    # to vmt_peakhr / avg_speed_mph.
    fg <- dodgr::dodgr_flows_aggregate(graph = g_clean,
                                       from = o_unique, to = d_unique,
                                       flows = flow_mat,
                                       norm_sums = FALSE)
    fg_edge_ids <- as.character(dgr_edge_id(fg))
    fcol <- if (is.matrix(fg$flow)) fg$flow[, 1] else fg$flow
    flow_lookup <- setNames(fcol, fg_edge_ids)
    flow_vec <- as.numeric(flow_lookup[as.character(dgr_edge_id(g))])
    flow_vec[is.na(flow_vec)] <- 0
    # MSA on FLOWS (Powell–Sheffi): successively average the all-or-nothing
    # link volumes rather than the link times, so parallel routes each take a
    # FRACTION of the flow instead of 100% flip-flopping every iteration. This
    # is what damps the cycle and converges the now-rerouting equilibrium
    # (averaging only times, with all-or-nothing flows, oscillates).
    w <- if (k < params$msa_start_step) 1 else 1 / k
    g$flow_vph <- if (k == 1L) flow_vec else (1 - w) * g$flow_vph + w * flow_vec

    # 6. BPR + reliability
    flow_seed_vec <- if ("flow_seed" %in% names(g)) g$flow_seed else 0
    total_flow <- g$flow_vph + flow_seed_vec
    vc <- total_flow / pmax(g$cap_vph_eff, 1)
    vc_for_bpr <- pmin(vc, params$bpr_vc_cap)
    # Per-edge BPR alpha from §5's annotate_caps (ARTDESCRIPT-derived
    # where available, OSM-derived otherwise). Falls back to the global
    # params$bpr_alpha for graphs built before this annotation was added.
    bpr_alpha_v <- if ("bpr_alpha_eff" %in% names(g))
      as.numeric(g$bpr_alpha_eff) else params$bpr_alpha
    bpr_alpha_v[!is.finite(bpr_alpha_v)] <- params$bpr_alpha
    bpr_factor <- 1 + bpr_alpha_v * vc_for_bpr^params$bpr_beta
    rel_factor <- 1 + params$reliability_lambda *
                  pmax(0, vc_for_bpr - params$reliability_vc_threshold)^2
    new_time <- g$t0_sec * bpr_factor * rel_factor

    # 7. Times come straight from the AVERAGED flow above — the successive
    # averaging now happens on the flow (step 5), not the time.
    # Keep fully-converted bus-lane edges off the through-routing graph.
    if (any(.broken_edge)) new_time[.broken_edge] <- BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC
    g <- set_edge_times(g, new_time)

    # 8. Recompute OD car skim and per-trip drive_tt (only for dodgr-routable)
    tt_sec <- route_pairwise_times(g,
      from = skim_drive_dodgr_in$o_vertex,
      to   = skim_drive_dodgr_in$d_vertex,
      shortest = FALSE)
    # car_tt_min_raw is the new dodgr raw time. The MNL was estimated on
    # GAM-calibrated drive_tt, so we apply each trip's per-OD calibration
    # ratio (cal/raw at baseline). For r5r-fallback ODs the dodgr time is
    # NA → keep the calibrated baseline.
    od_skim_min <- tibble(
      origin_id      = skim_drive_dodgr_in$origin_id,
      dest_id        = skim_drive_dodgr_in$dest_id,
      car_tt_min_raw = as.numeric(tt_sec) / 60
    ) |>
      distinct(origin_id, dest_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

    # Per-trip drive_tt is no longer needed (the unified interior-MNL
    # uses per-OD drive_tt_lookup_interior, refreshed below from the
    # same od_skim_min). Kept the routing call above because we still
    # need car_tt_min_raw for the bundle's od_skim_converged output and
    # for the static-extractor accessibility calculations.

    # Also expose calibrated OD-level skim for downstream metrics.
    od_skim_min <- od_skim_min |>
      mutate(car_tt_min = car_tt_min_raw)  # raw for VMT/speed math; cal is per-trip

    # Refresh the interior-MNL drive_tt lookup for the next iteration —
    # use this iter's converged car_tt_min_raw × per-OD TOD-GAM cal_ratio
    # where available, else fall back to free-flow × cal_ratio (Daysim
    # ODs that weren't dodgr-routable).
    drive_tt_lookup_interior <- skim_drive_full |>
      select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt_raw) |>
      left_join(od_skim_min |> select(origin_id, dest_id, car_tt_min_raw),
```
