```{r equilibrium-helper}
                by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      left_join(od_cal_lookup_in |>
                  select(origin_id, dest_id, cal_ratio),
                by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      mutate(cal_ratio = coalesce(cal_ratio, global_cal_ratio_in),
             drive_tt = if_else(is.finite(car_tt_min_raw),
                                car_tt_min_raw * cal_ratio,
                                as.numeric(drive_tt_raw) * cal_ratio)) |>
      select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt)

    # Convergence check (relative change in busy-edge times).
    big <- total_flow > 50
    if (any(big)) {
      rel <- abs(new_time[big] - prev_time[big]) / pmax(prev_time[big], 1)
      max_rel <- max(rel, na.rm = TRUE); mean_rel <- mean(rel, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      max_rel <- 0; mean_rel <- 0
    }

    # Trip-weighted iter-level mode shares from od_vol (the per-OD MNL
    # output blended with cordon-empirical). Used to track convergence
    # of the mode-choice equilibrium alongside the time-equilibrium.
    iter_mode_drive   <- weighted.mean(od_vol$p_drive,   od_vol$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
    iter_mode_transit <- weighted.mean(od_vol$p_transit, od_vol$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
    history[[k]] <- tibble(
      config_id = scenario, tod = tod_bin, iter = k, w = w,
      max_rel_change = max_rel, mean_rel_change = mean_rel,
      n_overcap = sum(vc > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_vc_busy = mean(vc[big], na.rm = TRUE),
      mode_share_drive   = iter_mode_drive,
      mode_share_transit = iter_mode_transit,
      seconds = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), iter_t0, units = "secs"))
    )

    pb_iter$tick(tokens = list(msg = sprintf("mean=%.4f max=%.1f", mean_rel, max_rel)))
    # Per-iteration heartbeat to run_progress.log so a HEADLESS run can be
    # watched live (the pb_iter bar only goes to the console, never the file).
    .tee(sprintf("      [%s/%s] iter %2d/%d  mean_rel=%.4f (tol %.3g)  max_rel=%.2f\n",
                 scenario, tod_bin, k, params$max_iter, mean_rel, params$rel_tol, max_rel))
    prev_time <- new_time

    # Converge on the MEAN relative time change over loaded links, not the MAX:
    # on this oversaturated network (V/C up to ~2.4) a handful of links where
    # the all-or-nothing assignment flickers keep max_rel noisy (~0.5–10) even
    # though the bulk — mean_rel, n_overcap, mode shares — is fully settled.
    if (mean_rel < params$rel_tol && k >= 3) {
      log_sub(sprintf("[%s] converged at iter %d (mean_rel=%.4f, max_rel=%.2f)",
                      scenario, k, mean_rel, max_rel))
      break
    }
  }

  # Broken bus-lane edges were pinned to BROKEN_ROUTE_TIME_SEC only to keep
  # through traffic off them DURING routing. The converged skim is already
  # computed, so restore their real free-flow time here — otherwise that 1e7
  # × the tiny residual flow on them dumps a fake mountain of vehicle-hours
  # into every downstream VMT / speed / Vision-Zero metric (it tanked the
  # network speed to ~0.9 mph). Flow on them is ~0, so at free-flow time their
  # VHT/VMT contribution is negligible (as it should be — they're bus-only).
  if (any(.broken_edge)) {
    g$time_weighted[.broken_edge] <- g$t0_sec[.broken_edge]
    g$time[.broken_edge]          <- g$t0_sec[.broken_edge]
  }

  # ---- Diagnostic: Daysim load accounting at convergence -----------------
  # Surfaces the gap between "MNL/Daysim says this many drive vehicles
  # should be on the network" vs "this many actually got loaded as flow_vph
  # by dodgr_flows_aggregate" vs "this is the contribution from flow_seed".
  # Useful for debugging cases where AV mode-share rises but VMT doesn't —
  # if the should-load number bumps but the actually-loaded number doesn't,
  # the loss is at the dodgr-routability join (skim_drive_dodgr filter).
  diag <- tryCatch({
    am_h <- hours_in
    occ  <- params$auto_occupancy
    skim_full  <- skim_drive_full      # in-scope from §7
    skim_dodgr <- skim_drive_dodgr_in  # function arg
    ov <- od_vol                        # full Daysim universe

    full_drive_pt  <- sum(ov$trips * ov$p_drive, na.rm = TRUE)
    full_drive_vph <- full_drive_pt / am_h / occ

    # Loadable subset: ODs that survived the skim_drive_dodgr filter.
    dodgr_keys <- skim_dodgr |> distinct(origin_id, dest_id)
    loadable   <- ov |> semi_join(dodgr_keys,
                                  by = c("origin_id", "dest_id"))
    load_drive_pt  <- sum(loadable$trips * loadable$p_drive, na.rm = TRUE)
    load_drive_vph <- load_drive_pt / am_h / occ

    # Implied VMT (full vs loadable) if every drive trip ran its
    # drive_dist_mi exactly once at the per-OD MNL share.
    full_with_dist <- ov |>
      inner_join(skim_full |>
                   select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_dist_mi),
                 by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      mutate(vmt_per_hr = trips * p_drive * drive_dist_mi / am_h / occ)
    full_vmt <- sum(full_with_dist$vmt_per_hr, na.rm = TRUE)
    load_vmt <- full_with_dist |>
      semi_join(dodgr_keys, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      pull(vmt_per_hr) |> sum(na.rm = TRUE)

    # Coverage × dodgr-routability breakdown (where the loss is, if any).
    # NOTE: drive_pt is computed FIRST (before the trips column is shadowed
    # by `trips = sum(trips)`). dplyr's summarise() evaluates left-to-right
    # and prior results mask the original columns — putting trips=sum(trips)
    # before drive_pt=sum(trips*p_drive) inflates drive_pt by N×scalar.
    cov_break <- ov |>
      left_join(dodgr_keys |> mutate(.in_dodgr = TRUE),
                by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      mutate(in_dodgr = coalesce(.in_dodgr, FALSE)) |>
      group_by(coverage, in_dodgr) |>
      summarise(n_od     = dplyr::n(),
                drive_pt = sum(trips * p_drive, na.rm = TRUE),
                trips    = sum(trips, na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop") |>
      select(coverage, in_dodgr, n_od, trips, drive_pt)  # column order

    # Network-integrated VMT (what extract_vmt_speed reports)
    edge_miles  <- as.numeric(g$d) / 1609.344
    flow_vph_vmt <- sum(g$flow_vph * edge_miles, na.rm = TRUE)
    flow_seed_vmt <- if ("flow_seed" %in% names(g))
      sum(g$flow_seed * edge_miles, na.rm = TRUE) else 0

    list(full_drive_pt = full_drive_pt, full_drive_vph = full_drive_vph,
         load_drive_pt = load_drive_pt, load_drive_vph = load_drive_vph,
         full_vmt = full_vmt, load_vmt = load_vmt,
         flow_vph_vmt = flow_vph_vmt, flow_seed_vmt = flow_seed_vmt,
         cov_break = cov_break)
  }, error = function(e) {
    log_sub(sprintf("diagnostic computation FAILED: %s", conditionMessage(e)))
    NULL
  })
  if (!is.null(diag)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n  --- Daysim load accounting [%s] ---\n", scenario))
    cat(sprintf("    Total Daysim drive person-trips (window):    %12.0f\n",
                diag$full_drive_pt))
    cat(sprintf("    Total Daysim drive vehicles per peak HOUR:   %12.0f\n",
                diag$full_drive_vph))
    cat(sprintf("    Loadable (dodgr-routable) drive vehicles:    %12.0f  (%.1f%%)\n",
                diag$load_drive_vph,
                100 * diag$load_drive_vph / pmax(diag$full_drive_vph, 1)))
    cat(sprintf("    Implied VMT/hr (full Daysim):                %12.0f\n",
                diag$full_vmt))
    cat(sprintf("    Implied VMT/hr (dodgr-routable subset):      %12.0f\n",
                diag$load_vmt))
    cat(sprintf("    Integrated flow_vph × miles  (loaded):       %12.0f  ← actual\n",
                diag$flow_vph_vmt))
    cat(sprintf("    Integrated flow_seed × miles (residual seed):%12.0f\n",
                diag$flow_seed_vmt))
    cat(sprintf("    Total network VMT (flow_vph + flow_seed):    %12.0f\n",
                diag$flow_vph_vmt + diag$flow_seed_vmt))
    cat(sprintf("    Daysim-share of total VMT: %.1f%% (flow_vph / total)\n",
                100 * diag$flow_vph_vmt /
                  pmax(diag$flow_vph_vmt + diag$flow_seed_vmt, 1)))
    cat(sprintf("    Load efficiency:           %.1f%% (loaded / should-load)\n",
                100 * diag$flow_vph_vmt / pmax(diag$load_vmt, 1)))
    cat("    Coverage × dodgr-routability breakdown:\n")
    print(diag$cov_break)
    cat("\n")
  }

  list(
    scenario      = scenario,
    tod           = tod_bin,
    graph         = g,
    od_skim       = od_skim_min,
    od_volumes    = od_vol,
    history       = bind_rows(Filter(Negate(is.null), history)),
    diag_load     = diag
  )
}
```


# 11. Per-config result extraction

Each result block runs on the equilibrium output of one configuration and
appends to `results_*` accumulators keyed by `config_id`.

```{r extract-mode-share}
# Daysim-weighted mode share: aggregate per-OD MNL shares across the full
# Daysim AM-peak universe, weighting each OD by its Daysim trip total.
# `res$od_volumes` carries one row per Daysim OD with assigned shares
# (HTS-MNL where covered, cordon for gateways, scenario-mean for interior
# fallback) — exactly the right object for population-level aggregation.
extract_mode_share <- function(res, trips_in, config_row) {
  ov <- res$od_volumes
  total_trips <- sum(ov$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
  cov_mix <- ov |>
    group_by(coverage) |>
    summarise(pct_trips = 100 * sum(trips, na.rm = TRUE) / total_trips,
              .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = coverage, values_from = pct_trips,
                       values_fill = 0,
                       names_prefix = "pct_trips_")
  shares <- ov |>
    summarise(
      drive   = weighted.mean(p_drive,   trips, na.rm = TRUE),
      transit = weighted.mean(p_transit, trips, na.rm = TRUE),
      walk    = weighted.mean(p_walk,    trips, na.rm = TRUE),
      bike    = weighted.mean(p_bike,    trips, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_od_pairs = dplyr::n(),
      daysim_weighted_trips = sum(trips, na.rm = TRUE))
  bind_cols(tibble(config_id = config_row$config_id,
                   tod = res$tod %||% NA_character_),
            shares, cov_mix)
}

extract_transit_tt_stats <- function(transit_skim_long, od_demand, config_row,
                                      tod_bin = "AM", dow_type = "Weekday") {
  # Daysim-weighted transit total time (mean / median / sd) across the
  # interior Daysim OD universe (gateway ODs excluded — buses don't run
  # those routes, and the transit skim doesn't cover gateway points anyway).
  # Bin = the scenario's TOD (default AM peak weekday).
  ts <- transit_skim_long |>
    filter(dow_type == !!dow_type, tod_bin == !!tod_bin,
           is.finite(transit_total_raw)) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, transit_total_raw)
  joined <- od_demand |>
    filter(!involves_gateway) |>
    inner_join(ts, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id"))
  if (nrow(joined) == 0) {
    return(tibble(config_id = config_row$config_id, tod = tod_bin,
                  n_od_pairs = 0L, mean_min = NA_real_,
                  median_min = NA_real_, sd_min = NA_real_,
                  weighted_trips = 0))
  }
  m <- weighted.mean(joined$transit_total_raw, joined$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    config_id = config_row$config_id,
    tod = tod_bin,
    n_od_pairs = nrow(joined),
    mean_min   = m,
    median_min = matrixStats::weightedMedian(joined$transit_total_raw,
                                             joined$trips, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_min     = sqrt(weighted.mean((joined$transit_total_raw - m)^2,
                                    joined$trips, na.rm = TRUE)),
    weighted_trips = sum(joined$trips, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

extract_vmt_speed <- function(res, config_row) {
  g <- res$graph
  # VMT = peak-hour vehicle-miles-traveled, summed over edges.
  # `d` (geographic meters) is the right column for true VMT; `d_weighted`
  # has motorcar penalty multipliers baked in and would over-count miles.
  flow       <- g$flow_vph + (if ("flow_seed" %in% names(g)) g$flow_seed else 0)
  edge_miles <- as.numeric(g$d) / 1609.344
  vmt_peakhr  <- sum(flow * edge_miles, na.rm = TRUE)
  veh_hr_peak <- sum(flow * (g$time_weighted / 3600), na.rm = TRUE)
  avg_speed   <- if (veh_hr_peak > 0) vmt_peakhr / veh_hr_peak else NA_real_
  free_speed  <- {
    fhr <- sum(flow * (g$t0_sec / 3600), na.rm = TRUE)
    if (fhr > 0) vmt_peakhr / fhr else NA_real_
  }

  # Per-edge V/C (pmax floors capacity at 1 to avoid divide-by-zero on
  # rare edges with cap=0 from a missing SND mapping).
  vc <- flow / pmax(g$cap_vph_eff, 1)
  total_vmt <- sum(flow * edge_miles, na.rm = TRUE)

  # `pct_overcap_links` is the *unweighted* proportion across all edges —
  # it gets diluted when most of the graph carries near-zero flow, so
  # tends to under-state congestion. We keep it for back-compat but the
  # headline-worthy congestion metrics are the two below:
  #   pct_vmt_on_overcap : share of vehicle-miles whose edge has V/C > 1
  #                        (i.e., "what fraction of driving happens on
  #                        over-saturated infrastructure?")
  #   flow_weighted_vc   : V/C experienced by the average vehicle-mile,
  #                        weighted by VMT contribution per edge.
  pct_vmt_on_overcap <- if (total_vmt > 0)
    100 * sum((flow * edge_miles)[vc > 1], na.rm = TRUE) / total_vmt
    else NA_real_
  flow_weighted_vc <- if (total_vmt > 0)
    sum(flow * edge_miles * vc, na.rm = TRUE) / total_vmt
    else NA_real_

  tibble(
    config_id            = config_row$config_id,
    tod                  = res$tod %||% NA_character_,
    vmt_peakhr           = vmt_peakhr,
    veh_hours_peakhr     = veh_hr_peak,
    avg_speed_mph        = avg_speed,
    free_flow_speed_mph  = free_speed,
    pct_overcap_links    = 100 * mean(vc > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_vc              = mean(vc, na.rm = TRUE),
    # New flow-weighted congestion metrics — these are the ones to
    # quote in the thesis. With ~30-43% of VMT on overcap edges and a
    # flow-weighted V/C of 1.07-2.38, "the average vehicle-mile happens
    # on a saturated link" is the honest summary.
    pct_vmt_on_overcap   = pct_vmt_on_overcap,
    flow_weighted_vc     = flow_weighted_vc
  )
}

# Capture the per-edge data that's needed to compute by-category breakdowns
# downstream. Saved into the bundle so we can iterate on the categorization
# (e.g., merge ARTDESCRIPT classes, refine the unknown buckets) without
# re-running scenarios. ~140k edges × 7 cols × 8 bytes ≈ 8 MB per config.
capture_converged_edge_data <- function(res) {
  g <- res$graph
  way_id_v <- dgr_way_id(g)
  if (is.null(way_id_v)) way_id_v <- NA_character_
  tibble(
    way_id        = way_id_v,
    highway       = as.character(g$highway),
    d_m           = as.numeric(g$d),
    cap_vph_eff   = as.numeric(g$cap_vph_eff),
    flow_vph      = as.numeric(g$flow_vph),
    flow_seed     = as.numeric(if ("flow_seed" %in% names(g)) g$flow_seed
                               else rep(0, nrow(g))),
    time_weighted = as.numeric(g$time_weighted),
    t0_sec        = as.numeric(g$t0_sec)
  )
}

# Per-link breakdown by SDOT ARTDESCRIPT class (joined via way_id from
# §4c's way_snd_attrs), with three OSM-highway-based unknown buckets for
# edges not covered by the SDOT mapping. Returns one row per category
# with: avg_vph, avg_speed_mph (flow-weighted = total VMT / total veh-hr),
# avg_capacity, pct_overcapacity, plus diagnostics (n_edges, total VMT).
extract_vmt_by_category <- function(edge_data, config_row, way_snd_attrs) {
  if (is.null(edge_data) || nrow(edge_data) == 0) {
    return(tibble(config_id = config_row$config_id, category = NA_character_,
                  n_edges = NA_integer_, avg_vph = NA_real_,
                  avg_capacity = NA_real_,
                  total_vmt_peakhr = NA_real_,
                  total_vehhr_peakhr = NA_real_,
                  avg_speed_mph = NA_real_,
                  pct_overcap = NA_real_,
                  total_oversaturation_vph = NA_real_,
                  mean_oversaturation_vph  = NA_real_,
                  n_edges_oversaturated    = NA_integer_))
  }
  art_lookup <- way_snd_attrs |>
    transmute(way_id = as.character(way_id),
              art_descript = as.character(art_descript))

  edge_data |>
    mutate(way_id = as.character(way_id)) |>
    left_join(art_lookup, by = "way_id") |>
    mutate(
      flow_total = flow_vph + flow_seed,
      vc         = flow_total / pmax(cap_vph_eff, 1),
      # Demand the model placed on the edge above its capacity. Static
      # assignment has no spillback/queuing, so this is "stuck demand"
      # the BPR cap absorbs without rerouting — i.e. flow the model put
      # on the edge that, in reality, would queue, spillback to upstream
      # edges, or shift to other trip departure times. Useful as a
      # diagnostic for where static assignment's capacity assumption breaks.
      oversaturation_vph = pmax(0, flow_total - cap_vph_eff),
      edge_miles = d_m / 1609.344,
      veh_hr     = flow_total * time_weighted / 3600,
      vmt        = flow_total * edge_miles,
      category = case_when(
        !is.na(art_descript) & nzchar(art_descript) ~ art_descript,
        highway %in% c("motorway", "motorway_link",
                       "trunk", "trunk_link",
                       "primary", "primary_link")    ~ "unknown highway",
        highway %in% c("secondary", "secondary_link",
                       "tertiary",  "tertiary_link") ~ "unknown arterial",
        highway %in% c("residential", "unclassified",
                       "living_street", "service")    ~ "unknown residential",
        TRUE                                          ~ "unknown other"
      )
    ) |>
    group_by(category) |>
    summarise(
      n_edges            = dplyr::n(),
      avg_vph            = mean(flow_total, na.rm = TRUE),
      avg_capacity       = mean(cap_vph_eff, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_vmt_peakhr   = sum(vmt, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_vehhr_peakhr = sum(veh_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
      avg_speed_mph      = if (sum(veh_hr, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)
                             total_vmt_peakhr / total_vehhr_peakhr
                           else NA_real_,
      pct_overcap        = 100 * mean(vc > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      # Sum of capacity-exceeding flow across all edges in the category
      # (vph-edge units). High values flag where the BPR cap is absorbing
      # demand that, in reality, would queue or reroute.
      total_oversaturation_vph = sum(oversaturation_vph, na.rm = TRUE),
      # Among edges that ARE oversaturated, by how much on average?
      mean_oversaturation_vph  = {
        v <- oversaturation_vph[oversaturation_vph > 0]
        if (length(v)) mean(v, na.rm = TRUE) else 0
      },
      # How many edges in the category have ANY oversaturation?
      n_edges_oversaturated    = sum(oversaturation_vph > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(total_vmt_peakhr)) |>
    mutate(config_id = config_row$config_id, .before = 1)
}

# ---- Walkshed helpers --------------------------------------------------
# Seattle LAND area in m^2, summed from tract ALAND. This is the proper
# denominator for transit walkshed coverage — `seattle_sf` (place polygon)
# also includes water bodies (Lake Union, Portage Bay, Elliott Bay strip,
# etc.), which inflate the denominator artificially. ALAND-only is the
# standard for accessibility metrics in the planning literature.
.seattle_land_area_m2 <- {
  if ("ALAND" %in% names(tracts_sf)) {
    sum(as.numeric(tracts_sf$ALAND[tracts_sf$GEOID %in% seattle_tract_ids]),
        na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    # Fallback if tracts_sf doesn't carry ALAND (older tigris cache).
    log_msg("WARNING: tracts_sf has no ALAND column; using place polygon area")
    as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_transform(seattle_sf, CRS_PLANAR)))
  }
}
log_msg(sprintf("Seattle land area (denominator for walkshed): %.1f sq mi",
                .seattle_land_area_m2 / (1609.344^2)))

# Read stops (lat/lon) from a list of GTFS zip paths.
.read_stops_from_zips <- function(zip_paths) {
  out <- lapply(zip_paths, function(p) {
    tdir <- tempfile("gtfs_"); dir.create(tdir)
    on.exit(unlink(tdir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
    suppressWarnings(utils::unzip(p, files = "stops.txt", exdir = tdir))
    sc <- file.path(tdir, "stops.txt")
    if (!file.exists(sc)) return(NULL)
    fread(sc, select = c("stop_id", "stop_lat", "stop_lon"))
  })
  rbindlist(Filter(Negate(is.null), out))
}

# Compute walkshed % of Seattle LAND covered by 1/4-mi buffers around the
# given stop coordinates.
.walkshed_pct <- function(stops_df) {
  stops_df <- stops_df[is.finite(stop_lat) & is.finite(stop_lon)]
  if (nrow(stops_df) == 0) return(list(n = 0L, pct = NA_real_))
  stops_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(stops_df, coords = c("stop_lon", "stop_lat"),
                           crs = CRS_LL) |> sf::st_transform(CRS_PLANAR)
  buffers <- sf::st_buffer(stops_sf, dist = params$walkshed_radius_m) |>
    sf::st_union()
  seattle_planar <- sf::st_transform(seattle_sf, CRS_PLANAR)
  inter <- sf::st_intersection(buffers, seattle_planar)
  area_walkshed <- if (length(inter) == 0) 0 else
                     as.numeric(sf::st_area(inter))
  list(n = nrow(stops_sf),
       pct = 100 * sum(area_walkshed) / .seattle_land_area_m2)
}

# GTFS helpers used by the frequent-walkshed branch of extract_walkshed.
# Same logic as in
# GTFSTriplication.Rmd. Defined locally to keep this notebook self-contained.
time_to_sec <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  x <- as.character(x)
  out <- rep(NA_integer_, length(x))
  ok <- !is.na(x) & nzchar(x)
  if (!any(ok)) return(out)
  parts <- stringr::str_split_fixed(x[ok], ":", 3)
  h <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(parts[, 1]))
  m <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(parts[, 2]))
  s <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(parts[, 3]))
  out[ok] <- h * 3600L + m * 60L + s
  out
}
sec_to_time <- function(s) {
  s <- as.integer(s)
  sprintf("%d:%02d:%02d", s %/% 3600L, (s %% 3600L) %/% 60L, s %% 60L)
}
pick_typical_service_date <- function(gtfs, weekday = "wednesday") {
  weekday <- tolower(weekday)
  target_wday <- match(weekday,
    tolower(c("sunday","monday","tuesday","wednesday","thursday","friday","saturday"))
  ) - 1L
  has_calendar <- "calendar" %in% names(gtfs) && !is.null(gtfs$calendar) &&
                    nrow(gtfs$calendar) > 0
  if (has_calendar) {
    cal <- gtfs$calendar |>
      mutate(start_date = lubridate::ymd(start_date),
             end_date   = lubridate::ymd(end_date))
    d0 <- min(cal$start_date, na.rm = TRUE)
    d1 <- max(cal$end_date,   na.rm = TRUE)
    candidates <- seq.Date(d0, d1, by = "day")
    candidates <- candidates[(lubridate::wday(candidates) - 1L) == target_wday]
    if (length(candidates) == 0) stop("No matching weekday in calendar range.")
    if ("calendar_dates" %in% names(gtfs) && !is.null(gtfs$calendar_dates) &&
        nrow(gtfs$calendar_dates) > 0) {
      cd <- gtfs$calendar_dates |> mutate(date = lubridate::ymd(date))
      ex_count <- vapply(candidates,
                         function(d) sum(cd$date == d, na.rm = TRUE),
                         integer(1))
      if (any(ex_count == 0L)) return(candidates[which(ex_count == 0L)[1]])
      return(candidates[which.min(ex_count)])
    }
    return(candidates[1])
  }
  if ("calendar_dates" %in% names(gtfs) && !is.null(gtfs$calendar_dates) &&
      nrow(gtfs$calendar_dates) > 0) {
    cd <- gtfs$calendar_dates |> mutate(date = lubridate::ymd(date))
    cands <- sort(unique(cd$date[(lubridate::wday(cd$date) - 1L) == target_wday]))
    if (length(cands) > 0) return(cands[1])
  }
  stop("GTFS has no calendar.txt and no usable calendar_dates.txt.")
}
services_active_on_date <- function(gtfs, date) {
  date <- as.Date(date)
  active <- character()
  if ("calendar" %in% names(gtfs) && !is.null(gtfs$calendar) &&
      nrow(gtfs$calendar) > 0) {
    cal <- gtfs$calendar |>
      mutate(start_date = lubridate::ymd(start_date),
             end_date   = lubridate::ymd(end_date))
    wday_col <- tolower(weekdays(date))
    if (!(wday_col %in% names(cal)))
      stop("Unexpected weekday columns in calendar.txt.")
    active <- cal |>
      filter(start_date <= date, end_date >= date,
             .data[[wday_col]] == 1) |>
      pull(service_id) |> unique()
  }
  if ("calendar_dates" %in% names(gtfs) && !is.null(gtfs$calendar_dates) &&
      nrow(gtfs$calendar_dates) > 0) {
    cd <- gtfs$calendar_dates |>
      mutate(date = lubridate::ymd(date)) |>
      filter(date == !!date)
    added   <- cd |> filter(exception_type == 1) |> pull(service_id) |> unique()
    removed <- cd |> filter(exception_type == 2) |> pull(service_id) |> unique()
    active  <- setdiff(union(active, added), removed)
  }
  unique(active)
}
expand_frequencies_to_trips <- function(gtfs) {
  if (!("frequencies" %in% names(gtfs)) || is.null(gtfs$frequencies) ||
      nrow(gtfs$frequencies) == 0) return(gtfs)
  freq <- gtfs$frequencies |>
    mutate(start_sec    = time_to_sec(start_time),
           end_sec      = time_to_sec(end_time),
           headway_secs = as.integer(headway_secs)) |>
    filter(!is.na(start_sec), !is.na(end_sec),
           !is.na(headway_secs), headway_secs > 0)
  if (nrow(freq) == 0) {
    gtfs$frequencies <- gtfs$frequencies[0, , drop = FALSE]
    return(gtfs)
  }
  st <- gtfs$stop_times |>
    mutate(arr_sec = time_to_sec(arrival_time),
           dep_sec = time_to_sec(departure_time))
  trips <- gtfs$trips
  trip_first_dep <- st |>
    group_by(trip_id) |>
    summarize(first_dep_sec = min(dep_sec, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  new_trips <- list(); new_st <- list()
  kill_ids <- unique(freq$trip_id)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(freq))) {
    f <- freq[i, ]
    tpl_trip <- trips |> filter(trip_id == f$trip_id)
    tpl_st   <- st |> filter(trip_id == f$trip_id) |> arrange(stop_sequence)
    if (nrow(tpl_trip) == 0 || nrow(tpl_st) == 0) next
    tpl_first <- trip_first_dep$first_dep_sec[trip_first_dep$trip_id == f$trip_id]
    if (length(tpl_first) == 0 || is.na(tpl_first)) next
    rebase <- f$start_sec - tpl_first
    runs   <- seq(from = f$start_sec, to = f$end_sec - f$headway_secs,
                  by = f$headway_secs)
    if (length(runs) == 0) next
    for (k in seq_along(runs)) {
      shift <- rebase + (runs[k] - f$start_sec)
      new_id <- paste0(f$trip_id, "_FREQ_", sprintf("%04d_%04d", i, k))
      new_trips[[length(new_trips) + 1]] <- tpl_trip |> mutate(trip_id = new_id)
      new_st[[length(new_st) + 1]] <- tpl_st |>
        mutate(trip_id = new_id,
               arrival_time   = sec_to_time(arr_sec + shift),
               departure_time = sec_to_time(dep_sec + shift)) |>
        select(-arr_sec, -dep_sec)
    }
  }
  gtfs$trips <- bind_rows(
    trips |> filter(!trip_id %in% kill_ids),
    bind_rows(new_trips))
  gtfs$stop_times <- bind_rows(
    gtfs$stop_times |> filter(!trip_id %in% kill_ids),
    bind_rows(new_st))
  gtfs$frequencies <- gtfs$frequencies[0, , drop = FALSE]
  gtfs
}

extract_walkshed <- function(combo_str, config_row,
                             midday_start_hr = 10L,
                             midday_end_hr   = 14L,
                             freq_headway_min = 10) {
  # Returns BOTH:
  #   walkshed_pct_total    = % Seattle land within 1/4 mi of ANY stop
  #   walkshed_pct_frequent = % Seattle land within 1/4 mi of a stop served
  #                           by a route with midday peak headway ≤ 10 min
  #                           (matches Seattle's 2025 frequent-transit goal)
  paths_all <- c(gtfs_files_for(combo_str), gtfs_unchanged_paths)

  # ---- (a) Total walkshed: every stop in every feed ----
  total_stops <- .read_stops_from_zips(paths_all)
  total <- .walkshed_pct(total_stops)

  # ---- (b) Frequent walkshed: stops served by routes with ≤ X-min midday
  #         headway (per direction, taking the min). Run per feed, union
  #         the resulting frequent-stop ID sets across feeds, then buffer.
  freq_stops_list <- lapply(paths_all, function(p) {
    g <- tryCatch(gtfsio::import_gtfs(p), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(g)) return(NULL)
    g <- expand_frequencies_to_trips(g)

    sd <- tryCatch(pick_typical_service_date(g, "wednesday"),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(sd)) return(NULL)
    active <- services_active_on_date(g, sd)
    trips_today <- g$trips |> filter(service_id %in% active)
    if (nrow(trips_today) == 0) return(NULL)

    # Trip start time (= min departure across stops on the trip)
    trip_start <- g$stop_times |>
      filter(trip_id %in% trips_today$trip_id) |>
      mutate(dep_sec = time_to_sec(departure_time),
             arr_sec = time_to_sec(arrival_time)) |>
      group_by(trip_id) |>
      summarise(start_sec = min(coalesce(dep_sec, arr_sec), na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop") |>
      filter(is.finite(start_sec))

    midday_lo <- midday_start_hr * 3600L
    midday_hi <- midday_end_hr   * 3600L
    midday_trips <- trips_today |>
      inner_join(trip_start, by = "trip_id") |>
      filter(start_sec >= midday_lo, start_sec < midday_hi)
    if (nrow(midday_trips) == 0) return(NULL)
    if (!"direction_id" %in% names(midday_trips))
      midday_trips$direction_id <- 0L
    midday_trips$direction_id <- as.integer(coalesce(midday_trips$direction_id, 0L))

    # Per (route, direction): median consecutive-trip-gap during midday.
    # The route is "frequent" if EITHER direction has median gap ≤ threshold.
    headway <- midday_trips |>
      group_by(route_id, direction_id) |>
      arrange(start_sec, .by_group = TRUE) |>
      summarise(
        n = n(),
        median_gap_min = if (n() >= 2)
          median(diff(sort(start_sec)), na.rm = TRUE) / 60 else NA_real_,
        .groups = "drop") |>
      group_by(route_id) |>
      summarise(min_dir_headway_min = suppressWarnings(
                  min(median_gap_min, na.rm = TRUE)),
                .groups = "drop")

    freq_routes <- headway |>
      filter(is.finite(min_dir_headway_min),
             min_dir_headway_min <= freq_headway_min) |>
      pull(route_id)
    if (length(freq_routes) == 0) return(NULL)

    freq_stop_ids <- g$stop_times |>
      filter(trip_id %in% midday_trips$trip_id[
                            midday_trips$route_id %in% freq_routes]) |>
      pull(stop_id) |> unique()

    g$stops |>
      filter(stop_id %in% freq_stop_ids,
             !is.na(stop_lat), !is.na(stop_lon)) |>
      transmute(stop_id, stop_lat = as.numeric(stop_lat),
                stop_lon = as.numeric(stop_lon))
  })
  freq_stops <- rbindlist(Filter(Negate(is.null), freq_stops_list),
                          fill = TRUE)
  freq <- .walkshed_pct(freq_stops)

  tibble(
    config_id                       = config_row$config_id,
    n_stops_total                   = total$n,
    walkshed_pct_seattle_total      = total$pct,
    n_stops_frequent_midday         = freq$n,
    walkshed_pct_seattle_frequent   = freq$pct,
    freq_headway_threshold_min      = freq_headway_min,
    midday_window                   = sprintf("%02d:00-%02d:00",
                                              midday_start_hr,
                                              midday_end_hr))
}

# ---- Per-mode TT distributions -----------------------------------------
# Daysim-trip-weighted mean / median / sd of travel time, by mode, on
# interior Daysim ODs (gateway-touching ODs excluded — gateways aren't a
# meaningful destination for walk/bike/transit accessibility).
#
# Inputs are static or per-config-summary, so this is recomputed at every
# §14 run (no equilibrium output needed).
.haversine_m <- function(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) {
  R <- 6371008.8
  lat1r <- lat1 * pi / 180; lat2r <- lat2 * pi / 180
  dlat <- (lat2 - lat1) * pi / 180
  dlon <- (lon2 - lon1) * pi / 180
  a <- sin(dlat/2)^2 + cos(lat1r) * cos(lat2r) * sin(dlon/2)^2
  2 * R * asin(pmin(1, sqrt(a)))
}

extract_tt_stats_all_modes <- function(od_demand, transit_skim_long,
                                       config_row,
                                       avg_speed_mph,
                                       free_flow_speed_mph,
                                       od_skim_converged = NULL,
                                       tod_bin = "AM", dow_type = "Weekday",
                                       od_cal_lookup_in = NULL,
                                       global_cal_ratio_in = NULL) {
  if (is.null(od_cal_lookup_in))    od_cal_lookup_in    <- od_drive_cal_lookup
  if (is.null(global_cal_ratio_in)) global_cal_ratio_in <- global_drive_cal_ratio
  od <- od_demand |> filter(!involves_gateway, trips > 0)
  if (nrow(od) == 0) return(tibble())

  # NOTE: walk and bike are intentionally NOT reported in tt_stats.
  # Phase 1's MNL uses r5r-network-routed walk and bike times (~2.24 mph
  # walk default, ~7.45 mph bike); any haversine × fixed-speed surrogate
  # here would be methodologically inconsistent with the MNL inputs.
  # Since we use Phase 1's r5r values for the MNL prediction (via
  # trips_in$walk_tt_raw / bike_tt_raw), there's nothing to add at the
  # OD-level for walk/bike — they're per-trip features, not OD-level
  # quantities the model treats as such.

  # Drive time: per-OD post-equilibrium dodgr time × Phase-1 GAM
  # calibration. Per-OD precision: a route that crosses saturated I-5
  # gets the right inflation; a perpendicular route on uncongested
  # arterials gets a clean free-flow-ish time. This requires bpr_vc_cap
  # to be tuned realistically (set to 2.0, giving max edge factor 3.4×)
  # so that path-aggregate BPR factors fall in the empirical 1.5-2.5×
  # range. With bpr_vc_cap = 3.0, BPR over-stated congestion
  # so the per-OD approach gave walking-pace results.
  #
  # Falls back to network-avg-speed scaling for ODs without a converged
  # time (r5r-fallback long-distance pairs).
  scale_freeflow_to_congested <-
    if (is.finite(free_flow_speed_mph) && free_flow_speed_mph > 0 &&
        is.finite(avg_speed_mph) && avg_speed_mph > 0)
      free_flow_speed_mph / avg_speed_mph else 1
  drive_base <- skim_drive_full |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt_raw) |>
    inner_join(od, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    mutate(drive_min_fallback = as.numeric(drive_tt_raw) *
                                scale_freeflow_to_congested)
  if (!is.null(od_skim_converged) && nrow(od_skim_converged) > 0) {
    drive <- drive_base |>
      left_join(od_skim_converged |>
                  select(origin_id, dest_id,
                         drive_min_eq = car_tt_min_raw),
                by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      mutate(drive_min_uncal = if_else(is.finite(drive_min_eq),
                                       drive_min_eq, drive_min_fallback))
  } else {
    drive <- drive_base |> mutate(drive_min_uncal = drive_min_fallback)
  }
  # Apply Phase-1 GAM calibration: per-OD where HTS covers the OD, global
  # mean elsewhere. Cap defensively at [0.2, 2.0] for noisy small-sample
  # per-OD estimates. This calibration is exact at baseline conditions
  # and a first-order approximation under congestion (uniform multiplier
  # on dodgr's penalty-inflated time).
  drive <- drive |>
    left_join(od_cal_lookup_in |>
                select(origin_id, dest_id, cal_ratio),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    mutate(cal_ratio = coalesce(cal_ratio, global_cal_ratio_in),
           # Loose sanity cap. GAM predictions in [0.1, 5.0] are realistic
           # for Phase-1 calibrated distributions; outside this is likely
           # extrapolation. The previous [0.2, 2.0] cap was clamping
           # legitimate values.
           cal_ratio = pmax(0.1, pmin(5.0, cal_ratio)),
           drive_min = drive_min_uncal * cal_ratio)

  # Transit: from transit skim (TOD-aware).
  ts <- transit_skim_long |>
    filter(dow_type == !!dow_type, tod_bin == !!tod_bin,
           is.finite(transit_total_raw)) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, transit_min = transit_total_raw)
  transit <- od |> inner_join(ts, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id"))

  stat_row <- function(values, weights, mode_name) {
    finite <- is.finite(values) & is.finite(weights) & weights > 0
    v <- values[finite]; w <- weights[finite]
    if (length(v) == 0) return(tibble(
      config_id = config_row$config_id, tod = tod_bin,
      mode = mode_name,
      n_pairs = 0L, mean_min = NA_real_, median_min = NA_real_,
      sd_min = NA_real_, weighted_trips = 0))
    m <- weighted.mean(v, w)
    tibble(
      config_id      = config_row$config_id,
      tod            = tod_bin,
      mode           = mode_name,
      n_pairs        = length(v),
      mean_min       = m,
      median_min     = matrixStats::weightedMedian(v, w),
      sd_min         = sqrt(weighted.mean((v - m)^2, w)),
      weighted_trips = sum(w))
  }

  bind_rows(
    stat_row(drive$drive_min,          drive$trips,       "drive"),
    stat_row(transit$transit_min,      transit$trips,     "transit"))
}

# ---- Employment accessibility by mode ---------------------------------
# Per Seattle origin tract: jobs reachable within max_minutes by each of
# walk / bike / drive / transit. Walk and bike use haversine-distance and
# fixed speeds (config-invariant). Drive uses the static drive_tt_raw
# from skim_drive_full scaled by the config's congestion ratio. Transit
# uses the per-config transit skim.
extract_employment_accessibility_by_mode <- function(transit_skim_long,
                                                     config_row,
                                                     avg_speed_mph,
                                                     free_flow_speed_mph,
                                                     od_skim_converged = NULL,
                                                     max_minutes = 30L,
                                                     tod_bin = "AM",
                                                     dow_type = "Weekday",
                                                     od_cal_lookup_in = NULL,
                                                     global_cal_ratio_in = NULL) {
  if (is.null(od_cal_lookup_in))    od_cal_lookup_in    <- od_drive_cal_lookup
  if (is.null(global_cal_ratio_in)) global_cal_ratio_in <- global_drive_cal_ratio
  origins <- intersect(seattle_tract_ids, all_tract_centroids$id)
  emp <- employment_by_tract |> rename(dest_id = GEOID)

  # NOTE: walk and bike accessibility are intentionally NOT reported.
  # Phase 1's MNL uses r5r-network-routed walk/bike times (with hill,
  # bike-network, and pedestrian-network awareness). A haversine ×
  # fixed-speed surrogate at the OD level would be methodologically
  # inconsistent with that. Walk/bike accessibility for the population
  # would require routing every Seattle origin × every job destination
  # through r5r WALK/BIKE — out of scope for Phase 2 (and the existing
  # Phase 1 walk/bike skims are per HTS-trip, not per OD).

  # Drive: per-OD post-equilibrium dodgr time × Phase-1 GAM calibration.
  # Same approach as extract_tt_stats_all_modes — see that function for
  # rationale. Requires bpr_vc_cap = 2.0 in the equilibrium to keep
  # per-edge BPR factors realistic.
  scale_freeflow_to_congested <-
    if (is.finite(free_flow_speed_mph) && free_flow_speed_mph > 0 &&
        is.finite(avg_speed_mph) && avg_speed_mph > 0)
      free_flow_speed_mph / avg_speed_mph else 1
  drive_base <- skim_drive_full |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_tt_raw) |>
    filter(origin_id %in% origins) |>
    mutate(drive_min_fallback = as.numeric(drive_tt_raw) *
                                scale_freeflow_to_congested)
  if (!is.null(od_skim_converged) && nrow(od_skim_converged) > 0) {
    drive_base <- drive_base |>
      left_join(od_skim_converged |>
                  select(origin_id, dest_id,
                         drive_min_eq = car_tt_min_raw),
                by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
      mutate(drive_min_uncal = if_else(is.finite(drive_min_eq),
                                       drive_min_eq, drive_min_fallback))
  } else {
    drive_base <- drive_base |> mutate(drive_min_uncal = drive_min_fallback)
  }
  drive_base <- drive_base |>
    left_join(od_cal_lookup_in |>
                select(origin_id, dest_id, cal_ratio),
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
    mutate(cal_ratio = coalesce(cal_ratio, global_cal_ratio_in),
           # Loose sanity cap. GAM predictions in [0.1, 5.0] are realistic
           # for Phase-1 calibrated distributions; outside this is likely
           # extrapolation. The previous [0.2, 2.0] cap was clamping
           # legitimate values.
           cal_ratio = pmax(0.1, pmin(5.0, cal_ratio)),
           drive_min = drive_min_uncal * cal_ratio)
  drive_acc <- drive_base |>
    filter(is.finite(drive_min), drive_min <= max_minutes) |>
    inner_join(emp, by = "dest_id") |>
    group_by(origin_id) |>
    summarise(jobs = sum(jobs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    transmute(GEOID = origin_id, mode = "drive", jobs_30min = jobs)

  # Transit (walk + transit): from transit skim at this TOD/dow.
  transit_acc <- transit_skim_long |>
    filter(dow_type == !!dow_type, tod_bin == !!tod_bin,
           is.finite(transit_total_raw),
           transit_total_raw <= max_minutes,
           origin_id %in% origins) |>
    inner_join(emp, by = "dest_id") |>
    group_by(origin_id) |>
    summarise(jobs = sum(jobs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    transmute(GEOID = origin_id, mode = "transit", jobs_30min = jobs)

  bind_rows(drive_acc, transit_acc) |>
    mutate(config_id = config_row$config_id, tod = tod_bin, .before = 1)
}

# ---- Legacy single-mode accessibility (transit only) -------------------
# Kept for back-compat with the existing extract loop and RSE correlation.
extract_employment_accessibility <- function(combo_str, config_row,
                                             max_minutes = 30L,
                                             tod_bin = "AM",
                                             dow_type = "Weekday") {
  tskim <- transit_skims[[combo_str]] |>
    filter(dow_type == !!dow_type, tod_bin == !!tod_bin)
  reachable <- tskim |>
    filter(is.finite(transit_total_raw),
           transit_total_raw <= max_minutes) |>
    inner_join(employment_by_tract, by = c("dest_id" = "GEOID")) |>
    group_by(origin_id) |>
    summarise(jobs_30min = sum(jobs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  reachable |>
    transmute(config_id = config_row$config_id,
              tod = tod_bin,
              GEOID = origin_id,
              jobs_30min)
}

extract_rse_correlation <- function(emp_acc_long, baseline_emp_acc) {
  delta <- emp_acc_long |>
    inner_join(baseline_emp_acc |>
                 transmute(GEOID, jobs_30min_base = jobs_30min),
               by = "GEOID") |>
    mutate(delta_jobs_pct = (jobs_30min - jobs_30min_base) /
                            pmax(jobs_30min_base, 1) * 100) |>
    inner_join(rse_index |> select(GEOID, rse_composite_percentile),
               by = "GEOID")
  if (nrow(delta) < 5) return(tibble(
    config_id = unique(emp_acc_long$config_id),
    n_tracts = nrow(delta),
    pearson_r = NA_real_, spearman_rho = NA_real_))
  tibble(
    config_id = unique(emp_acc_long$config_id),
    n_tracts = nrow(delta),
    pearson_r = stats::cor(delta$delta_jobs_pct,
                           delta$rse_composite_percentile,
                           use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson"),
    spearman_rho = stats::cor(delta$delta_jobs_pct,
                              delta$rse_composite_percentile,
                              use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
                              method = "spearman")
  )
}
```


# 12. Per-trip frame

```{r build-trips-in}
# Master per-trip frame for all configs.
#
# Replaces Phase 1's drive_tt_raw / drive_dist_mi (which were routed on
# Phase 1's graph) with Phase 2's values from skim_drive_full. All other
# per-trip features (parking, travelers, vehicle_count, is_work,
# transit_avail, walk_tt_raw, bike_tt_raw, estimated_transit_fare) still
# come from Phase 1's trips_calibrated.rds — they're properties of the
# trip itself, not of the routing graph.
#
# The cal_ratio (drive_tt_cal_baseline / drive_tt_raw_baseline) is
# recomputed below via the per-TOD GAM (predict_drive_cal_ratio), which
# applies Phase 1's fitted GAM to Phase 2's drive_dist_mi.
trips_in <- trips_aux |>
  filter(origin_id %in% seattle_tract_ids,
         dest_id   %in% seattle_tract_ids) |>
  # Drop Phase 1's drive_tt_raw / drive_dist_mi and replace with Phase 2's
  # values from skim_drive_full.
  select(-drive_tt_raw_baseline, -drive_dist_mi) |>
  left_join(skim_drive_full |>
              transmute(origin_id, dest_id,
                        drive_tt_raw_baseline = drive_tt_raw,
                        drive_dist_mi        = drive_dist_mi,
                        drive_source         = drive_source),
            by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
  # Drop trips whose OD didn't route in Phase 2 (snap failure across
  # all (1,n)/(n,1) tiers means we have no drive_tt for them).
  filter(is.finite(drive_tt_raw_baseline), drive_tt_raw_baseline > 0,
         is.finite(drive_dist_mi),        drive_dist_mi > 0) |>
  # drive_cal_ratio (Phase 1 value) becomes stale because the denominator
  # changed; recompute below via the AM-GAM. For now, mark NA and let the
  # GAM block in this chunk overwrite it.
  mutate(drive_cal_ratio = NA_real_)

log_msg(sprintf("trips_in: %d trips (drive_tt_raw / drive_dist_mi from Phase 2)",
                nrow(trips_in)))
log_msg(sprintf("  dodgr-routable trips: %d (%.1f%%); rest had snap failure",
                sum(trips_in$drive_source == "dodgr", na.rm = TRUE),
                100 * mean(trips_in$drive_source == "dodgr", na.rm = TRUE)))
log_msg("  drive_cal_ratio will be computed below via AM-GAM.")

# Per-OD calibration scalar (Phase-1 GAM ratio aggregated to OD level) plus
# a global trip-weighted fallback. Used by extract_tt_stats_all_modes and
# extract_employment_accessibility_by_mode to undo dodgr's motorcar-profile
# time inflation.
#

# ===== Phase-1 GAM-direct drive calibration (audit Fix #2 + #3) =========
# Replaces the prior weighted-median + cap approach with a direct
# application of Phase 1's fitted mgcv GAM at AM-peak conditions for
# EVERY Daysim OD (not just HTS-covered ones). The GAM uses DISTANCES
# not TIMES as features (s(log_obs_dist) + s(log_pred_dist) + ti(...) +
# s(peer_log_ratio) + tod_bin + dow_type), so a single per-OD AM-
# conditioned cal_ratio is the right answer — independent of congestion.
log_msg("Loading Phase 1 drive calibration GAM...")
gam_path <- latest_cache_rds("drive_gam")
if (is.na(gam_path)) stop(
  "Phase 1's drive_gam cache not found. Re-knit Phase1BuildMNL.Rmd.")
cal_drive_model <- readRDS(gam_path)
log_msg(sprintf("  Loaded GAM from %s", basename(gam_path)))

# Rebuild peer_drive tables from drive HTS trips. Phase-1-matching with
# one change: drive_tt_raw and drive_dist_mi come from Phase 2's
# skim_drive_full (Phase 1's values are inconsistent with Phase 2's
# graph). Match Phase 1's logic (Phase1BuildMNL §7 lines 1591–1671)
# of filtering to mode_norm == "drive" trips for the peer fit (not
# drive_avail across all modes, which biases the peer ratio toward
# walk/bike/transit trips that happen to have a routable drive alt).
MIN_POSITIVE_MI <- 0.0001
cal_drive_df_p2 <- trips_cal_full |>
  # Drop Phase 1 drive columns; bring in Phase 2's per-OD values
  select(-any_of(c("drive_tt_raw", "drive_dist_mi"))) |>
  left_join(skim_drive_full |>
              transmute(origin_id, dest_id,
                        drive_tt_raw = drive_tt_raw,
                        drive_dist_mi = drive_dist_mi),
            by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
  filter(mode_norm == "drive",  # Phase 1's calibration frame restriction
         is.finite(duration_minutes), duration_minutes > 0,
         is.finite(drive_tt_raw), drive_tt_raw > 0,
         is.finite(distance_miles), distance_miles > 0,
         is.finite(drive_dist_mi), drive_dist_mi > 0) |>
  left_join(trip_weights, by = "trip_id") |>
  transmute(
    origin_id, dest_id, tod_bin, dow_type,
    log_ratio    = log(duration_minutes / drive_tt_raw),
    obs_dist_mi  = pmax(distance_miles, MIN_POSITIVE_MI),
    pred_dist_mi = pmax(drive_dist_mi,  MIN_POSITIVE_MI),
    w            = pmax(coalesce(trip_weight, 1), 0.01))

peer_drive_p2 <- list(
  od = cal_drive_df_p2 |>
    group_by(origin_id, dest_id, tod_bin, dow_type) |>
    summarise(peer_log_ratio = stats::weighted.mean(log_ratio, w, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop"),
  td = cal_drive_df_p2 |>
    group_by(tod_bin, dow_type) |>
    summarise(td_peer = stats::weighted.mean(log_ratio, w, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop"),
  global = stats::weighted.mean(cal_drive_df_p2$log_ratio,
                                cal_drive_df_p2$w, na.rm = TRUE))
log_msg(sprintf("  Rebuilt peer_drive: %d per-OD entries, %d per-(tod,dow)",
                nrow(peer_drive_p2$od), nrow(peer_drive_p2$td)))

# Predict the cal_ratio per OD via the GAM at a chosen TOD/dow combination.
# This is the engine of Fix #3 (TOD alignment) from the audit: the Daysim
# demand we apply this to is per-TOD, so the calibration must be TOD-
# conditioned regardless of each HTS kernel trip's actual TOD. With no
# observed distance for Daysim-only ODs, we substitute drive_dist_mi for
# both obs and pred; the GAM's ti(...) interaction term evaluates near
# zero on the diagonal.
predict_drive_cal_ratio <- function(ods_df, tod_bin = "AM",
                                     dow_type = "Weekday") {
  # Pre-force the args to plain characters and bind to LOCAL names to
  # avoid any dplyr data-mask shadowing where `tod_bin = tod_bin` on the
  # mutate RHS might be mis-resolved against the data frame.
  .tod_bin  <- as.character(tod_bin[[1]])
  .dow_type <- as.character(dow_type[[1]])
  nd <- ods_df |>
    mutate(
      tod_bin       = .tod_bin,
      dow_type      = .dow_type,
      obs_dist_mi   = pmax(drive_dist_mi, MIN_POSITIVE_MI),
      pred_dist_mi  = pmax(drive_dist_mi, MIN_POSITIVE_MI),
      log_obs_dist  = log(obs_dist_mi),
      log_pred_dist = log(pred_dist_mi)) |>
    left_join(peer_drive_p2$od,
              by = c("origin_id", "dest_id", "tod_bin", "dow_type")) |>
    left_join(peer_drive_p2$td, by = c("tod_bin", "dow_type")) |>
    mutate(peer_log_ratio = coalesce(peer_log_ratio, td_peer,
                                     peer_drive_p2$global))
  ok <- is.finite(nd$log_obs_dist) & is.finite(nd$log_pred_dist) &
        is.finite(nd$peer_log_ratio)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(nd))
  if (any(ok)) {
    # GAM prediction. If the saved model lost its QR component (some
    # mgcv versions strip it under certain save options), fall back to
    # the empirical peer log-ratio — that's the dominant signal the GAM
    # itself fits, and it produces a numerically reasonable cal_ratio.
    out[ok] <- tryCatch(
      exp(predict(cal_drive_model,
                  newdata = nd[ok, ],
                  type = "response")),
      error = function(e) {
        log_sub(sprintf(
          "    GAM predict() failed (%s); falling back to peer_log_ratio",
          conditionMessage(e)))
        exp(nd$peer_log_ratio[ok])
      })
  }
  out
}

# Build a per-TOD lookup list. Each entry is an OD-level cal_ratio tibble
# conditioned on that TOD (and Weekday dow). Downstream code that does
# `od_drive_cal_lookup[[tod]] |> select(...)` plugs in the right ratio
# regardless of which TOD's equilibrium is being run.
od_drive_cal_lookup_per_tod <- lapply(params$tods_to_run, function(tn) {
  skim_drive_full |>
    filter(is.finite(drive_dist_mi), drive_dist_mi > 0) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, drive_dist_mi) |>
    mutate(cal_ratio = predict_drive_cal_ratio(
                         tibble(origin_id     = origin_id,
                                dest_id       = dest_id,
                                drive_dist_mi = drive_dist_mi),
                         tod_bin  = tn,
                         dow_type = "Weekday")) |>
    filter(is.finite(cal_ratio), cal_ratio > 0) |>
    select(origin_id, dest_id, cal_ratio)
})
names(od_drive_cal_lookup_per_tod) <- params$tods_to_run

global_drive_cal_ratio_per_tod <- vapply(od_drive_cal_lookup_per_tod,
  function(tbl) {
    v <- median(tbl$cal_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (!is.finite(v) || v <= 0) 1.0 else v
  }, numeric(1))

for (tn in params$tods_to_run) {
  tbl <- od_drive_cal_lookup_per_tod[[tn]]
  log_msg(sprintf("[%s] GAM cal_ratios: %d ODs predicted (median = %.3f, IQR = [%.3f, %.3f], n_above_2 = %d)",
                  tn, nrow(tbl),
                  global_drive_cal_ratio_per_tod[[tn]],
                  quantile(tbl$cal_ratio, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
                  quantile(tbl$cal_ratio, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
                  sum(tbl$cal_ratio > 2.0)))
}

# Back-compat scalars / tibble. Defaults to the FIRST TOD in tods_to_run
# (AM if available). Used by:
#   - run_equilibrium_v2 default code path (overridden via `tod` arg)
#   - extract_tt_stats_all_modes (per-TOD-aware via `tod` arg)
#   - cache-signature digesters in §13b / §14
.default_tod <- params$tods_to_run[[1]]
od_drive_cal_lookup    <- od_drive_cal_lookup_per_tod[[.default_tod]]
global_drive_cal_ratio <- global_drive_cal_ratio_per_tod[[.default_tod]]

# Replace per-trip drive_cal_ratio in trips_in with the OD-level GAM
# prediction at the default TOD. This is preserved for back-compat with
# §13b/§14 cache signatures; the actual interior-MNL uses the per-OD
# `drive_tt_lookup_interior` initialized per-TOD inside run_equilibrium_v2.
trips_in <- trips_in |>
  rename(drive_cal_ratio_orig_tod = drive_cal_ratio) |>
  left_join(od_drive_cal_lookup, by = c("origin_id", "dest_id")) |>
  mutate(drive_cal_ratio = coalesce(cal_ratio, global_drive_cal_ratio)) |>
  select(-cal_ratio)
log_msg(sprintf("  trips_in: replaced drive_cal_ratio with %s-GAM for %d/%d trips",
                .default_tod,
                sum(!is.na(trips_in$drive_cal_ratio)), nrow(trips_in)))
```

# 13. Build observed-flow seed

The PSRC trip table only covers Seattle-internal demand. Real Seattle
streets carry significant background traffic (out-of-region commuters,
freight, taxis, deliveries) that the model doesn't see. Without seeding
these the modeled volumes underload the network and bus-lane / AV effects
hit at unrealistically low V/C.

The seed pipeline:

1. **Seasonal calibration** via control-point segments studied ~monthly.
   A handful of SDOT segments are deliberately re-counted across many
   years; we extract a (year, month) seasonality index from them and
   normalize every other study's AMPK to a comparable reference month.
2. **Directional preservation**: studies have STUDY_DIRFLOW (N/S/E/W);
   we keep direction through the count cleaning. Spread to dodgr edges
   uses 50/50 split for two-way streets, 100% for one-way (per SND data).
3. **Attribute (way_id) matching**, NOT spatial buffer. Each SDOT COMPKEY
   has a known OSM way_id via `snd_compkey_csv`; we attach counts by
   attribute join. No tertiary_link / service road false matches.
4. **SDOT corridor layer** as the unit of analysis: each corridor has a
   list of constituent COMPKEYs and curated AWDT/AMPK/PMPK. We use the
   corridor's value where available, fall back to recent-studies-mean
   for COMPKEYs in that corridor, and finally an AMPK/AWDT ratio for
   corridors with only AWDT.
5. **WSDOT counts** for state highways (I-5/SR-99/SR-520/I-90) — SDOT
   data doesn't cover those. Matched to dodgr edges by route name → SND
   ord_stname → way_id, then nearest count point along the route.
6. **Unseeded baseline run** to get model_flow_vph; final
   `flow_seed = max(0, observed - model)`.

```{r build-counts-clean}
log_stage("Stage 13a.2: SDOT counts — seasonal calibration & directional cleaning")

counts_clean <- with_cache("counts_clean_seasonal",
  list(counts_sig = file_signature(params$seattle_counts_csv),
       version = "v1"),
  function() {
    # Read raw counts. The CSV occasionally has rows where the embedded
    # location text has unquoted commas → use fill=TRUE to parse safely.
    raw_csv <- fread(params$seattle_counts_csv, fill = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
    log_msg(sprintf("Read %d raw count rows", nrow(raw_csv)))

    # Need an sf with point geometry. The CSV has X/Y in a non-canonical
    # CRS sometimes; we look for lon/lat-like columns first.
    nm <- toupper(stringr::str_replace_all(names(raw_csv),
                                           "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_"))
    names(raw_csv) <- nm

    # Required columns
    needed <- c("START_DATE", "ACTUAL_DAYS", "STUDY_DIRFLOW",
                "STUDY_AMPK", "STUDY_AWDT", "STUDY_PMPK", "SEG_COMPKEY")
    missing <- setdiff(needed, names(raw_csv))
    if (length(missing) > 0)
      stop("seattle_flow_counts.csv missing columns: ",
           paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

    # 1) Project + filter
    raw <- raw_csv |>
      mutate(
        start_date    = lubridate::mdy_hms(START_DATE, tz = "UTC", quiet = TRUE),
        year          = lubridate::year(start_date),
        month         = lubridate::month(start_date),
        ACTUAL_DAYS   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(ACTUAL_DAYS)),
        STUDY_DIRFLOW = trimws(as.character(STUDY_DIRFLOW)),
        STUDY_AWDT    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(STUDY_AWDT)),
        STUDY_AMPK    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(STUDY_AMPK)),
        STUDY_PMPK    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(STUDY_PMPK)),
        SEG_COMPKEY   = as.character(SEG_COMPKEY))

    cardinal_dirs <- c("N", "S", "E", "W", "NE", "NW", "SE", "SW")
    filtered <- raw |>
      filter(!is.na(start_date),
             start_date >= as.POSIXct("2021-05-01", tz = "UTC"),
             ACTUAL_DAYS == 7,
             STUDY_DIRFLOW %in% cardinal_dirs,
             is.finite(STUDY_AMPK), STUDY_AMPK > 0)
    log_msg(sprintf("After date/days/dir filter: %d studies kept (of %d)",
                    nrow(filtered), nrow(raw)))

    # 2) Identify calibration (SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW) pairs:
    #    studies in EVERY year of the window with >= 10 per year
    window_start <- as.Date("2021-05-01")
    window_end   <- as.Date(max(filtered$start_date))
    candidate_years <- seq(lubridate::year(window_start),
                           lubridate::year(window_end))
    months_in_year <- sapply(candidate_years, function(y) {
      yr_lo <- max(window_start, as.Date(sprintf("%d-01-01", y)))
      yr_hi <- min(window_end,   as.Date(sprintf("%d-12-31", y)))
      if (yr_hi < yr_lo) return(0L)
      length(seq(yr_lo, yr_hi, by = "month"))
    })
    target_years <- candidate_years[months_in_year >= 10]
    log_msg(sprintf("Calibration target years: %s",
                    paste(target_years, collapse = ", ")))

    yearly_counts <- filtered |>
      filter(year %in% target_years) |>
      group_by(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW, year) |>
      summarise(n_studies = n(), .groups = "drop")
    cal_pairs <- yearly_counts |>
      group_by(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW) |>
      summarise(
        ok = length(target_years) > 0 &&
             all(target_years %in% year) &&
             all(n_studies[match(target_years, year)] >= 10),
        .groups = "drop") |>
      filter(ok) |>
      select(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW)
    log_msg(sprintf("Calibration (segment, direction) pairs: %d",
                    nrow(cal_pairs)))
    if (nrow(cal_pairs) == 0) {
      log_msg("WARNING: no calibration pairs found — applying NO seasonal adjustment")
    }

    # 3) Build cal grid + backfill 1-2 missing months
    cal_studies <- filtered |>
      semi_join(cal_pairs, by = c("SEG_COMPKEY", "STUDY_DIRFLOW")) |>
      group_by(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW, year, month) |>
      summarise(AMPK = mean(STUDY_AMPK, na.rm = TRUE),
                AWDT = mean(STUDY_AWDT, na.rm = TRUE),
                PMPK = mean(STUDY_PMPK, na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop")
    ym_grid <- expand.grid(year = target_years, month = 1:12) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(ym_date = as.Date(sprintf("%04d-%02d-01", year, month))) |>
      filter(ym_date >= window_start - lubridate::days(1),
             ym_date <= window_end) |>
      select(year, month)
    cal_grid <- cal_pairs |>
      tidyr::crossing(ym_grid) |>
      left_join(cal_studies,
                by = c("SEG_COMPKEY", "STUDY_DIRFLOW", "year", "month")) |>
      group_by(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW) |>
      arrange(year, month, .by_group = TRUE) |>
      mutate(
        AMPK_filled = if_else(is.na(AMPK),
                              (lag(AMPK)  + lead(AMPK))  / 2, AMPK)) |>
      ungroup()

    # 4) Monthly index from sum of calibration AMPK; mean=1
    cal_index <- cal_grid |>
      group_by(year, month) |>
      summarise(total_AMPK = sum(AMPK_filled, na.rm = TRUE),
                n_segs_present = sum(!is.na(AMPK_filled)),
                .groups = "drop") |>
      filter(n_segs_present >= 0.5 * nrow(cal_pairs)) |>
      mutate(cal_factor = total_AMPK / mean(total_AMPK, na.rm = TRUE))
    log_msg(sprintf("Monthly cal_factor range: [%.2f, %.2f]",
                    min(cal_index$cal_factor, na.rm = TRUE),
                    max(cal_index$cal_factor, na.rm = TRUE)))

    # 5) Normalize every study by its cal_factor; mean across re-studies
    normalized <- filtered |>
      left_join(cal_index |> select(year, month, cal_factor),
                by = c("year", "month")) |>
      mutate(cal_factor = coalesce(cal_factor, 1),
             AMPK_norm  = STUDY_AMPK / cal_factor,
             PMPK_norm  = STUDY_PMPK / cal_factor,
             AWDT_norm  = STUDY_AWDT / cal_factor)

    counts_clean <- normalized |>
      group_by(SEG_COMPKEY, STUDY_DIRFLOW) |>
      summarise(n_studies = n(),
                AMPK_norm = mean(AMPK_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                PMPK_norm = mean(PMPK_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                AWDT_norm = mean(AWDT_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop") |>
      transmute(
        seg_compkey         = as.character(SEG_COMPKEY),
        direction           = STUDY_DIRFLOW,
        n_studies,
        AMPK_norm, PMPK_norm, AWDT_norm,
        observed_peakhr_vph = AMPK_norm)

    log_msg(sprintf("counts_clean: %d (compkey, dir) rows; AMPK_norm range [%.0f, %.0f] (median %.0f)",
                    nrow(counts_clean),
                    min(counts_clean$AMPK_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                    max(counts_clean$AMPK_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                    median(counts_clean$AMPK_norm, na.rm = TRUE)))
    counts_clean
  })
```

```{r build-wsdot-counts}
log_stage("Stage 13a.3: WSDOT state-highway counts")

wsdot_counts <- with_cache("wsdot_counts",
  list(csv_sig = file_signature(params$wsdot_counts_csv),
       k = params$default_k_factor, version = "v1"),
  function() {
    if (!file.exists(params$wsdot_counts_csv)) {
      log_msg("WSDOT CSV not found; skipping (state highways won't be seeded)")
      return(tibble(state_route = character(0), wsdot_lon = double(0),
                    wsdot_lat = double(0), wsdot_direction = character(0),
                    observed_peakhr_vph = double(0), aadt_one_direction = double(0)))
    }
    raw <- readr::read_csv(params$wsdot_counts_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      mutate(RelatedRouteType = trimws(as.character(RelatedRouteType))) |>
      filter(is.finite(X), is.finite(Y),
             is.finite(AADT), AADT > 0,
             is.na(ReportingYear) | ReportingYear >= 2021,
             is.na(RelatedRouteType) | RelatedRouteType == "")  # mainline only
    log_msg(sprintf("WSDOT after filter (mainline + 2021+): %d rows", nrow(raw)))

    # CRS detection: lon/lat range vs WA SP North vs Web Mercator
    max_abs_x <- max(abs(raw$X), na.rm = TRUE)
    detected_crs <- if (max_abs_x <= 180) 4326 else
                    if (max_abs_x > 1e7)  3857 else 2926
    wsdot_sf <- raw |>
      sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = detected_crs) |>
      sf::st_transform(4326)
    coords <- sf::st_coordinates(wsdot_sf)
    k <- as.numeric(params$default_k_factor)

    # Bothways AADT is bidirectional → halve before applying K-factor.
    is_bothways <- toupper(trimws(as.character(wsdot_sf$DirectionOfTravel))) ==
                     "BOTHWAYS"
    one_dir_aadt <- ifelse(is_bothways, as.numeric(wsdot_sf$AADT) / 2,
                           as.numeric(wsdot_sf$AADT))

    out <- tibble(
      wsdot_lon            = coords[, 1],
      wsdot_lat            = coords[, 2],
      wsdot_direction      = as.character(wsdot_sf$DirectionOfTravel),
      state_route          = as.character(wsdot_sf$StateRouteNumber),
      aadt_one_direction   = one_dir_aadt,
      observed_peakhr_vph  = one_dir_aadt * k)

    in_box <- out$wsdot_lon >= params$count_bbox_lon[1] &
              out$wsdot_lon <= params$count_bbox_lon[2] &
              out$wsdot_lat >= params$count_bbox_lat[1] &
              out$wsdot_lat <= params$count_bbox_lat[2]
    out <- out[in_box, ]
    log_msg(sprintf("WSDOT count points kept (Seattle bbox): %d", nrow(out)))
    out
  })
```

```{r load-sdot-corridors}
log_stage("Stage 13a.4: SDOT 2022 corridor flow layer")

corridors <- with_cache("sdot_corridors",
  list(cache_sig = file_signature(params$sdot_corridor_cache_rds),
       version = "v1"),
  function() {
    corr_cache <- params$sdot_corridor_cache_rds
    if (!is.null(corr_cache) && file.exists(corr_cache)) {
      corridors_sf <- readRDS(corr_cache)
      log_msg(sprintf("Loaded cached SDOT corridor layer: %d features",
                      nrow(corridors_sf)))
    } else {
      if (!requireNamespace("httr", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("httr")
      log_msg("Fetching SDOT 2022 Flow Counts corridor layer from ArcGIS...")
      fetch_arcgis_corridors <- function(url) {
        base <- httr::parse_url(url)
        base$query$resultRecordCount <- 2000
        base$query$f <- "geojson"
        all_chunks <- list(); offset <- 0
        repeat {
          base$query$resultOffset <- offset
          u <- httr::build_url(base)
          resp <- httr::GET(u); httr::stop_for_status(resp)
          chunk <- sf::st_read(httr::content(resp, as = "text"), quiet = TRUE)
          if (nrow(chunk) == 0) break
          all_chunks[[length(all_chunks) + 1]] <- chunk
          if (nrow(chunk) < 2000) break
          offset <- offset + nrow(chunk)
        }
        do.call(rbind, all_chunks)
      }
      corridors_sf <- fetch_arcgis_corridors(params$sdot_corridor_url) |>
        sf::st_transform(4326)
      if (!is.null(corr_cache)) {
        dir.create(dirname(corr_cache), recursive = TRUE,
                   showWarnings = FALSE)
        saveRDS(corridors_sf, corr_cache)
      }
    }
    corridors_sf |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
      transmute(
        flowsegid    = suppressWarnings(as.integer(FLOWSEGID)),
        stname_ord   = as.character(STNAME_ORD),
        compkey_str  = as.character(COMPKEY),
        awdt         = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(AWDT)),
        adt          = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ADT)),
        ampk         = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(AMPK)),
        pmpk         = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(PMPK)),
        dir_flow     = trimws(as.character(DIR_FLOW)),
        downtown     = as.character(DOWNTOWN),
        days         = suppressWarnings(as.integer(DAYS))) |>
      mutate(compkey_list = stringr::str_split(compkey_str, ",\\s*"))
  })

# Raw corridor-layer availability (pre-cascade). The cascade in §13a.5
# fills in corridors that lack AMPK directly, by either (a) recent-studies
# AMPK from counts_clean for any constituent COMPKEY, or (b) AWDT × the
# network-mean AMPK/AWDT ratio. Final corridor coverage is reported there.
log_msg(sprintf("Raw corridor layer:"))
log_msg(sprintf("  with non-zero AMPK directly: %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                sum(corridors$ampk > 0, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(corridors),
                100 * mean(corridors$ampk > 0, na.rm = TRUE)))
log_msg(sprintf("  with non-zero AWDT (fallback eligible): %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                sum(corridors$awdt > 0, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(corridors),
                100 * mean(corridors$awdt > 0, na.rm = TRUE)))
log_msg(sprintf("  with EITHER AMPK or AWDT: %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                sum(corridors$ampk > 0 | corridors$awdt > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
                nrow(corridors),
                100 * mean(corridors$ampk > 0 | corridors$awdt > 0,
                           na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r build-observed-per-edge}
log_stage("Stage 13a.5: Corridor → way_id → dodgr edge with directional split")

# ---- Bearing helpers (used by §13a.5 directional seed) ----------------
# Initial bearing from (lon1, lat1) to (lon2, lat2), in degrees [0, 360).
# 0 = N, 90 = E, 180 = S, 270 = W.
.edge_bearing <- function(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) {
  lat1r <- lat1 * pi / 180; lat2r <- lat2 * pi / 180
  dlon  <- (lon2 - lon1) * pi / 180
  y <- sin(dlon) * cos(lat2r)
  x <- cos(lat1r) * sin(lat2r) - sin(lat1r) * cos(lat2r) * cos(dlon)
  (atan2(y, x) * 180 / pi + 360) %% 360
}

# Map SDOT DIR_FLOW text to a target bearing in degrees, or NA for
# undirected/unrecognized values (e.g. "BOTH").
.dirflow_to_bearing <- function(dir_flow) {
  d <- toupper(trimws(as.character(dir_flow)))
  dplyr::case_when(
    d %in% c("N",  "NB",  "NORTH",     "NORTHBOUND")    ~ 0,
    d %in% c("NE", "NEB", "NORTHEAST", "NORTHEASTBOUND") ~ 45,
    d %in% c("E",  "EB",  "EAST",      "EASTBOUND")     ~ 90,
    d %in% c("SE", "SEB", "SOUTHEAST", "SOUTHEASTBOUND") ~ 135,
    d %in% c("S",  "SB",  "SOUTH",     "SOUTHBOUND")    ~ 180,
    d %in% c("SW", "SWB", "SOUTHWEST", "SOUTHWESTBOUND") ~ 225,
    d %in% c("W",  "WB",  "WEST",      "WESTBOUND")     ~ 270,
    d %in% c("NW", "NWB", "NORTHWEST", "NORTHWESTBOUND") ~ 315,
    TRUE                                                 ~ NA_real_)
}

# Normalize DIR_FLOW for grouping. Returns one of NB/NE/EB/SE/SB/SW/WB/NW
# for recognized directional values; NA for empty / "BOTH" / "TWO-WAY" /
# unrecognized (those are treated as undirected, hence 50/50 split).
.normalize_dir_flow <- function(dir_flow) {
  d <- toupper(trimws(as.character(dir_flow)))
  dplyr::case_when(
    d %in% c("N",  "NB",  "NORTH",     "NORTHBOUND")    ~ "NB",
    d %in% c("NE", "NEB", "NORTHEAST", "NORTHEASTBOUND") ~ "NE",
    d %in% c("E",  "EB",  "EAST",      "EASTBOUND")     ~ "EB",
    d %in% c("SE", "SEB", "SOUTHEAST", "SOUTHEASTBOUND") ~ "SE",
    d %in% c("S",  "SB",  "SOUTH",     "SOUTHBOUND")    ~ "SB",
    d %in% c("SW", "SWB", "SOUTHWEST", "SOUTHWESTBOUND") ~ "SW",
    d %in% c("W",  "WB",  "WEST",      "WESTBOUND")     ~ "WB",
    d %in% c("NW", "NWB", "NORTHWEST", "NORTHWESTBOUND") ~ "NW",
    TRUE                                                 ~ NA_character_)
}

# This is the heart of the corridor-based seed pipeline. We:
# 1. For each corridor pick the best AMPK source: recent normalized
#    studies > corridor layer's own AMPK > AWDT × network AMPK/AWDT ratio.
# 2. Expand corridor → compkey list → way_id list (via compkey_to_way).
# 3. Inner-join match-class dodgr edges with way_id list, applying
#    50/50 directional split for two-way streets, 100% for one-way.
# 4. WSDOT route-name fill for un-seeded mainline ways.
# 5. Final per-edge `observed_peakhr_vph` vector.

build_observed_per_edge_corridor <- function(graph_in,
                                             counts_clean, wsdot_counts,
                                             corridors,
                                             compkey_to_way, snd_to_way,
                                             way_snd_attrs,
                                             route_pairs,
                                             match_classes) {
  # ---- (a) Per-COMPKEY recent-studies AMPK from counts_clean ----
  recent_per_compkey <- counts_clean |>
    filter(!is.na(seg_compkey)) |>
    group_by(seg_compkey) |>
    summarise(
      ampk_recent_compkey = mean(observed_peakhr_vph, na.rm = TRUE),
      awdt_recent_compkey = mean(AWDT_norm,           na.rm = TRUE),
      n_studies_compkey   = sum(n_studies, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop")

  # ---- (b) Per-corridor: best AMPK source ----
  corr_long <- corridors |>
    select(flowsegid, stname_ord, ampk_corr = ampk,
           awdt_corr = awdt, dir_flow, compkey_list) |>
    tidyr::unnest_longer(compkey_list, values_to = "compkey") |>
    mutate(compkey = stringr::str_trim(compkey)) |>
    filter(nzchar(compkey)) |>
    left_join(recent_per_compkey, by = c("compkey" = "seg_compkey"))

  corridor_recent <- corr_long |>
    group_by(flowsegid) |>
    summarise(
      n_compkeys_with_recent = sum(!is.na(ampk_recent_compkey)),
      ampk_recent = mean(ampk_recent_compkey, na.rm = TRUE),
      awdt_recent = mean(awdt_recent_compkey, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop")

  # Network mean ratio for fallback
  ratio_pool <- corridors |>
    filter(is.finite(ampk), is.finite(awdt), ampk > 0, awdt > 0)
  ampk_awdt_ratio <- if (nrow(ratio_pool) > 0)
    median(ratio_pool$ampk / ratio_pool$awdt, na.rm = TRUE) else 0.07
  log_msg(sprintf("Network AMPK/AWDT ratio (fallback): %.4f", ampk_awdt_ratio))

  corridor_seed <- corridors |>
    left_join(corridor_recent, by = "flowsegid") |>
    mutate(
      ampk_source = case_when(
        n_compkeys_with_recent > 0 & is.finite(ampk_recent) & ampk_recent > 0
          ~ "recent_studies",
        is.finite(ampk) & ampk > 0  ~ "corridor_layer",
        is.finite(awdt) & awdt > 0  ~ "fallback_awdt_ratio",
        TRUE                        ~ "no_data"),
      ampk_used = case_when(
        ampk_source == "recent_studies"      ~ ampk_recent,
        ampk_source == "corridor_layer"      ~ ampk,
        ampk_source == "fallback_awdt_ratio" ~ awdt * ampk_awdt_ratio,
        TRUE                                  ~ NA_real_),
      awdt_used = if_else(is.finite(awdt_recent) & awdt_recent > 0,
                          awdt_recent, awdt))
  log_msg("Corridor seed sources:")
  print(dplyr::count(corridor_seed, ampk_source))

  # ---- (c) Corridor → COMPKEY → way_id (per direction) ----
  ck_to_way <- compkey_to_way |>
    select(COMPKEY, way_id) |>
    mutate(COMPKEY = as.character(COMPKEY))

  ck_long <- corridor_seed |>
    transmute(flowsegid, stname_ord, ampk_used, awdt_used, dir_flow,
              ampk_source, compkey_list) |>
    tidyr::unnest_longer(compkey_list, values_to = "compkey") |>
    mutate(compkey = stringr::str_trim(compkey),
           dir_flow_norm = .normalize_dir_flow(dir_flow)) |>
    filter(nzchar(compkey)) |>
    left_join(ck_to_way, by = c("compkey" = "COMPKEY"))

  # Group by (way_id, dir_flow_norm) so per-direction counts are kept as
  # separate rows. A way that has both NB and SB counts now produces two
  # rows (one per direction); the old version collapsed both into the
  # single highest-AMPK row, which then got 50/50-split with the other
  # direction getting nothing.
  corridor_way_seed <- ck_long |>
    filter(!is.na(way_id), !is.na(ampk_used), ampk_used > 0) |>
    group_by(way_id, dir_flow_norm) |>
    arrange(desc(ampk_source == "recent_studies"),
            desc(ampk_used), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    slice(1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    transmute(way_id_c = way_id,
              ampk_corridor = ampk_used,
              awdt_corridor = awdt_used,
              dir_flow_corr = dir_flow_norm,
              ampk_source)
  log_msg(sprintf("Way × direction rows: %d (across %d distinct ways)",
                  nrow(corridor_way_seed),
                  length(unique(corridor_way_seed$way_id_c))))
  log_msg(sprintf("  with directional info (NB/SB/EB/WB/...): %d",
                  sum(!is.na(corridor_way_seed$dir_flow_corr))))
  log_msg(sprintf("  undirected (BOTH / unrecognized DIR_FLOW): %d",
                  sum(is.na(corridor_way_seed$dir_flow_corr))))

  # ---- (d) Match to dodgr edges, bearing-aware directional split ----
  way_id_g <- dgr_way_id(graph_in)
  if (is.null(way_id_g))
    stop("Graph has no way_id (object_); can't run attribute-join seed.")

  in_class <- as.character(graph_in$highway) %in% match_classes
  log_msg(sprintf("Match-class edges: %d", sum(in_class)))

  # Per-edge bearing (degrees from N, 0-360). Each dodgr edge is directional
  # (.vx0 → .vx1), so its bearing tells us which way traffic flows.
  edge_bear_all <- .edge_bearing(
    dgr_from_x(graph_in), dgr_from_y(graph_in),
    dgr_to_x(graph_in),   dgr_to_y(graph_in))

  # Per-edge oneway is read directly from the graph's `effective_oneway`
  # column (set by `annotate_caps`: SND first, OSM fallback). No need to
  # re-join from way_snd_attrs.
  if (!"effective_oneway" %in% names(graph_in))
    stop("Graph missing `effective_oneway`; re-run annotate_caps. ",
         "(Rebuild via StreetSetup.Rmd to ensure OSM `oneway` is in keep_cols.)")

  match_links <- tibble(
    edge_idx         = seq_len(nrow(graph_in)),
    way_id_c         = way_id_g,
    highway          = as.character(graph_in$highway),
    cap_baseline     = graph_in$cap_vph_baseline,
    edge_bear        = edge_bear_all,
    effective_oneway = as.logical(graph_in$effective_oneway)) |>
    filter(in_class)

  # Cross-join (each edge with each per-direction corridor row on its way),
  # then per edge keep the candidate with best bearing alignment.
  sdot_candidates <- match_links |>
    inner_join(corridor_way_seed, by = "way_id_c",
               relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(
      effective_oneway = coalesce(effective_oneway, FALSE),
      target_bear  = .dirflow_to_bearing(dir_flow_corr),
      bearing_diff = if_else(is.na(target_bear), NA_real_,
                             abs((edge_bear - target_bear + 180) %% 360 - 180)),
      dir_factor = case_when(
        effective_oneway        ~ 1.0,    # one-way: 100% (only one directional
                                          # edge per node-pair → no split)
        is.na(target_bear)      ~ 0.5,    # corridor undirected → 50/50
        bearing_diff <= 45      ~ 1.0,    # edge aligned with count direction
        bearing_diff >= 135     ~ 0.0,    # edge opposite to count direction → drop
        TRUE                    ~ 0.5),   # cross direction (rare): hedge 50/50
      assignment_kind = case_when(
        effective_oneway        ~ "one-way (full)",
        is.na(target_bear)      ~ "undirected (50/50)",
        bearing_diff <= 45      ~ "aligned (full)",
        bearing_diff >= 135     ~ "opposite (drop)",
        TRUE                    ~ "cross (50/50)"))

  # Per edge: keep the candidate with the highest dir_factor (tiebreak
  # AMPK). This means an edge that matches both an NB and SB corridor row
  # picks the one whose direction matches its bearing.
  sdot_per_edge <- sdot_candidates |>
    filter(dir_factor > 0) |>
    group_by(edge_idx) |>
    arrange(desc(dir_factor), desc(ampk_corridor), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    slice(1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(observed_peakhr_vph = ampk_corridor * dir_factor)

  log_msg("Bearing-aware seed assignment (post-edge dedup):")
  print(sdot_per_edge |>
          dplyr::count(assignment_kind, name = "n_edges") |>
          arrange(desc(n_edges)))
  log_msg(sprintf("Edges seeded from SDOT corridors: %d (one-way: %d)",
                  nrow(sdot_per_edge), sum(sdot_per_edge$effective_oneway)))

  # ---- (e) WSDOT route-name fill for state highways ----
  wsdot_per_edge <- tibble(edge_idx = integer(0),
                           observed_peakhr_vph = double(0))
  if (!is.null(wsdot_counts) && nrow(wsdot_counts) > 0 && nrow(snd_to_way) > 0) {
    pairs <- route_pairs
    route_to_snd <- snd_to_way |>
      mutate(ord_norm = toupper(trimws(as.character(ord_stname_concat)))) |>
      inner_join(
        pairs |> transmute(state_route, snd_name = toupper(trimws(snd_name))),
        by = c("ord_norm" = "snd_name")) |>
      transmute(state_route, way_id_c = way_id) |>
      distinct()
    log_msg(sprintf("WSDOT route → way_id pairs: %d", nrow(route_to_snd)))

    already_seeded <- unique(sdot_per_edge$edge_idx)
    route_edges <- match_links |>
      inner_join(route_to_snd, by = "way_id_c",
                 relationship = "many-to-many") |>
      filter(!(edge_idx %in% already_seeded))
```
